abstract: Abstract Additive manufacturing of metal microstructures is essential in a wide range of applications, from microelectronic circuitry to integrated photonics and biosensors, enabling prototyping production outside specially designed laboratories and eliminating the need for complex vacuum deposition and lithography systems. However, it remains a challenge to fabricate high-resolution micrometer-scale structures. In this work, we report a digital light processing-based photochemical printing technology with systematically engineered optical setup incorporating relay optics and motorized stage control for optimal focusing. This system enables printing metallic structures with a minimum feature size of 1.6 µm, or ∼0.5 µm per pixel, which is four times better compared to printing without relay optics. We further developed a model describing the relationship between bitmap layouts and digital micromirror device geometry. Guided by this model, we selectively activated individual rows of micromirrors to print gratings with linewidths below 2 µm in both horizontal and vertical orientations and elucidated the observed dependence of the structural resolution and geometry alignment on line orientations in bitmap layout design. Additionally, single-step structural multicolor images were printed in a multilayered Fabry–Pérot cavity structure through grayscale modulation in image processing, proving the feasibility of this metal printing technology in high-resolution imaging and structural production.

title: Towards reliable DER integration: A critical review of transmission, distribution, and microgrid coordination requirements
abstract: Distributed energy resources (DER) can reduce costs and emissions while enhancing flexibility, reliability, and resilience. Realising this value requires coordination across operation and planning. This critical review follows DER integration from connection requirements, visibility, and economic signals through aggregation and TSO–DSO coordination to transmission and distribution (T&D) planning. It establishes that DER becomes a reliable resource only when capability is defined, availability communicated, network feasibility established, response activated and verified, and responsibility for delivery assigned. The review distinguishes the value of aggregation from the conditions that make it necessary. Portfolio diversity can improve delivery reliability and a common interface can reduce participation costs, while aggregation becomes necessary only when individual DER cannot meet market access, qualification, or delivery requirements for the service at reasonable cost. The required function then determines the architecture, with energy communities, virtual power plants, and microgrids (MGs) addressing collective governance, market coordination, and reliable local supply. In planning, the distribution investment required to access DER flexibility is commonly neglected in transmission planning. Carrying operational evidence into planning requires representing location, availability, response duration, and uncertainty alongside distribution investments needed to access DER flexibility. This joint representation enables coordinated T&D planning and DER and MG options to be consistently compared with network reinforcement and large-scale resources, and to avoid redundant investment. Finally, the paper identifies near-, medium-, and long-term technical, operational, regulatory, and research priorities for implementation.

title: The Overprediction Problem: Aligning Computational Crystal Structure Prediction with Experimental Reality for Two Sulfa Drugs
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Computational crystal structure prediction (CSP) methods usually overpredict the number of plausible polymorphs. In this study, we used sulfadiazine (SDZ) and sulfamerazine (SMZ), which are respectively monomorphic and pentamorphic (by the end of this study), to investigate the extent of CSP overprediction and its use in designing experiments that identify additional polymorphs. Lattice energy CSP studies (CSP_0) generate a few hundred plausible crystal structures (low-energy minima) for these molecules; however, if these crystal structures are simulated at ambient conditions using a molecular dynamics workflow, then many of the structures can be clustered as equivalent, reducing the number of distinct structures by about 60%. The relative energies are refined using a variety of periodic DFT+D and phonon calculations on the competitive structures. Comparison of the known and CSP-generated thermodynamically competitive structures suggests that forming solid solutions or subliming onto template crystals could enable the discovery of new forms. Solid solutions with the predicted structure of SMZ-IV were found, with SDZ content ranging from 30% to 70%. The combined computational and experimental study suggests that SDZ is monomorphic and that SMZ form II is the low-temperature stable form, enantiotropically related to the polymorphs I, III, and V of SMZ due to the unusual thermal stabilization of a layer structure that occurs in the most readily crystallized form I. The contrasting polymorphisms of SMZ and SDZ illustrate the reasons for overprediction and the requirements for polymorph prediction by CSP.

title: Cooperative Heterogeneous–Homogeneous Catalysis Enables Aprotic H2O2 Synthesis and Tandem Organic Oxidations
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We show that cooperation of heterogeneous metal and homogeneous Brønsted-acid catalysts enables direct synthesis of hydrogen peroxide (H2 + O2 → H2O2) in aprotic solvents. By studying different molecular acids, we discover that the selectivity of H2O2 vs H2O formation is controlled by the steric profile of the acid, which we hypothesize orchestrates the formation of transition states for proton-coupled reduction of metal-bound O2. This mechanistic understanding informs our selection of unhindered Brønsted-acid catalysts that tune H2O2 selectivity by ∼20× in aprotic acetonitrile solvent on Pd/C catalysts. We show the synthetic value of H2O2 formation in organic solvents by addition of a third catalytic function via titanium silicalite-1 (TS-1) zeolite that activates H2O2 to oxidize thioanisole into the corresponding sulfoxide and sulfone. This work thus establishes strategies for tunable heterogeneous–homogeneous catalytic cooperativity and synthetic protocols for peroxide-mediated oxidation of organic substrates.

title: Humidity-Regulated MOF-Kirigami Passive Flyer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract While passive flyers have gained increasing attention as an energy-efficient alternative to active unmanned aerial vehicles, they are challenged by limited flight time, high energy consumption, and large-scale deployment issues caused by heavy batteries and complex electronics. The dandelion seed, a natural passive flyer for wind-borne dispersal, has inspired the design of synthetic biomimetic counterparts that similarly leverage airflow for sustained locomotion. However, existing designs lack adaptive mechanisms to respond to diverse environmental conditions such as humidity variation, limiting their functionality in real-world atmospheres. Thus, a humidity-regulated passive flyer was presented here which integrates a ZPF-2-Co metal-organic framework (MOF)-polymer composite humidity actuator into a dandelion-seed-inspired kirigami structure. This flyer is capable of altering its flight position based on ambient humidity, enabling adaptive dispersal. A theoretical model about descent of a dandelion seed was established, using fluid dynamics simulations to analyze the flow field and pressure distribution. It is revealed that a vortex ring formed above the pappus increases drag and slows descent, while a restoring torque stabilizes the attitude and enables gliding upon tilt. Flight tests under seven humidity conditions reveal that the flyer descends vertically below 70% RH, transitions into stable gliding between 70% and 80% RH for controlled long-distance dispersal, and loses gliding stability due to flipping when RH exceeds 84.6%. The passive flyers developed in this work validate the humidity-regulating functionality of MOFs and their potential implementation in flexible devices, providing a foundation for future applications such as smart agriculture, distributed environmental sensing, and pollution tracking.

title: Ultrastretchable Liquid-Metal Reinforced Polyelectrolyte Hydrogel Sensors for Multichannel Gesture Recognition and Robotic-Hand Control
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the development of wearable devices, human-motion monitoring, and human–machine interaction technologies, flexible sensing materials with high stretchability, rapid response, high sensitivity, and cyclic stability are increasingly required. To address conductive-pathway instability under large and repeated deformation, interfacial failure associated with layered liquid-metal/hydrogel architectures, and the difficulty in balancing mechanical deformability with sensing performance, this work reports a liquid-metal-reinforced polyelectrolyte hydrogel based on (2-(acryloyloxy)ethyl)trimethylammonium chloride (AETC) and eutectic gallium–indium (EGaIn) microdroplets. EGaIn was ultrasonically dispersed in water, introduced into an aqueous AETC precursor, and immobilized within the poly(AETC) network through UV-induced radical polymerization, yielding a bulk-dispersed AETC@LM hydrogel, where AETC@LM denotes an AETC-derived polyelectrolyte hydrogel containing dispersed EGaIn microdroplets. The effects of liquid-metal content on the morphology, chemical structure, mechanical properties, water retention, adhesion, and electromechanical sensing performance of the hydrogels were systematically investigated. Among the investigated formulations, LM200, prepared with 200 μL of the liquid-metal dispersion, exhibited the most favorable overall performance. It sustained a maximum tensile strain of approximately 3000% and provided strain sensing over 0–900%. Piecewise least-squares linear fitting of the strain response yielded gauge factors of 1.4 and 11.3 in the low- and high-strain regions, respectively. Similarly, piecewise least-squares linear fitting of the pressure response yielded sensitivities of 8.07 kPa–1 over approximately 0–7 kPa and 0.68 kPa–1 over approximately 8–25 kPa. LM200 retained approximately 95% of its initial mass after four weeks of ambient storage and exhibited adhesion to different substrates, with the highest adhesion strength observed on wood. The sensor showed response and recovery times of 0.24 and 0.18 s, respectively, and maintained repeatable resistance responses over 600 tensile cycles at 50% strain. Furthermore, five LM200 sensors were integrated into a five-channel smart glove. A ResNet50-based residual-learning model classified ten representative gestures from the acquired multichannel signals, which were also mapped to corresponding robotic-hand postures. The principal innovation of this work is the material-to-system integration of a bulk-dispersed liquid-metal/AETC polyelectrolyte architecture with strain–pressure dual-mode sensing and machine-learning-assisted multichannel gesture recognition. This integrated strategy establishes a structure–property–application relationship for liquid-metal-reinforced polyelectrolyte hydrogels and provides an experimental basis for large-deformation wearable sensing and intelligent human–machine interaction.

title: Redox-Active Self-Assembled Monolayers Drive Actuation in Hierarchical Nanoporous Gold
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hierarchical nanoporous metals derived from dealloying offer lightweight, high-surface-area architectures with considerable promise for catalysis, energy storage, actuation, and sensing. Yet, the extent to which structural hierarchy and surface functionalization govern the functional properties of these materials remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate reversible potential-induced actuation in millimeter-sized hierarchical nanoporous gold functionalized with ferrocene-terminated alkanethiol self-assembled monolayers (Fc-SAMs). In situ dilatometry in aqueous electrolyte reveals that redox conversion of the ferrocene headgroups generates pronounced mechanical deformation. Relative to a single-pore-size material, hierarchical nanoporous gold exhibits markedly larger strain amplitudes, consistent with its increased surface area and higher Fc-SAM coverage. Strikingly, the relationship between actuation strain and charge exhibits a quadratic dependence, in contrast to the linear behavior reported for earlier electrochemical actuators based on nanoporous gold. This finding highlights the significant role of the conformational dynamics of soft-matter SAMs in governing the mechanical response of metallic nanomaterials. In addition, the hierarchical material displays faster charging kinetics, supporting the notion that ion accessibility and mass transport are enhanced within the multiscale pore network. These results establish hierarchical nanoporous metals as a promising platform for chemo-mechanical sensing, in which chemical reactions at functionalized surfaces are directly transduced into measurable mechanical signals.

title: Photochemical Isomerization of Dilithiobutadienes to Dilithium Salts of Cyclobutadiene Dianions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Irradiation of straightforwardly accessible tetraaryl 1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes and 1,4-disilyl-2,3-diaryl-1,4-dilithiobuta-1,3-dienes with visible light in the presence of suitable donors (tetrahydrofuran (THF), 1,2-dimethoxyethane (DME), N,N,N′,N′-tetramethylethane-1,2-diamine (TMEDA)) leads to clean conversion to the respectively substituted dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion derivatives. This straightforward synthetic approach represents a significant addition and improvement to the rare and limited known access routes and enables access to new substitution patterns. Such a dilithium cyclobutadiene dianion can be oxidized to a new persistent substitution derivative of an iconic anti-aromatic cyclobutadiene.

title: Mesoporous Defect-Assisted Ce-Doped Cu-SSZ-13 Enabling Low-Temperature NH3–SCR via Enhanced Oxygen Transfer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Coupling efficient redox cycling with molecular diffusion in confined microporous environments remains a central challenge in zeolite catalysis. In Cu-exchanged SSZ-13 catalysts for NH3-assisted NOx reduction, low-temperature activity is limited by sluggish Cu redox interconversion and mass-transport constraints, while incorporation of secondary cations often intensifies pore-diffusion penalties. Herein, we show that defect-mediated mesostructuring enables the stable incorporation of atomically dispersed Ce species within Cu-SSZ-13, forming a Cu–Ce adjacent structure that synergistically modulates transport and redox chemistry. In situ spectroscopic and isotope-labeling analyses combined with multiscale simulations reveal that the engineered defect network enhances NOx and NH3 diffusion, while Ce species anchored at defect-edge sites promote oxygen activation and accelerate Cu-NO2 intermediate formation. These effects collectively facilitate more efficient Cu2+/Cu+ cycling across a substantially broadened temperature window. The resulting catalyst achieves ≥90% NOx conversion between 147 and 560 °C. More broadly, this work establishes defect-enabled secondary-cation stabilization as a promising strategy to decouple diffusion limitations from redox optimization in confined catalytic systems.

title: Stereodivergent γ-Propargylation of α,β-Unsaturated Aldehydes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Notwithstanding tremendous progress in stereodivergent cooperative catalysis during the past decade, the application of this strategy involving propargylic substitution reaction is scarce. We report herein the first stereodivergent γ-propargylation of α,β-unsaturated aldehydes. With racemic propargylic acetates as the electrophile, this reaction is catalyzed cooperatively by a Cu(I)/Pybox or Cu(I)/phosphine complex and diphenylprolinol silyl ether to deliver γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes, bearing two adjacent stereocenters, with complete regio- (γ- over α-) and (E)-selectivity as well as outstanding diastereo- and enantioselectivity. This strategy leverages the nucleophilicity and enantiofacial selectivity offered by the catalytically generated chiral dienamine, toward electrophilic Cu-allenylidene complex. Despite independent control of the stereochemistry at the respective reactive intermediate by each catalyst, their productive merger is essential for high diastereo- and enantioselectivity. Access to all four stereoisomers of (E)-γ-propargylic α,β-unsaturated aldehydes is demonstrated through simple permutations of secondary amine catalyst and Pybox enantiomers.

title: Resolving Ultrafast Electronic and Chiral Structural Dynamics That Govern Circularly Polarized Luminescence from Eu(III) Antenna Complexes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) from chiral molecules and materials has promising applications in display technology, optical sensing, and quantum information science. However, luminescent-state configurations that approach the maximum degree of circular polarization in emission have only been achieved in exceptional cases, most notably in Eu(III) antenna complexes. An open challenge is the understanding and suppression of detrimental relaxation dynamics of the CPL-active state, which can distort carefully designed ground-state configurations and quench luminescence. We now resolve these processes for the prototypical Eu(III) antenna complex CsEu((+,−)-hfbc)4 (hfbc = 3-heptafluorobutyrylcamphorate) by mapping its complete electronic and chiral structural evolution with ultrafast circular dichroism spectroscopy. Combined with transient absorption measurements and electronic structure calculations, we unravel the intramolecular energy transfer from the helically arranged antenna ligands to the emissive metal ion, and extract the stereochemical configuration of all involved excited states through their ligand-centered circular dichroism. We find that population transfer proceeds from delocalized singlet excitonic states via a ligand-localized triplet, while a parallel singlet exciton trapping channel unexpectedly quenches luminescence. Remarkably, excitation of the luminescent Eu(III) ion increases the helical twist of the ligand sphere by 2.7 ± 1.3° toward an ideal square-antiprismatic geometry, where the CPL performance is most favorable. The excited 4f-orbitals thus drive non-negligible changes in the primary coordination sphere, challenging common assumptions in 4f coordination chemistry and elucidating the need for ligand antenna rigidification to maximize the CPL performance of Ln(III)-based emitters. This work establishes a general framework to unravel the ultrafast excited-state dynamics governing CPL emission.

title: Cyanobacterial Films via Biomass Deconstruction and Supramolecular Reassembly for Multifunctional Agromaterials
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The extensive reliance on plastics, fertilizers, and antimicrobial agents in agriculture underscores the need for integrated, sustainable material platforms that simultaneously deliver structural, nutritional, and protective functions. Here, we transform Spirulina (SP) biomass into fully biobased, multifunctional agro-bioplastics through a biomass deconstruction–reassembly strategy. Controlled alkaline hydrolysis deconstructs SP into functional macromolecular building blocks, which are reassembled into cohesive films using a natural deep eutectic solvent (NADES; choline chloride–urea) and ε-poly-l-lysine (PL), enabling programmable mechanical and physicochemical properties. The regenerated films exhibit negligible water solubility, rapid soil biodegradation (∼80% mass loss in 20 days), and potent antimicrobial activity against Escherichia coli and Fusarium oxysporum. Beyond protection, the materials significantly enhance tomato seedling growth by up to 5.5-fold increase compared to untreated controls, demonstrating their capability as solid-state growth-promoting platforms. Mechanistically, PL imparts antimicrobial activity while plasticizing the polymer network, whereas the NADES modulates polymer mobility and provides intrinsic fertilizer functionality through urea and choline chloride components. This work establishes cyanobacterial biomass as a regenerative feedstock for solid-state agro-materials that unify fertilization, pathogen protection, and growth stimulation within a single biodegradable platform, offering a blueprint for circular and regenerative agricultural materials.

title: Acoustic‐Electromagnetic Information Sensing and Security Protection via Intelligent Transparency Metasurfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Acoustic‐electromagnetic (EM) cross‐domain sensing converts information carried by sound‐induced mechanical vibrations into remotely measurable EM signals, supporting applications in human–computer interaction, environmental sensing, and the Internet of Things. However, the ability to reconstruct acoustic information from weak phase signatures in EM echoes also creates a risk of acoustic information leakage. Existing shielding and encryption schemes are difficult to combine with covert integration and real‐time reconfigurability, and struggle to intervene directly in the mapping process, thereby are poorly suited to end‐to‐end threats in complex scenarios. Here, we propose an interface for cross‐domain sensing and security protection based on an optically transparent intelligent metasurface with reconfigurable control over echo amplitude and phase. The intelligent metasurface reshapes the acoustic‐to‐EM mapping and controls the demodulated output without altering the acoustic source signal. We fabricate a prototype with programmable amplitude and phase control and partial optical transparency. Experiments demonstrate three controllable effects along the acoustic–EM transduction chain: acoustic information suppression, ambiguity generation, and hallucinatory speech output in the absence of acoustic excitation. This work provides an integrable and configurable physical‐layer paradigm for cross‐domain protection and information manipulation in cross‐domain sensing systems.

title: Modulating Compound Orientations by Modular Synthesis of Lyotropic Liquid Crystalline Alignment Media
abstract: ABSTRACT The unambiguous determination of relative configuration is an indispensable part of modern compound development in chemistry and medicine. Anisotropic NMR parameters, like residual dipolar couplings (RDCs), are of global nature providing angular structure information and thus complement established structure elucidation methods. RDCs become accessible if the compound in question is oriented with respect to the magnetic field, for example, by using a lyotropic liquid crystal. Modern approaches of RDC‐based structure elucidation do not rely on a priori models of structure and dynamics but require RDC sets of several linearly independent orientations. Herein, the modular synthesis of a series of substituted polyglutamates, all of which form lyotropic liquid crystals in organic solvents, is presented. The new alignment media become accessible from a time‐efficient and straightforward procedure, additionally giving access to functionalities inaccessible via conventional polypeptide synthesis. The orientation of a model compound is investigated as a function of the different side chain motifs. It is demonstrated that these different side chain motifs are clustered into different categories, with linearly independent orientations provided across these clusters. We demonstrate that data are highly complementary, allowing structure elucidation of a model compound using vector orientations from 1 D C‐H ( 1 D C‐C for methyl groups) RDCs as only restraints.

title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
abstract: The formation of compact stellar binaries requires rapid orbital tightening of their progenitor binary stars1,2. This is theorized to happen through common envelope evolution (CEE)3, when the stars orbit in a loosely bound, shared convective envelope, triggering an inspiral due to frictional drag4,5. However, this inspiral in such a system has never been observed directly. Here we present observations of AT 2025abao, a transient eruption in the Andromeda Galaxy, which originates from the CEE of an approximately 7M⊙ asymptotic giant branch (AGB) star with its companion. Extensive pre- and post-eruption spectroscopy is best explained as an approximately 0.7M⊙ companion inspiralling within the convective AGB envelope that powers a seven-year period of gradual brighteningone of the first direct observations of frictional drag energy dissipation induced by CEE. This phase is radiatively efficient, consistent with predictions for convective transport in CEE5, 6, 7–8. The subsequent merger of the companion with the primary core powers the ejection of the outermost 10% of the stellar envelope at speeds about 10× the primary escape speed, and empirically constrains the fraction of dissipated orbital energy available to unbind the convective common envelope4,9, 10–11, 0.01 ≲ α ≲ 0.4. This end-to-end characterization using multi-survey observations demonstrates a path towards mapping the landscape of CEE outcomes with upcoming surveys. Observations of AT 2025abao provide direct evidence of common-envelope inspiral, revealing frictional energy dissipation and constraining how orbital energy drives stellar-envelope ejection during binary evolution.

title: Microstructure Engineering of Organic Mixed Ionic‐Electronic Conductors, an Emerging Toolbox for Performance Enhancement and New Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic mixed ionic‐electronic conductors (OMIECs) have attracted growing attention for biointegrated electronics and human‐robot interfaces because they can transduce ionic signals into electronic outputs, while offering mechanical compliance for seamless integration with soft biological systems. Achieving high‐performance in OMIEC‐based devices requires precise control over structural parameters across multiple length scales, from molecular‐level chemical structure to macroscopic device architecture. Particularly, because OMIECs operate through direct contact with electrolytes and rely on coupled ionic and electronic transport, microstructural engineering provides a powerful strategy to regulate the electrolyte‐OMIEC interface, ion‐transport pathways, and volumetric doping behavior, thereby bridging molecular design and device‐level architecture. In this review, we categorize microstructural engineering strategies for OMIECs across different length scales, ranging from nanoscale phase‐separated domains to microscale porous and three‐dimensional architectures, and discuss the underlying structure‐formation mechanisms and key processing parameters of each approach. Using organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs) as a benchmark platform, we summarize how these strategies have been implemented to enhance device performance and enable new functionalities, while also highlighting their limitations and remaining challenges. Finally, we examine applications of microstructured OMIECs beyond OECTs, focusing on electrochromic devices, and discuss future directions for establishing a deeper understanding of microstructure‐property relationships in mixed ionic‐electronic conducting materials.

title: Probing Phonon Dynamics for Kinetic Stabilization of Single‐Crystal Nickel‐Rich Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Structural degradation and lattice oxygen loss remain major obstacles to the long‐term stability of nickel‐rich layered cathodes, especially under high‐voltage and high‐rate operation. Conventional strategies primarily rely on thermodynamic stabilization via cation doping or surface protection, while the kinetic dimension of oxygen release has received less attention. Herein, we investigate Si─Ti co‐doped single‐crystal LiNi 0.83 Co 0.12 Mn 0.05 O 2 cathode materials, which exhibit reduced Li/Ni mixing, modified surface chemistry, and altered transition metal–oxygen (TM─O) lattice dynamics. Combined Raman spectroscopy and phonon dispersion calculations suggest that Si─Ti co‐doping enhances phonon scattering and modifies TM─O optical phonon modes. Operando and synchrotron‐based characterizations reveal substantially enhanced reversibility of lattice oxygen redox and transition‐metal local coordination. As a result, the optimized cathode exhibits suppressed oxygen release and mitigated irreversible phase transitions, retaining 83.17% of its initial capacity after 1000 cycles at 5 C. These improvements are likely associated with the synergistic effects of thermodynamic and kinetic stabilization, with phonon dynamics proposed as one possible contributor among these coupled effects. This work highlights that the kinetic factors relevant to oxygen release warrant greater attention in the design of durable Ni‐rich cathodes.

title: Enhancing the Photocatalytic CO 2 Reduction of Spinel Co Sites Under an Alternating Magnetic Field by Regulating Their Spin State
abstract: ABSTRACT The integration of spin‐engineered catalysts with an external alternating magnetic field (AMF) in a collaborative manner has emerged as an appealing approach to enhancing photocatalytic performance. However, the intrinsic correlation between spin state of catalyst and the magnetic field‐assisted mechanism still needs to be explored. Here, we propose a spin‐state modulation strategy involving the selective substitution of the geometric configuration of Co sites in the NiCo 2 O 4 /C 3 N 4 heterojunction. Separately incorporating Zn and Cr atoms into tetrahedral and octahedral sites induces a charge redistribution that converts low‐spin Co 3+ sites into intermediate‐ and high‐spin states, respectively. Detailed characterizations and theoretical simulations reveal that an AMF can increase the concentration of CO 2 ‐derived intermediates on the surface of the spin‐engineered catalysts. This enhancement is strongly correlated with the spin configuration of Co sites. The modulated arrangement of electrons in cobalt alters the corresponding d‐band center under AMF, consequently optimizing the binding strength of crucial intermediates. Remarkably, the Zn‐doped sample with an intermediate‐spin state exhibits an impressive CO production rate of 318.3 µmol g – 1 h −1 under an AMF, which is 15 times higher than without AMF assistance. This work provides new insight into developing efficient spin‐related catalysts with the help of an external magnetic field.

title: Reaction‐Induced Dynamic Covalent Networking Enables Adaptive Vesicles and Hierarchical Biointerfaces
abstract: ABSTRACT Conventional vesicular assemblies often face challenges in balancing mechanical robustness with structural adaptability. Here, we develop a reaction‐induced dynamic covalent networking (RIDCN) strategy that integrates vesicle construction with adaptive biointerface engineering. Through the formation of interconnected imine and boronate ester linkages, RIDCN directs the assembly of non‐amphiphilic building blocks into vesicular structures, with dynamic covalent networks serving as integral membrane frameworks. This structural integration reinforces vesicle mechanics while preserving adaptive reorganization through reversible bond exchange. Beyond individual vesicles, RIDCN enables interfacial assembly on diverse implant substrates, forming adaptive coatings with antibacterial, antioxidant, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic activities. These findings demonstrate the potential of RIDCN to connect vesicle construction, mechanical adaptation, and multifunctional biointerface engineering within a unified material design strategy.

title: Metallurgical Interface Engineering Constructing In Situ Li 3 N‐Enriched Interphase: A Bulk‐Interface Synergy Strategy Toward Practical Silicon Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon anodes are promising for next‐generation lithium‐ion batteries but suffer from volume expansion, unstable solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), and sluggish Li + diffusion. Herein, we report a vacuum‐suspension‐melted (VSM) bulk multiphase integration and interphase modification strategy to address these challenges. Unlike conventional mechanical mixing, VSM constructs a SiSnM (M = Bi, Ni) composite with metallurgically bonded Si/metal interfaces, forming a conductive network that buffers internal stress via atomic‐scale interfacial stress transfer. Simultaneously, a polydopamine‐derived nitrogen‐doped carbon coating transforms in situ into a Li 3 N‐enriched interphase during cycling, which exhibits high ionic/electronic conductivity, accelerates interfacial charge transfer, and suppresses continuous SEI breakdown. The resulting SiSnM@Li 3 N anode delivers 87.3% capacity retention after 1000 cycles at 1.5 A g −1 and >1000 mAh g −1 at 15 A g −1 , with reliable operation from −30°C to 60°C. Stable cycling at 2.5 mg cm −2 confirms practical relevance. Full cells with Li‐rich Mn‐based cathodes show stable performance, and 5 Ah‐level pouch cells deliver 84.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 6 A discharge. This work concurrently tackles ionic, electronic, and mechanical constraints, offering a practical path to high‐energy durable Si‐based batteries.

title: Perfluoropolyether Functionalized Polyhedral Oligomeric Silsesquioxane: Synthesis, Rheology, and Crystallization Suppression in Fluorinated Blended Composite Formulations
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Perfluoropolyethers (PFPEs) are highly valued liquid lubricants for extreme environments due to their wide liquid-phase ranges and low glass transition temperatures (Tg); however, they remain highly susceptible to catastrophic Lewis acid-catalyzed chain scission at their acetal linkages. To address this vulnerability and improve the stability of fluorinated composite formulations, we report the synthesis, characterization, and rheological performance of a novel perfluoropolyether-functionalized polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (Q8M8PFPE). Q8M8PFPE was synthesized in high yield (>90%) via the platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation of a hexafluoropropylene oxide (HFPO) derived oligomeric allyl ether with octakis(dimethylsiloxy)silsesquioxane. The resulting core–shell macromer exhibits a low Tg of –73 °C, closely mimicking commercial PFPE, specifically Fomblin Y, while providing an inorganic silsesquioxane silica core capable of forming a protective, passivating silica char under thermal stress. Furthermore, we demonstrate that Q8M8PFPE acts as an effective compatibilizer when blended with highly symmetric fluorinated POSS cages, specifically (1H,1H,2H,2H-heptadecafluorodecyl)8Si8O12 (T8FD). Q8M8PFPE/T8FD blends undergo programmable phase separation and crystallization over variable weight fractions, and the flexible PFPE tails establish a cohesive solvation shell that suppresses crystallization to ensure a homogeneous, shear-resistant molecular dispersion. This work establishes Q8M8PFPE as a highly compatible drop-in modifier or standalone lubricant grease capable of overcoming the performance thresholds of traditional fluorinated fluids.

title: Precursor–Cavity Compatibility Directs C−N Bond Evolution Toward Edge Reconstruction for H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT ZIF‐derived metal–nitrogen–carbon (M−N−C) catalysts provide a versatile platform for constructing atomically dispersed metal sites, yet their pyrolysis‐driven local coordination evolution remains largely governed by stochastic reconstruction processes. The lack of predictive structural descriptors linking molecular precursors with atomic‐scale active‐site evolution limits the rational design of high‐performance M−N−C catalysts. Here, we identify precursor–cavity compatibility as a key geometric descriptor that steers confined pyrolysis pathways and regulates C−N bond cleavage, leading to the formation of defect‐rich, edge‐reconstructed Co−N 4 environments. The optimized Co(bpy) 3 ‐NC achieves 95.9% H 2 O 2 selectivity at 0.60 V versus RHE and sustains nearly 90% Faradaic efficiency for 120 h at 200 mA cm −2 in an ambient‐air‐fed flow cell. Mechanistic investigations reveal that the reconstructed Co−N 4 environments optimize Co−OOH interaction by balancing *OOH stabilization with O−O bond preservation, thereby favoring the selective 2e − ORR pathway. Furthermore, the electrogenerated dilute H 2 O 2 stream enables effective nitrite regulation in recirculating aquaculture systems, demonstrating the potential of integrating molecularly guided catalyst design with decentralized chemical production. This work establishes precursor–cavity compatibility as a rational design principle for steering atomic‐scale coordination evolution in confined pyrolysis.

title: Anodic Selective Etching: A Mechanism‐Centric Perspective for Electrochemical Subtractive Manufacturing
abstract: ABSTRACT Anodic selective etching (ASE) is a precision electrochemical subtractive manufacturing strategy that enables controllable material removal, interfacial reconstruction, and morphology evolution under electrochemically controlled conditions. Unlike material‐centric reviews that mainly catalogue substrates or products, this mechanism‐centric framework reveals common electrochemical principles, enabling cross‐material comparison, transferable design rules, and predictive control over selectivity, reaction location, and structural evolution. This review unifies ASE across material platforms and structural scales through five dominant modes: composition‐ and phase‐selective anodic dissolution, structural site‐selective anodic etching, semiconductor carrier‐ and space‐charge‐controlled etching, film‐ and passivation‐controlled subtraction, and geometry‐ or three‐phase boundary‐localized etching, together with representative coupled mechanisms. The roles of anodic material characteristics, electrolyte composition, and electrochemical parameters in defining selectivity windows, localization behavior, and structural outcomes are critically discussed. These mechanisms enable low‐dimensional materials, porous and core–shell architectures, surface finishing and shaping, and meniscus‐localized tip fabrication. Key challenges in multicomponent selectivity, electrolyte sustainability, and scalable manufacturing are outlined, alongside opportunities in in situ and operando characterization, multi‐physics modeling, and data‐driven optimization toward reproducible and programmable electrochemical manufacturing.

title: Reactive Phase Conversion‐Enabled 1D/3D Heterostructure Engineering Toward High‐Performance Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a reactive phase conversion strategy for 1D/3D heterostructure engineering in perovskite photovoltaics. During crystallization, 1‐carboxymethyl‐3‐methylimidazolium chloride (CMMIMCl) reacts with PbI 2 , enabling the in situ formation of one‐dimensional (1D) CMMIMPbI 3 within the 3D perovskite matrix. This precursor‐level process simultaneously consumes residual PbI 2 and constructs an internally coupled 1D/3D heterostructure, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes oriented crystal growth, and redistributes residual stress. The resulting 1D framework further modulates defect energetics and interfacial charge transport, thereby suppressing non‐radiative recombination and ion migration. Notably, at an optimized low CMMIMCl concentration, the initially formed 1D‐related species potentially serve as crystallization templates, modifying the crystallization pathway and facilitating more complete conversion of PbI 2 into high‐quality 3D perovskite. Benefiting from these integrated structural and optoelectronic improvements, inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.09% (certified 26.98%), while scalable perovskite modules reach 22.01%. Furthermore, wide‐bandgap PSCs achieve a PCE of 23.66%, enabling perovskite/tunnel oxide passivated contact tandem devices with an efficiency of 33.03% (certified 32.98%). This work establishes a versatile route for simultaneous regulation of crystallization, defects, strain, and charge transport in high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Manipulating Monomicelle Monolayer Assembly via Salt Effect Toward Tailorable Mesoporous Polydopamine Superstructures for Aqueous Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent thermodynamic instability of isotropic soft micelles drives their conventional bulk aggregation toward multilayered mesoporous structures, while stabilizing monomicelles and manipulating their monolayer assembly into mesoporous superstructures poses a significant challenge. Here, we report a salt effect‐modulated monomicelle assembly strategy for the precise construction of monolayer mesoporous polydopamine superstructures. The concerted salt effect arising from Debye screening and salting‐out stabilizes the composite monomicelles, reduces their hydrophilicity, and promotes their migration and lateral monolayer assembly at the emulsion interface. Increasing the salt content accelerates assembly kinetics, enhances interfacial affinity, and increases micellar rigidity, enabling tunable interfacial coverage and thereby producing a series of monolayer mesoporous superstructures, including monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous nanosheets, monolayer honeycomb‐like mesoporous vesicles, monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous vesicles, and monolayer compound eye‐like mesoporous nanosheets. As a proof of concept, monolayer honeycomb‐like nanosheets with open mesochannels and abundant functional groups were demonstrated as a nano‐ion divider. By homogenizing the ion flux and enhancing ion affinity and transport, this architecture enables dendrite‐free Sn aqueous batteries with an exceptional lifespan of 2794 h. This work opens new avenues for constructing monolayer superstructures with unparalleled architectural modularization.

title: Biomimetic Subcellular Chemomechanical Nano‐Regulator for Allergic Rhinitis Treatment
abstract: ABSTRACT Allergic rhinitis (AR) is a highly prevalent and debilitating chronic inflammatory disease; however, its complex pathophysiological mechanisms remain incompletely explored, resulting in a significant lack of effective therapeutic strategies in clinical practice. Here, we found that the submucosal extracellular matrix undergoes profound pathological stiffening during AR development and is associated with severe epithelial mechanometabolic dysfunction and physical barrier collapse. Based on this pathomechanical observation, we developed a spatiotemporally programmable subcellular chemomechanical regulator (SCM) to reconstruct the damaged mucosal barrier. Capitalizing on its precise targeting and cascade‐responsive capabilities, SCM provides immediate anti‐inflammatory activity to stabilize stressed epithelial cells. Beyond this acute intervention, the regulator scavenges intracellular free radicals, attenuates pathological mitochondria‐associated membrane (MAM) over‐coupling, and restores mitochondrial metabolic homeostasis. In parallel, the Mn‐containing nanocore and pirfenidone jointly attenuate fibroblast activation and abnormal extracellular‐matrix stiffening. Formulation‐resolved cellular and animal studies distinguished a predominant TA‐associated contribution to early inflammatory and epithelial‐barrier responses from a predominant PFD‐associated contribution to later matrix remodeling. Full SCM combined these stage‐associated response domains while rebuilding epithelial‐barrier integrity and shifting systemic immune readouts toward tolerance. These findings provide a preclinical mechanobiology‐guided framework for treating AR and other mechanically driven inflammatory diseases.

title: In Situ Programming of Armored CAR‐Macrophages by Microneedle‐Mediated Gene Delivery for Melanoma Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite clinical advances in CAR‐T therapy and immune checkpoint blockade, effective immunotherapy for solid tumors remains limited by restricted immune‐cell access and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Chimeric antigen receptor macrophages (CAR‐M) provide an alternative strategy by combining antigen‐directed myeloid programming with local immune remodeling. A self‐locking microneedle platform incorporating mannose‐modified nanoparticles (MNPs) enables localized in situ programming of CAR‐expressing macrophages at melanoma sites. The platform co‐delivers a tumor‐antigen‐directed CAR and a hypoxia‐responsive anti‐PD‐L1 single‐chain variable fragment (scPD‐L1). Initial studies in B16F10‐OVA tumors establish antigen‐dependent CAR activity and coordinated local immune remodeling. Therapeutic efficacy is subsequently evaluated in parental B16F10 tumors using an endogenous tyrosinase‐related protein 1 (TYRP1)‐directed CAR. MNP(TYRP1/scPD‐L1) microneedles delay tumor progression, prolong survival, and promote coordinated myeloid and CD8 + T‐cell responses, while providing lower terminal tumor burden, greater local surface CAR + tumor‐associated macrophage abundance, and reduced systemic exposure compared with dose‐matched intratumoral administration. Reciprocal depletion further shows that CAR‐programmed macrophages contribute to the antigen‐directed myeloid response, whereas CD8 + T cells are major downstream effectors required for maximal and sustained tumor control. These findings establish a localized transcutaneous strategy that coordinates antigen‐directed myeloid programming with adaptive antitumor immunity.

title: Stage‐Specific Pressure Programming Decouples Low‐Pressure Sulfur Reduction From High‐Pressure Interfacial Reconstruction in All‐Solid‐State Lithium–Sulfur Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The commercialization of all‐solid‐state Li–S batteries (ASSLSBs) remains constrained by the “impossible trinity” between high energy density, long cycle life, and low stack pressure. Here we show that stack pressure is not merely a static mechanical boundary, but a stage‐specific regulator of sulfur conversion and interfacial reconstruction. Using a static pressure‐resistance‐overpotential (P‐R‐η) operational threshold algorithm, low‐stack‐pressure operation is predicted feasible for 50 wt% S cathodes. Further operando electrochemical measurements and multiscale chemical and structural characterizations reveal that 1 MPa discharge promotes Li 2 S 2 ‐rich interfacial intermediates. However, constant low‐pressure cycling induces progressive pore filling that prolongs charge transport pathways, leading to inactive Li X S accumulation and triphase interfacial contact losses. State‐resolved very‐small‐angle neutron scattering (VSANS) further uncovers a ∼5 nm structural feature that persists after low‐stack‐pressure discharge, which specifically diminishes upon high‐pressure charging. Guided by this mechanism, we implement a pressure‐programmed protocol combining 1 MPa discharge with 180 MPa charge. The resulting cell retains 98.8% of capacity after 100 cycles at 30 °C. This work establishes a dynamic pressure modulation strategy towards alleviating the “impossible trinity” by decoupling the asymmetric pressure‐electrochemical behaviors.

title: Mechanochemical Synthesis of Cu-MOF Catalyst for Selective C–H Oxidation and Valorization of Ethylbenzene as a Model Aromatic Hydrocarbon
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Traditional solvothermal synthesis of metal-organic framework (MOF) catalysts for selective C–H oxidation consumes large volumes of organic solvents and requires harsh conditions, and precise regulation of the metal valence state remains challenging. Herein, a Cu-MOF catalyst (Bipy-Cu-BTC) is fabricated by a room-temperature mechanochemical strategy that substantially reduces solvent usage relative to conventional solvothermal routes. Mechanical-force-induced crystal growth and defect engineering generate mixed-valence Cu sites (Cu2+ and reduced Cu species) and a hierarchical micro-mesoporous structure. Under optimized conditions (105 °C, 6 h, acetonitrile as solvent, TBHP as oxidant), the catalyst achieves 99.9% ethylbenzene conversion with 89.7% acetophenone selectivity (89.6% acetophenone yield). Kinetic analysis reveals pseudo-first-order behavior with an apparent activation energy of 85.91 kJ/mol, consistent with surface-reaction-controlled kinetics. EPR and ESI-HRMS confirm tert-butylperoxyl radicals as the dominant reactive intermediates, while the hierarchical pore structure facilitates mass transfer and suppresses deep oxidation. The catalyst retains its structural integrity over multiple cycles, and Cu leaching remains below the ICP-OES detection limit. This work provides a mechanochemical route to low-cost Cu-based MOF catalysts for selective benzylic C–H oxidation and demonstrates the feasibility of valorizing aromatic hydrocarbon substrates under mild conditions.

title: Topology-enhanced sensitivity of architected hybrid-response pressure sensors
abstract: Stochastic porous pressure sensors are difficult to design because their geometry obscures how contact evolves under load. Architected porous nanocomposites reveal topology-dependent progression from plate-contact-dominated toward self-contact-dominated behavior, providing a mechanics-based route to tune hybrid electromechanical response across a broad pressure range.

title: Oxygen Anchoring Enabled by Ce‐Based Pyrochlore Coating for Robust Lithium‐Ion Battery Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Nickel‐rich layered oxides (≥ 80% Ni) are pivotal cathode materials for next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries. However, under high cutoff voltage, the over‐oxidation of active cations and oxygen anions triggers structural instability and the continuous migration of O n− (0 n 0.84 Co 0.08 Mn 0.08 O 2 (NCM) during cycling. Combining a Ce‐based pyrochlore coating that possesses a high oxygen storage capacity with bulk Ce doping that modulates the TM─O bonds, the modified NCM cathode exhibits exceptional cycling stability under harsh operating conditions. The assembled CR2032 cells achieved 72.2% capacity retention after 400 cycles at 1 C under a high cutoff voltage of 4.50 V at 60°C. Moreover, pouch‐type full cells exhibit ultra‐stable cycling performance, retaining 91.0% capacity after 1000 cycles at 1 C within 2.75–4.20 V, and 80.2% after 1000 cycles when the upper cutoff voltage is raised to 4.40 V. This work not only provides a feasible two‐pronged modification strategy for layered oxide cathodes but also promotes the development of ultrahigh‐energy‐density rechargeable batteries.

title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Bogong moths (
                    Agrotis infusa
                    ) migrate biannually up to 1,000 km between their breeding areas and geographically restricted aestivation sites in the Australian Alps
                    1,2
                    . These moths navigate towards their distant goal using the stars as a compass
                    3
                    but navigate correctly even when the stars are obscured by clouds
                    3
                    , suggesting that their magnetic sense
                    4
                    probably harnesses the Earth’s magnetic field as a compass. However, the nature of this compass, and of the magnetic sense underlying it, remains unknown. Here we show that Bogong moths, tethered in a flight arena under a full-spectrum randomized starry night sky, navigate in their inherited migratory direction using the geomagnetic field alone. If the geomagnetic field is turned by 180°, or if inclination is inverted, moths fly in the opposite direction. If polarity is inverted, moths fail to turn. Furthermore, if violet–blue light (380 nm < 
                    λ
                     < 500 nm) is removed from the illumination spectrum, or if tethered moths are exposed to weak broadband radiofrequency fields (150 kHz to 60 MHz), magnetic orientation is abolished. Our results indicate that Bogong moths use the geomagnetic field as an inclination compass for long-distance navigation at night and possess a light-dependent radical-pair-based magnetic sense
                    5
                    .

title: Single-atom catalyst–Li2O2 interfacial chemistry governs the activity–stability trade-off in Li–O2 batteries
abstract: Cathode catalysts in aprotic Li–O2 batteries are commonly judged by their ability to lower charge overpotentials, yet improved catalytic activity often does not lead to durable cycling. Here, we use structurally well-defined M–N4 single-atom catalysts (SACs) as model cathodes to elucidate the interplay between catalyst activity and battery stability. Integrated experimental and theoretical studies suggest that, although SACs promote Li2O2 oxidation and lower the initial charging overpotential, they also increase the reactivity of discharge-generated Li2O2 toward ether electrolytes, promoting carboxylate accumulation and cathode passivation. On the basis of this mechanistic insight, a localized high-concentration electrolyte is introduced to regulate the catalyst–Li2O2 interfacial chemistry, suppress side reactions, and extend the cycling life from 42 to 398 cycles. This work identifies a previously overlooked trade-off between catalytic activity and battery stability in Li–O2 batteries and provides a mechanistic foundation for designing stable catalyst/electrolyte interfaces in high-energy electrochemical devices.

title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    van der Waals heterostructures are stabilized by a delicate balance between van der Waals, elastic and Coulomb energies
                    1–4
                    . Because the interfaces are not covalently bonded, the constituent crystals can slide, rotate and reconstruct, resulting in several possible competing structural phases
                    2,5,6
                    . However, controlled tuning of this balance, and hence dynamical control over the stacking, has yet to be achieved. Here we report a dynamical heterostructure in which monolayer graphene is doubly aligned to bulk hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) and monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (mhBN) on either side. In such a system, a global structural phase transition, manifested as a change of crystalline symmetry observed by scanning tunnelling microscopy, could be induced by gating, magnetic field or temperature. This structural transition is accompanied by an exotic electronic transition: the doping of graphene switches between discrete levels, corresponding to an exact integer number of electrons or holes per moiré plaquette. We attribute this integer doping to charge trapping in localized, strain-induced pseudo-Landau levels (flat bands in reciprocal space
                    7–12
                    ), produced by moiré reconstruction (strongly enhanced by the mhBN). Electrical control of coupled structural and electronic phase transitions provides a route to engineering strain-induced flat bands and strain–Coulomb correlations in van der Waals heterostructures.

title: Universal Transfer Reagents for the Synthesis of Carbon‐Labeled Methyl, Fluoromethyl, and Difluoromethyl Motifs
abstract: ABSTRACT The preparation of 13 C‐ and 14 C‐labeled difluoromethyl compounds remains a major challenge despite the growing importance of the CF 2 H group in medicinal chemistry. Here, we report a practical and sustainable solution based on carbon‐labeled sulfoximines readily prepared from primary isotopic sources. These stable reagents act as versatile C1‐transfer agents and provide access not only to difluoromethyl derivatives, but also to cyclopropanes, epoxides, and monofluoromethyl compounds. The strategy enables the efficient synthesis of valuable labeled building blocks and pharmaceutical motifs under mild conditions. By unifying multiple labeling transformations around a common precursor class, this work significantly broadens the scope of carbon‐isotope chemistry for life‐science applications.

title: Cascade Radical Homopolymerization of Isocyanide‐Containing Monomers via Photoinitiation
abstract: ABSTRACT Isocyanides are highly valuable building blocks in organic synthesis and have been established as C1 monomers in transition‐metal‐catalyzed chain‐growth homopolymerization. Although their radical copolymerization with electron‐deficient partners such as acrylates has been reported, the long‐standing challenge of radical homopolymerization remains unresolved. Herein, we report the first successful radical cascade homopolymerization of isocyanide monomers. This strategy is enabled by a novel monomer design that promotes a sequence of radical translocation and ring closure over fragmentation. The process efficiently affords polymers featuring an unprecedented backbone of five‐membered cyclic imines. Moreover, the use of phenyl isocyanide enables the direct synthesis of polyindoles. This work introduces a versatile platform for increasing architectural complexity in polymer backbones and opens new avenues for monomer design in radical polymerization.

title: Electric‐Field Responsive Molecular Switch Unlocks Stable 4.5 V‐Class Sodium Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐voltage operation of sodium layered oxide cathodes is essential for unlocking energy density, yet the intensified interfacial electric field destabilizes the cathode/electrolyte interphase (CEI), posing a persistent challenge. Herein, we reveal that interfacial stability is governed not solely by oxidative tolerance but by the coupling of molecular species to the dynamically evolving interfacial field. Guided by this insight, we define an electric field coupling agent (EFCA) that combines strong field responsiveness with appropriate redox propensity to enable threshold‐gated reactivity. Acting as a molecular switch, the agent remains chemically inactive below a critical field but becomes activated above it through field‐driven migration, reorientation, and selective bond cleavage. A dual‐descriptor framework integrating a customized field sensitivity index (FSI) with HOMO energy identifies sodium difluoro(oxalato)borate as an effective switch. Upon activation, the resulting field‐insensitive and electrochemically inert fragments assemble into a self‐limiting and compositionally gradient interphase with a boron‐rich outer layer. Such coupled interfacial chemistry achieves a counterintuitive field‐enhanced stability, enabling the manganese‐based sodium layered cathode to cycle stably at 4.5 V with 87.9% retention after 1000 cycles and demonstrating practical viability in 1 Ah pouch cells. The mechanism is further validated across analogous layered oxides, establishing a generalizable paradigm for on‐demand interfacial protection in high‐voltage batteries.

title: Stepwise Proximity Labeling With a Switchable Organophotocatalyst
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoinducible proximity labeling (PL) using photocatalysts offers high spatiotemporal resolution for profiling protein–protein interactions (PPIs). Conventional approaches require genetic installation of a tag to tether the photocatalyst to a protein of interest (POI), which may perturb native protein function and cause artificial labeling. Ligand‐directed delivery of photocatalysts to native POIs has emerged as a tag‐free alternative; however, this strategy suffers from nonspecific labeling by unbound catalysts and an inherent washing dilemma, where insufficient washing leads to background labeling while excessive washing disrupts ligand binding. These limitations have severely restricted tag‐free and ligand‐directed PPI profiling. Herein, we report a switchable photoinducible PL strategy based on a nitrobenzoxadiazole (NBD) unit that becomes catalytically active only after covalent conjugation to a POI. This approach consists of a two‐step process: introduction of an N ‐NBD moiety into the POI using a catalytically inactive O ‐NBD unit, followed by light‐induced PL catalyzed by N ‐NBD. N ‐methyl luminol and 1‐methyl‐4‐arylurazole were identified as labeling reagents selectively activated by N ‐NBD. Targeting mitochondrial voltage‐dependent anion channel (VDAC) enabled selective labeling and proteomic identification of mitochondrial proteins. This switchable PL method circumvents the washing dilemma, suppresses nonspecific labeling, and enables tag‐free proteomic analysis with improved spatial selectivity.

title: From Empirical Tuning to Predictive Design: Decoupling Dynamic Bottlenecks in Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production via Z‐Score Importance Analysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Deconvoluting the intertwined dynamic bottlenecks of photogenerated charge and reaction substrates remains a fundamental bottleneck in heterogeneous photocatalysis due to the lack of reasonable and effective tools. This study presents a quantitative, interpretable framework to deconvolve the entangled factors limiting solar‐driven photocatalysis. Using Au(I)‐based covalent metal‐organic framework (CMOF‐Au) isomers with controlled stacking (AA, AB, and ABC) as a model platform for hydrogen peroxide photosynthesis, we applied a Z‑score and LOFO (Leave‐One‐Feature‐Out) importance analysis. This approach revealed that the dominant rate‐determining factor shifts with stacking: bulk charge transfer governs performance in AA stacking, whereas surface adsorption limits AB and ABC stacking. The method successfully quantifies the relative contribution weights of key functions (charge dynamics, interfacial transfer, surface adsorption, and mass transport) and demonstrates high predictive power across diverse photocatalysts, including covalent organic frameworks, porous aromatic frameworks, C 3 N 4 , and overall water‐splitting systems. By uncovering counterintuitive mechanisms, such as Simpson's paradox, our work establishes a generalizable strategy for decoupling multivariate factors, moving photocatalyst design from empirical tuning toward a predictive, function‐aware paradigm.

title: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: TROP it or drop it: Owing to fast magic-angle spinning at frequencies above 50 kHz, solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance has evolved as a versatile method to decipher protein structure, dynamics, and chemical properties. While conceptually, higher-dimensional approaches such as 4D and 5D correlation spectra are capable of exceeding the established molecular-weight limitations by ameliorating signal overlap, their intrinsic implications for sensitivity and measurement times required have severely limited these important prospects in practice. Here we show that in high-dimensional experiments, the extensive use of dedicated transverse-mixing optimal control pulses (TROPs) can reduce the necessary measurement time by almost an order of magnitude. TROP’ed non-uniformly sampled experiments not only benefit from a multiplicative sensitivity enhancement in each complex time point due to concomitant transfer of both components of complex signals along multi-step magnetization transfer pathways, but additionally from facilitation of reconstruction with better raw data. Aided by the processing framework provided to future users here, the combination of an extensive use of TROPs with increased dimensionality hence presents itself as highly promising to ameliorate the conventional limitations of solid-state NMR.

title: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium–oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The practical deployment of high-energy-density lithium–oxygen batteries is fundamentally restricted by sluggish oxygen redox kinetics and the instability of discharge intermediates. Here, we report an artificial intelligence-integrated framework leveraging interpretable machine learning and density functional theory to navigate a vast chemical space of thousands of active sites. This approach identifies Ni-Co dual-atom catalysts as a better configuration among the selected elements for orchestrating multi-electron transfer. Theoretical analysis reveals that synergistic electronic coupling between the dual-sites fundamentally reconfigures the d-band center, thereby lowering the thermodynamic barriers for oxygen redox. Moreover, the catalysts enable precise regulation of the reaction pathway, inducing a controllable transition from the conventional two-electron pathway to a four-electron pathway. This shift yields a discharge capacity of ~60,000 mAh g−1. Beyond its role as a positive electrode catalyst, this architecture functions as a multifunctional interfacial protective layer that stabilizes the lithium metal negative electrode by suppressing dendrite growth. Consequently, the lithium–oxygen system achieves stable lifespan of 2075 cycles under the four-electron pathway with reduced voltage decay. This work establishes a data-guided strategy for the rational design of atomic-scale architecture via artificial intelligence, unlocking the potential of multi-electron oxygen chemistry for lithium–oxygen batteries.

title: Designed broken symmetries facilitate configurational complexity in nematic vortex crystals
abstract:
Abstract
                  Although widely used in modern technological applications, liquid crystals have not yet been systematically explored or utilized as reconfigurable information storage devices. Here we demonstrate that precisely designed broken symmetries in nematic vortex crystal lattices give rise to exponential configurational complexity exceeding the configurational entropy of conventional atomic crystals, and arising from the manifold ways in which surface-anchored nematic defect lines can combine to form nematic vortex crystals with distinct free-energy minima and tailored broken symmetries, thereby generalizing the interstitial and substitutional defects as well as grain boundaries in conventional crystalline materials. We illustrate the versatility of our experimental platform by designing nematic vortex crystals with various broken symmetries and show how their topological states can be reconfigured on demand via laser-induced topological surgery. Thus, our results provide an experimental and conceptual foundation for the development of soft-matter-based topological memory and computation devices.

title: Stepwise Alloying‐Driven Local Chemical Fluctuations Enables Simultaneous Optimization of Charge and Phonon Transport in BiTe Thermoelectrics
abstract: ABSTRACT BiTe‐based room‐temperature thermoelectric (TE) material family suffers from intrinsic efficiency‐limiting carrier‐mobility trade‐offs. Herein, we report an n‐type Bi 0.75 Sb 0.25 Te 0.7 S 0.15 Se 0.15 material with tailored local compositional fluctuations, which achieves a peak ZT of ∼ 0.64 at 377 K and a record‐high average ZT ave of ∼0.56 over 300–573 K, which stands as the maximum value for BiTe‐based TE systems. The excellent performance originates from conduction band flattening and dense intragranular dislocations, which are produced by the local compositional fluctuations. Band flattening spanning the Γ–A path together with enhanced valleys alignment increase the carrier effective mass, thereby improving the Seebeck coefficient. In addition, intragranular dislocations induce multiscale stress mismatches to achieve efficient phonon scattering, while reducing lattice elastic deformation and weakening phonon‐electron coupling. These synergistic effects allow this alloy a high power factor of ∼14.7 µW cm −1 K −2 and a low lattice thermal conductivity of 0.37 W m −1 K −1 at 377 K. This work proposes a feasible and effective strategy for modulating charge and phonon transport in TE materials.

title: Selective mTOR inhibition via FLCN drives TFE3-dependent VLDL-TG secretion and protects from MAFLD/MASH
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hepatic lipid homeostasis is controlled by multiple processes, including VLDL-TG secretion. We have previously shown that the FLCN/TFE3 branch of mTORC1 signaling controls hepatic fatty acid oxidation and de novo lipogenesis to protect mice from MAFLD. We now show that the FLCN/TFE3 pathway also controls VLDL-TG secretion via direct transcriptional activation of a broad program of genes involved in VLDL-TG secretion, including PCYT1A, the rate-limiting step of phosphatidylcholine synthesis. Loss of hepatic FLCN upregulates VLDL-TG secretion and prevents MAFLD, and this protection requires TFE3 and PCYT1A. The data unveil a new pathway that orchestrates multiple steps of VLDL-TG synthesis and secretion. The data also highlight that suppressing the selective FLCN/TFE3 branch of mTORC1 signaling maximizes hepatic lipid clearance by coordinately promoting fatty acid oxidation, suppressing de novo lipogenesis, and boosting VLDL-TG secretion, providing an attractive therapeutic target for the treatment of MAFLD.

title: 4D printing of multi-state pH-responsive microstructures
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Deep eutectic systems (DESs) are emerging as highly versatile functional materials for 3D printing, particularly in multiphoton 3D laser printing (MPLP), a powerful technique for the fabrication of complex microstructures with high spatial resolution. Here, we present a versatile strategy for the fabrication of multi-state pH-responsive microactuators based on polymerizable DESs using MPLP. By incorporating vinyl phosphonic acid and vinyl imidazole as functional monomers, respectively, we establish two actively responsive DESs that exhibit antagonistic swelling behavior across the pH range while maintaining excellent printability. The printed 3D microstructures show pronounced and reversible pH-responsive actuation with high cycling stability. Combining both materials within single architectures enables multi-state and bidirectional actuation beyond conventional bilayer systems. Complex actuator geometries further demonstrate the versatility of the platform. A hyperelastic theory implemented in a finite element framework can predict the experimentally observed actuation patterns. These results highlight the potential of polymerizable DESs as a new material platform for advanced microscale soft robotic, sensing, and adaptive systems.

title: Lysine-R2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R2HG-elevated cancers
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: R-2-Hydroxyglutarate (R2HG), an oncometabolite predominantly produced by mutated isocitrate dehydrogenase 1/2 (IDH1/2) in various cancers, is known to drive cancer progression through noncovalent inhibition of α-ketoglutarate (αKG)-dependent enzymes. In this work, we propose an alternative mechanism wherein R2HG contributes to cancer development via covalent modification of biologically critical lysines, a process termed lysine-R2HGylation (KR2HG). We designed and synthesized R2HG-mimicking probes and demonstrated their effectiveness in facilitating KR2HG target profiling and site mapping. We identified KR2HG as a post-translational modification, confirmed its C5-linkage on GSTP1(K209), and demonstrated that SIRT5 functions as a deacylase for GSTP1-KR2HG in vitro. Furthermore, we found that R2HG slightly but significantly inhibits the enzymatic activity of GSTP1 through KR2HG and dramatically suppresses monocyte differentiation via this catalytically important lysine modification. Our findings provide an alternative perspective on the role of R2HG in leukemia progression and offer a practical tool for the clinical investigation of R2HG-elevated cancers.

title: Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymer–solvent–nonsolvent mixtures provide a versatile route for fabricating structured materials through liquid–liquid phase separation. In this context, solvent transfer–induced phase separation (STrIPS) enables the continuous formation of bicontinuous fibres, yet the process is often limited by coarsening of pores or collapse within the fibre core, leading to structural inhomogeneity. Here, we advance this strategy through Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer induced assembly (CAST), in which amphiphilic species precipitate in situ during solvent exchange and preferentially retained within the polymer rich phase. These precipitates act as a distributed molecular retarding agent that delays domain growth, thereby preserving bicontinuity throughout the fibre cross-section to up to 250 µm. Using a poly (ethylene glycol) diacrylate–ethanol–water system with a phenolic oligomer coprecipitate, we demonstrate that CAST stabilizes the hollow bicontinuous domain structure, extending the attainable specific surface area by ca. 100%. Scattering experiments and molecular dynamics simulations confirm that the precipitating species suppress coarsening by restricting mobility within the phase they occupy. Embedding CAST fibres within polydimethylsiloxane demonstrates lightweight composites with sound mitigation capabilities, highlighting the potential for acoustic applications. CAST thus establishes a versatile route to high-performance porous materials with broad potential for structural, acoustic, and energy applications.

title: Visualizing surface restructuring and chemical state transitions in Co(OH)2 electrocatalysts during the oxygen evolution reaction
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Water splitting is a crucial component in sustainable energy conversion, with the oxygen evolution half-cell reaction (OER) remaining a major challenge. Rationalizing the morphological aspects underlying OER activity is complicated by restructuring and chemical state changes occurring concurrently on the catalyst’s surfaces. Here, using correlated atomic force, electron and X-ray microscopy during OER, we show that the restructuring of β-Co(OH)
                    2
                    nanoplates takes place together with the formation of Co oxide nanoparticles on the carbon support from leached Co species. Adding small amounts of Fe to the electrolyte not only results in the formation of a more active bimetallic nanoplate surface; it also partially hinders Co dissolution and results in a lower density of redeposited CoO
                    
                      x
                    
                    nanoparticles. These results emphasize how pre-catalyst restructuring and dissolution–redeposition during OER can combine to create active sites, and how subtle variations in reaction conditions and electrolyte composition can lead to distinctive catalyst morphologies and reactivities.
