title: GTP hydrolysis by Ras proceeds without a stabilized nucleophilic water molecule
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: A comprehensive understanding of the Ras self-inactivation mechanism at atomic resolution—specifically, intrinsic GTP hydrolysis converting the GTP-bound active form to the GDP-bound inactive form—is essential for designing therapies against Ras-driven cancers. Conventional models describe a biphasic GTP-bound state: Ras interconverts between inactive state 1 and active, catalytically competent state 2. However, the structural pathway leading to Ras/GDP via these states remains unclear. Here, we use time-resolved serial femtosecond and synchrotron crystallography to capture GTP hydrolysis in Ras crystals loaded with photoactivatable caged GTP, across timescales from milliseconds to hours. Photolysis yielded Ras in state 1—a conformation lacking a stabilized nucleophilic water characteristic of state 2. Remarkably, this state persists for hours and converts directly to Ras/GDP without passing through state 2. These findings challenge the prevailing view that state 2 is essential and suggest that state 1 can directly support catalysis, offering an alternative conceptual basis for targeting clinically relevant Ras mutants that preferentially adopt this conformation.

title: Distinct DNA-binding modes of Sp8 and Sp6 shape a hierarchical regulatory network in limb ectoderm
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Sp8 and Sp6 are closely related transcription factors expressed in the limb ectoderm, where they control proximo-distal and dorso-ventral patterning, yet their direct targets and molecular mechanisms have remained unclear. Combining genome-wide chromatin occupancy with transcriptomic profiling in vivo, we identify shared and specific targets and reconstruct the Sp8/Sp6 gene regulatory network, establishing Sp8 as its dominant, hierarchical node. Mechanistically, the two factors diverge: Sp8 binds DNA directly at canonical GC-rich Sp motifs, regulating targets including Fgf8 and Sp6 itself, whereas Sp6 acts as a transcriptional cofactor. Via indirect binding to AT-rich motifs through Dlx, both cooperatively regulate limb-patterning pathways, including Wnt, FGF, TGF-β/BMP, and Notch. Biochemical assays confirm that both form homo- and heterodimers and interact with Dlx5 through their zinc-finger domains. Together, these findings reveal how Sp8 and Sp6 orchestrate AER formation and dorso-ventral patterning, providing a mechanistic framework for congenital limb malformations such as split-hand/foot malformation.

title: Aggregation-induced radical
abstract: Differing from the aromaticity recovery-stabilized radicals explored since 1907 and AIE, we elaborate the mechanism, experimental and theoretical validation, material design, potential application and future directions of the AIR concept with ACQ.

title: The effect of inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste on the catalytic cracking of polyolefins
abstract: Polyolefin upcycling is challenged by inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste. Here the authors show that common metal contaminants, particularly zeolite poisons such as Na, K, Ca, Mg and Cu, drive catalyst deactivation during cracking, while sulfur and chlorine are more benign. The catalyst remains active over extended operation and has the potential to yield cleaner pyrolysis oils than thermal pyrolysis.

title: Entropy‐Triggered Mechanistic Reconfiguration: Unleashing Adjacent‐Site Oxygen Coupling to Circumvent Scaling Limit in Water Oxidation
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains the anodic bottleneck of water electrolysis for green hydrogen production. The conventional adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) is constrained by linear scaling relationships, whereas lattice oxygen involvement inevitably causes structural degradation, imposing a persistent activity‐stability trade‐off. Here, we realize a mechanistic transition from AEM to the oxide pathway mechanism (OPM), thereby circumventing the activity scaling limit, by constructing a noble‐metal‐free high‐entropy spinel oxide featuring a three‐dimensionally ordered macroporous (3DOM) hierarchical porous architecture. Mn/Al‐induced high‐entropy lattice contraction shortens adjacent‐metal distances, providing the geometric prerequisite for direct O–O coupling. Meanwhile, entropy‐driven electronic redistribution elevates Co valence and modulates Co–O covalency, optimizing oxygenated‐intermediate adsorption and enriching surface *OH species for subsequent O–O coupling. The 3DOM hierarchical porous framework further exposes OPM‐favorable sites and accelerates mass transport. Consequently, the catalyst delivers a low overpotential of 218 mV at 10 mA cm −2 , sustains stable operation for over 3000 h at 100 mA cm −2 , and enables an anion‐exchange membrane water electrolyzer to achieve 1.604 V at 1 A cm −2 with 2500 h durability. This mechanism‐guided high‐entropy design opens a route beyond the activity‐stability trade‐off.

title: Beyond Lithium Solvation: Tuning Cation‐Solvent‐Anion Interactions for Stable Lithium‐Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrolyte chemistry in nonaqueous solvents is central to the electrochemical performance of high‐energy rechargeable batteries, yet the molecular basis of ion solvation in these systems remains incompletely understood. In conventional dipolar aprotic electrolytes, the high electron‐donating ability of the solvent favors cation‐dominated ion‐dipole interactions, such that anions remain largely free or are only weakly incorporated into cation solvation structures. Here we establish an explicit molecular picture of cation‐solvent‐anion ternary interactions in nonaqueous electrolytes and show that these interactions critically govern both bulk electrolyte properties and electrode‐electrolyte interfaces. We find that fluorinated ether‐based solvents, despite being widely regarded as non‐solvating diluents, can exhibit selective solvation of high‐electron‐donating anions, including halides and polysulfides. Coupling these ternary interactions to the redox chemistry of sulfur electrodes suppresses the dissolution and migration of polysulfide intermediates in ether‐based electrolytes, thus mitigating the shuttle effect and improving the cycling stability of Li°||S cells. More broadly, our findings revise the prevailing view of solvation in nonaqueous electrolytes and provide a molecular framework for solvent design and electrolyte formulation to advance high‐energy lithium‐ and other monovalent cation‐based rechargeable batteries.

title: Pathway Selection in Phenol Oxidation by a Ni(III)−Hydroxo Complex: Solvent and Substrate Control of Proton‐Coupled Electron Transfer
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the factors governing pathway selection in proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) remains a challenge in oxidative chemistry. Herein, we investigate phenol oxidation by a late‐transition metal hydroxo complex [Na(15c5)][Ni(PS3″)(OH)] ([Na(15c5)][ 1 ], 15c5 = 15−crown−5 ether and PS3″ = [P(C 6 H 3 ‐3‐Me 3 Si‐2‐S) 3 ] 3− ). Oxidation in CH 3 CN affords a mononuclear Ni(II) product, whereas reactions in THF generate a mixed‐valent Ni(II)Ni(III) dimer, revealing a solvent dependence of both reaction pathway and product distribution. Reactions in THF exhibit saturation kinetics and a kinetic isotope effect (KIE) value of 2.1, enabling direct interrogation of the elementary PCET step. Hammett, thermodynamic, and semiempirical free‐energy analyses independently reveal a substrate‐dependent mechanistic crossover: Electron‐rich phenols undergo concerted proton−electron transfer (CPET), whereas increasingly acidic substrates react through a stepwise proton‐transfer/electron‐transfer (PT/ET) pathway. In contrast, reactions in CH 3 CN display inverse KIE value together with anomalous free‐energy relationships, indicating a kinetically coupled regime in which precursor association and PCET become experimentally inseparable. Moreover, oxidation in CH 3 CN proceeds 10 3 −10 4 times faster than in THF, suggesting that the polar solvent facilitates PCET through stabilization of a polarized transition state. These findings establish an example of solvent‐ and substrate‐controlled pathway selection in PCET and highlight how the reaction medium can influence the mechanistic manifestation of O─H bond activation.

title: Chromosomally unstable cancer cells exhibit heightened dependence on the mitotic SKA complex
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Aneuploidy and chromosomal instability are common characteristics of cancer but remain underexploited therapeutically. Chromosomally unstable cells are often selectively vulnerable to inhibition of the kinesin KIF18A, and this dependence is related to altered mitotic control. Here, we identify the spindle and kinetochore-associated (SKA) complex as a mitotic regulator that establishes a similar dependency. SKA complex loss is tolerated in cells with a defective mitotic checkpoint, but when mitosis is prolonged, it leads to mitotic errors and loss of viability. Genetic analysis reveals that the SKA complex and KIF18A are epistatic, although they function through mechanistically distinct mitotic pathways. SKA complex depletion selectively impacts chromosomally unstable cancer cells and mirrors the effects of KIF18A inhibition. We thus identify a cellular vulnerability associated with prolonged mitosis in chromosomally unstable cancers.

title: Toward a Deeper Understanding of Single-Atom Catalysis
abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts (SACs) promise control of heterogeneous reactivity at a molecular level by maximizing metal utilization and enabling deliberate tuning of local coordination and microenvironment. Yet SACs expose a central challenge in modern catalysis: the catalytically relevant site is often a working-state ensemble whose coordination, charge, spin state, adsorbate binding, and environment evolve under operating conditions. As the field expands toward bimetallic motifs, atom pairs, and hybrid SAC–nanoparticle architectures, multiple site families can coexist and interconvert. This complicates unambiguous site assignment and limits general structure–property relationships. This Review offers a critical mechanistic perspective on the use of single atoms in thermal catalysis, electrocatalysis, and photocatalysis. We first summarize stabilization strategies for host matrices, emphasizing how anchoring motifs and microenvironments govern site identity and its evolution. We then develop an evidence-based approach to site assignment that treats characterization as hypothesis testing and clarifies what can and cannot be concluded regarding coordination, electronic structure, site density, and working-state identity. Finally, we connect recurring descriptors to reactivity, selectivity, and durability. We thereby highlight benchmarking techniques, site-retention metrics, and durability protocols. The goals are reliable comparison of results across studies and the transition from empirical optimization to rational design of single-atom active sites.

title: Manufacturing Halide Perovskite PV: Considerations To Enable Wide-Scale Deployment
abstract: Abstract Perovskite photovoltaic (PV) technologies have witnessed rapid progress during the past decade and are rapidly approaching the stage of commercialization. With small-area perovskite solar cells rapidly overtaking many conventional PV technology records, scaling and material stability have become roadblocks to commercialization. Wide-scale market adoption of perovskite-based PV technologies can only be achieved when key challenges for all three pillars of efficiency, scalability, and stability/reliability are successfully addressed. Although lab-scale material stability and performance are often measured in controlled laboratory settings, module-scale reliability must be demonstrated in real-world conditions. Here, we aim to provide a comprehensive review of the current challenges to commercialization as well as recent innovations and pathways to overcome these challenges. For recent material and processing innovations, we focus on solution-based approaches, but we also briefly discuss some vapor-based approaches. For reliability considerations, we review module packaging approaches, current state of real-world demonstrations, and efforts to field test modules. We also discuss economic considerations and potential next steps on remaining challenges toward commercialization of perovskite PV technologies.

title: A pluripotent source of immune tolerance
abstract: Pluripotent stem cells produce extracellular vesicles with unique molecular signatures and potent immunomodulatory activity.

title: Pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for systemic immune modulation in diabetes therapy
abstract: Embryonic development is characterized by remarkable immune tolerance, yet whether this property extends to pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) has remained unclear. Here we show that EVs from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), including embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells, outperform mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in suppressing proinflammatory cytokine secretion, reducing T cell activation and inducing regulatory T cells. PSC EVs display distinct molecular signatures, containing unique proteins and microRNAs absent from mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs, including the pluripotency-associated proteins ROR1 and CD133 and members of the miR-302 family. Dynamic suspension culture of PSC aggregates enhances the EV yield, providing a scalable and reproducible source. Delivered via a biomaterial scaffold, two local injections of induced PSC EVs significantly improved diabetes-free survival in an antigen-specific type 1 diabetes model, increasing regulatory T cell populations in draining lymph nodes, as well as inducing systemic immune modulation and preserving β-cell mass. These findings establish PSC EVs as a scalable immunomodulatory platform for autoimmune disease and for immune tolerance in cell therapy.

title: An extracellular contractile injection system for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells
abstract: Protein delivery into plant cells remains a major barrier in plant biotechnology. The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC) is an extracellular contractile injection system, a phage tail-like bacterial nanomachine that naturally delivers proteins into insect host cells. Here we retargeted PVCs to plants by engineering their tail fibres to recognize the plant cell surface receptor FLAGELLIN SENSITIVE 2 (FLS2). We designed and characterized a library of FLS2-targeting PVCs and evaluated their ability to deliver native and non-native cargoes, including a fluorescent protein, Cre recombinase and R2 retroelement genome editor. Engineered PVCs delivered Cre into wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana benthamiana protoplasts and leaf cells with efficiencies up to 16%. Delivery was FLS2 dependent and scaled with receptor abundance, reaching 75% of leaf cells in FLS2-overexpressing Arabidopsis. We further demonstrated the PVC-mediated delivery of R2 protein, resulting in the targeted insertion of a reporter gene into the plant genome and the expression of the integrated gene. This work establishes PVCs as a platform for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells, laying the foundation for targeted and precise plant genetic engineering.

title: A master gene for Drosophila male courtship prevents the behavior in females via a truncated protein
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Decades of studies have established that a terminal gene in the sex determination hierarchy, fruitless (fru), controls nearly all aspects of male courtship behaviors in Drosophila and many other insects. fru is transcribed in a sex-specific manner to produce male-specific Fru proteins (FruM) and was considered nonfunctional in females. In this study, we identify a female-specific truncated Fru protein (FruF) that is specifically expressed during the pupal stage and distributed in both cell bodies and neuronal projections, in contrast to FruM, which is expressed from larval to adult stages and localized to nuclei. We discover that FruF cooperates with another sex determination gene, doublesex (dsx), to prevent male-typical courtship in females. Knocking down fruF in dsx-expressing pC1 neurons induces courtship in females. These results reveal that the master gene for male courtship prevents this behavior in females via a truncated protein, thereby refining the canonical sex determination hierarchy that controls sexual development and behaviors.

title: Targeted technology coadoption for reconciling energy savings and equity gains in the residential energy transition
abstract: Targeting burden reduction realigns technology distribution towards disadvantaged households. The study shows that solar co-adoption for these households can deliver equity gains, highlighting the need for bundled, multifamily and renter-accessible policies.

title: Optimal grid-forming distributed generation allocation and sizing in radial islanded microgrids under single-feeder contingencies: A loadability-driven approach
abstract: The transition from passive distribution systems to actively managed microgrids requires planning frameworks that account for islanded operation under network contingencies. In radial microgrids with inverter-interfaced, droop-controlled distributed generation units (DGs), a single-feeder outage partitions the system into two islands with different generation and load compositions. Under these conditions, DG allocation and sizing, combined with priority-driven load shedding, determine the loadability and curtailment needed to satisfy voltage, frequency, and line-current limits. This paper develops a loadability-driven planning framework for islanded radial microgrids that minimizes the total priority-weighted load shed across all single-feeder contingencies. The planning problem is formulated as a double-stage mixed-integer nonlinear program (MINLP). The outer stage selects DG locations and discrete ratings under a fixed capacity budget using a bound-guided search, while the inner stage determines priority-level loadability factors for each island through deterministic droop-based nonlinear power-flow (NLPF) evaluations subject to DG capability, voltage, frequency, and line-current constraints, with voltage- and frequency-dependent loads. On the IEEE 33-bus microgrid, the selected layout fully serves high-priority loads in all single-feeder contingencies and requires shedding in only two contingencies, with a weighted shedding objective of 0.2013 pu. Under a common NLPF evaluation, it reduces weighted shedding by 91% relative to a layout selected by mixed-integer second-order cone programming (MISOCP), while maintaining operational constraints on voltages, frequency, and line ampacity. Additional studies on droop representation, installed capacity, DG spatial distribution, load prioritization, loss-oriented planning, DG firm-capacity availability, and 141-bus scalability examine the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed contingency-driven planning framework.

title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Biomolecular thermodynamics and spectroscopy depend on relative conformer energies, local curvatures, and collective dipole fluctuations on the potential-energy surface. Conventional molecular mechanics force fields enable large-scale simulations, but their fixed functional forms can misrepresent infrared intensities, mode character, and environment-dependent vibrational response. Here we assess general-purpose machine-learned force fields by using finite-temperature infrared spectra across small molecules, gas-phase peptides, and monomeric, oligomeric, and solvated protein assemblies. To enable this analysis, we introduce QVib, a dataset of 293 molecules and 1366 conformers, together with peptide amide-band benchmarks and p53 oligomerization-domain models, to evaluate vibrational transferability from DFT references to experimental spectra. Across these systems, machine-learned force fields improve over molecular mechanics in reproducing DFT-level forces, vibrational frequencies, densities of states, mode eigenvectors, conformational energetics, and experimental infrared spectra. Among models with explicit long-range electrostatics, SO3LR provides the best accuracy–cost balance of the models tested here. These results show that machine-learned force-field dynamics can recover collective, environment-dependent vibrational landscapes at near-DFT fidelity, enabling spectroscopically validated biomolecular simulations at force-field-like cost.

title: Ikaros transcription factors prevent the activation of an endothelial cell program in bone marrow hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) are generally committed to the hematopoietic lineage, but how that commitment is maintained is not well understood. We show that the Ikaros family of transcription factors is essential for HSC identity. Ikaros, alone or in combination with Helios, is required to sustain the pool of multipotent HSCs and their downstream progenitor cells in adult animals, by directly repressing a core group of genes implicated in wound healing, cell junction organization, and actin cytoskeleton organization. Remarkably, upon in vivo or in vitro deletion of Ikaros or Ikaros+Helios, nearly one-third of the hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) rapidly exhibit an endothelial cell transcriptomic signature, and develop non-hematopoietic structures resembling CD144+ endothelial-like cells. These results indicate that adult HSPCs are highly plastic and prevented from activating an endothelial cell program by Ikaros family transcription factors.

title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
abstract: Homo erectus represents one of the longest-persisting hominin species, with a geographic range from Africa to eastern Eurasia from approximately 1.9 million years ago1 to 108 thousand years ago (ka)2. Despite this, there are still large gaps in our understanding of the adaptation capabilities of this species and the extent of its persistence in China. Assumptions over ecological preferences based on the Trinil3, Sangiran4 and Ngandong2 (in Java) open woodland-grassland mosaics have persisted, combined with limited direct stable carbon isotope measurements in Asia. Here we present a rich temporal and environmental context for nine hominin teeth, eight of which were morphologically and genetically identified as H. erectus5, found in two sister caves in Guangxi province, southern China. We modelled 43 radiometric ages from five dating techniques to establish a timeline for H. erectus presence in this region. Stable and clumped isotopes and trace elements from teeth were used to establish the dominant environments and their behavioural responses. We show that H. erectus was present in southern China between 324 and 184 ka, which is substantially more recent than previously established in this region for unequivocally H. erectus fossils at approximately 400 ka. The evidence suggests that they were persisting in closed rainforest ecosystems, thought to be the domain of only Homo sapiens, and were demonstrating long-term mobility and ecological flexibility. This evidence challenges the assumptions over the ecological preferences and behavioural limitations of H. erectus.

title: Impacts of Residence Time and Temperature on CO Electrolysis to Acetate at the 100 cm2 Electrode Scale
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The electrochemical reduction of carbon monoxide (CO) to acetate offers a promising route to upgrade waste carbon into a valuable product, yet scale-up beyond laboratory-scale cells remains underexplored. Here, we develop a 100 cm2 CO electrolyzer in a membrane–electrode assembly (MEA) configuration using a computational fluid dynamics (CFD)-guided approach. An anode-side serpentine flow field increases electrolyte velocity and anolyte residence time, facilitating oxygen removal and promoting further anodic oxidation of crossover ethanol to acetate. Combined with controlled reactor temperature, these effects improve acetate selectivity and operational stability. At 200 mA cm–2, the electrolyzer achieves a peak acetate Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 65% and stable operation for 140 h. These results identify anolyte residence time and reactor temperature as important reactor-level parameters impacting product distribution and stability, providing practical design guidance for selective and scalable CO-to-acetate electrolysis at the 100 cm2 scale.

title: Controllable Growth of Micron-Thick Films for Bifacial Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Bifacial perovskite solar cells require a micron-thick absorber layer to compensate for optical losses, yet the poor controllability in fabricating high-quality thick films critically limits device performance. Here, we developed an isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor atmosphere control system. By precisely tuning the duration of N2 purging to introduce IPA vapor into the PbI2 annealing chamber, we obtained a porous, highly crystalline PbI2–IPA intermediate film that facilitates subsequent ammonium salt intercalation. This results in a substantially lower energy barrier for the conversion from PbI2–IPA to α-FAPbI3, enabling the spontaneous α-phase formation at room temperature while completely bypassing the undesirable δ-phase. The resulting bifacial PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency of 23.78% (certified 23.71%) and a power generation density of 27.83 mW/cm2 with a short-circuit current density of 29.96 mA/cm2, at an albedo of 0.2, demonstrating excellent performance for bifacial PSCs. This work provides a rational pathway toward efficient bifacial perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Architected Si-Based Anodes for All-Solid-State Lithium Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Silicon anodes have emerged as a key enabler for next-generation all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs). In particular, the Li-Si alloy shows a low expansion coefficient and high ionic/electronic conductivity, but remains plagued by poor mechanical integrity and interfacial stability. Here we describe a Mg-doped Si interlayer at the Li metal-Li6PS5Cl interface, which electrochemically transforms into a Li-rich composite anode comprising Li14.39Mg0.61Si4 and Li-Mg alloy during cycling. Mg incorporation promotes the formation of a homogeneous lithiated Si framework, establishing a continuous ion/electron transport network. In addition, the unique porous architecture effectively mitigates stress and achieves favorable mechanical matching with Li6PS5Cl, thereby enhancing structural stability. Paired with a LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 cathode, the cell with an areal loading of 17.9 mg cm–2 delivers stable cycling over 1000 cycles at 3 C with 92.5% capacity retention. This multicomponent anode design offers a new paradigm for structural engineering of Si-based anodes and paves the way for high-energy-density ASSBs.

title: Halogen‐Dependent Regulation of the Thyroid Hormone Transporter by Antipsychotic Drugs and Their Analogues
abstract: ABSTRACT Antipsychotic drugs are primarily used to manage psychosis and other psychotic disorders. Their main mechanism of action involves blocking dopamine D2 receptors in the brain, and they remain important for the treatment for schizophrenia. In this paper, we describe an unusual property of several commonly used antipsychotic drugs and their analogues for their ability to modulate the thyroid hormone transporter system. Specifically, these compounds significantly increase the protein expression of monocarboxylate transporter 8 (MCT8), a key transporter responsible for carrying thyroid hormones across the plasma membrane in a variety of cell lines. Our findings indicate that the presence of halogen substituents plays a critical role in promoting the MCT8 upregulation. Furthermore, the magnitude of this effect is dependent on the nature of the halogen atom, with iodine‐containing phenothiazine derivatives exhibiting the strongest induction of MCT8 expression. The increased transporter expression was accompanied by enhanced cellular uptake of MCT8‐selective fluorescent probes, confirming functional activity. To the best of our knowledge, this study provides the first example of halogen‐dependent regulation of protein expression in mammalian cells.

title: Brønsted Acid Enrichment Around Zeolite‐Encapsulated Pd Promotes Efficient Tandem Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal‐acid bifunctional catalyst design is essential for selectivity control in tandem catalysis. However, reactive intermediates often experience a kinetic mismatch between metal‐ and acid‐catalyzed elementary steps, thereby being consumed through competing pathways and diverted toward undesired products. Herein, we developed a metal cation‐directed Al siting (MCD‐Al) strategy to enrich framework Al sites around Pd nanoparticles encapsulated in Beta zeolite (Pd@Beta‐MCD), enabling tunable Brønsted acid site density close to metal sites by controlling metal precursor loading. When Pd@Beta‐MCD was employed in benzene hydroalkylation, the spatial proximity of metal–acid sites accelerated transfer of Pd‐generated cyclohexene to adjacent acid sites, and the high Brønsted acid site density around Pd nanoparticles remarkably facilitated cyclohexene protonation for alkylation. Pd@Beta‐MCD achieved its maximum cyclohexylbenzene yield of 48.1% with a corresponding selectivity of 77.5%, outperforming Pd/HBeta (21.1% and 30.1%) and Pd@HBeta (27.7% and 38.3%), representing the best performance reported to date for this reaction. Moreover, Pd@Beta‐MCD showed superior cycling stability over eight runs. We demonstrated that the concentrated Brønsted acid sites adjacent to metal centers resolve the kinetic mismatch and steer the cyclohexene intermediate toward an alkylation‐dominated pathway. This work provides an effective strategy to strengthen metal–acid synergistic matching and facilitates precise control of key intermediates in tandem catalysis.

title: Luminescent radicals – synthesis, photophysics and applications
abstract: Room temperature luminescent radicals stormed the literature in the last decade. Structure-properties relationship as well as synthetic and computational aspects are reviewed. Overview of applications is presented.

title: VapC40 diverts autophagic flux from xenophagy to mitophagy via ammonia-dependent metabolic toxicity
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Mycobacteria survive inside the immune cells meant to destroy them. Toxin-antitoxin systems, gene pairs that help bacteria withstand stress, are abundant in the Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, yet their role in infection remains unclear. Here we show that the Mycobacterium bovis toxin VapC40 disrupts host nitrogen metabolism. VapC40 redirects glutamine catabolism in infected macrophages, producing excess glutamate and ammonia. Ammonia is transported into lysosomes through the transporter RHCG, raising their pH and rupturing their membranes. Ammonia then enters mitochondria, collapsing membrane potential and triggering oxidative damage. VapC40 recruits NIX to the damaged mitochondria and activates TBK1 on their surface, inducing mitophagy. At the same time, autophagosome maturation is impaired and fewer bacteria reach lysosomes, so the pathogen escapes clearance. Mice infected with VapC40-deficient bacteria show less ammonia toxicity and lung necrosis. These findings show that mycobacteria manipulate host nitrogen metabolism, and identify ammonia-induced organelle damage as a potential therapeutic target.

title: Dual-functional-unit modulation enables superior energy storage in high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-performance dielectric capacitors are indispensable for next-generation pulsed power systems. However, simultaneously achieving high recoverable energy density and efficiency remains challenging because of the intrinsic trade-off between polarization and breakdown strength. Here, we develop a dual-functional-unit modulation strategy to overcome this limitation in Bi0.47Na0.47Ba0.06TiO3-based ceramics through configurational-entropy engineering combined with microstructural optimization. Specifically, configurational entropy simultaneously tailors two key local functional units, namely local polarization configurations and oxygen octahedral tilt configurations. Multicomponent substitution at the A site (Ba2+) and B site (Zn2+/Nb5+) induces fragmented heterogeneous polarization configurations together with weakened and disordered oxygen octahedral tilt, enabling strong field-induced polarization, highly reversible polarization responses, and enhanced intrinsic breakdown strength. Combined with grain refinement and improved densification achieved by high-energy ball milling, which further enhances electrical homogeneity and suppresses interfacial polarization, the optimized ceramic exhibits a breakdown strength of 94 kV mm−1, a large recoverable energy density of 16.19 J cm−3 and a high efficiency of 91.3%. This work establishes dual-functional-unit modulation as an effective design principle for high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics and provides a general framework for overcoming the polarization-breakdown trade-off in dielectric energy storage materials.

title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Cyanobacteria are important primary producers and popular in biotechnology. Synechocystis 6803 is a model cyanobacterium, yet many coding regions are ambiguous, or have remained undetected. Here, we present a riboproteogenomic analysis combining ribosome profiling with inhibitors that stall ribosomes at translation initiation and termination sites, and proteogenomic re-annotation of its genome. Based on proteogenomics, we report translation of 3055 annotated genes (83%), 3492 based on Ribo-seq (95.2%), and 3,018 supported by both methods (82%). The data suggest additional protein-coding genes and corrections for annotated ones. We validate 15 proteins translated from antisense, intergenic and intragenic loci and provide proteogenomic support for up to 69 additional, mostly small proteins. We identify three genes with ~300 nt long intragenic out-of-frame translons and demonstrate that internal and host translons are translated into interacting proteins. Our data are accessible at https://www.bioinf.uni-freiburg.de/~ribobase/. They illustrate the enormous value of consolidating genome annotations with integrated experimental data.

title: Poxviruses probably evolved in the digestive system of animals
abstract: Large and giant DNA viruses that infect unicellular eukaryotes are abundant in the environment but have rarely been found in the gut microbiome. The discovery of such viruses that prevail in the digestive system of humans and animals exposes a long-overlooked facet of the gut microbiome that clarifies the origin of poxviruses.

title: Meet ‘egoviruses’: the surprise microbes living in the guts of millions of people
abstract: Egoviruses could be the evolutionary missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and those that can infect people.

title: A new view of Amazonian leaf seasonality
abstract: Much of the Amazon rainforest was thought to be evergreen, but high-resolution satellite imagery reveals that many of its trees can remain leafless for longer than expected.

title: Injured locusts heal or are cannibalized depending on levels of a bacterial odour molecule
abstract: When migratory locusts are injured, an odorous chemical produced by bacteria living in or on their bodies activates the immune system, helping them to fight disease-causing agents. However, when a wound is large and the chemical becomes too concentrated, it attracts cannibalistic locusts. At low levels, guaiacol promotes immune function; at high levels, it prompts other locusts to eat their swarm-mate.

abstract: Demonstrating your location to someone far away is surprisingly hard. Quantum correlations offer a way to do so without needing to trust any quantum hardware.

title: LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of exocytic RABs disrupts neurotrophin/neuropeptide secretion
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Neuropeptide signals such as BDNF secreted from dense-core vesicles (DCVs) are essential for neuronal development, maturation and survival. RAB3 GTPases are established regulators of DCV exocytosis, but their functional diversity remains poorly understood. Here, we use live-cell imaging and neuropeptidomics to show that distinct exocytic RABs control DCV exocytosis in a neuron type specific manner, whereas RIM1/2 is a universal effector. Striatal neurons express both RAB3A and RAB27B but, surprisingly, only the latter controls DCV exocytosis. This is explained by selective phosphorylation of RAB3A by LRRK2, preventing its recruitment to DCVs. Finally, a LRRK2 hyperactive mutation associated with Parkinson’s disease disrupts DCV exocytosis in both hippocampal and striatal neurons. These findings uncover an unexpected diversity in controlling neuropeptide secretion in different neurons and establish LRRK2-mediated inhibition of RAB recruitment to DCVs as a powerful inhibitory principle that may also contribute to neurodegeneration upon gain-of-function mutations.

title: Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
abstract: Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light-matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6-arising from collective quantum interference among emitters-has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open new opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8-10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

title: Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions
abstract: Corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement's temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement's Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Quantum field theories provide fundamental models of complex interacting systems
                    1–3
                    , from high-energy physics and cosmology to condensed matter. However, solving these models in non-perturbative and dynamical regimes is often challenging, particularly in more than one spatial dimension. Analogue simulation using tunable synthetic quantum systems can both verify existing theoretical predictions and lead to physical insights. Here we realize analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time), using two coherently coupled spin components
                    4,5
                    in a uniform two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate
                    6,7
                    . Specifically, we encode the paradigmatic sine-Gordon model
                    8,9
                    in the long-wavelength modes of the field describing the relative phase,
                    ϕ
                    , of the two components. In the perturbative regime, collective field excitations exhibit a relativistic dispersion with a tunable mass gap. We also observe explicitly non-perturbative phenomena, including the existence of topological domain walls across which
                    ϕ
                    rapidly winds by 2π (ref.
                    10
                    ). Our work opens possibilities for studies of cosmologically relevant phenomena including preheating
                    11,12
                    , dynamics of topological defects
                    13,14
                    and relativistic false-vacuum decay
                    15–19
                    .

title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
abstract: Metabolic disorders such as diabetes mellitus are global health crises driven by metabolic imbalance, chronic inflammation and dysfunction of the neuroimmune axis1-3. Electroceuticals targeting the autonomic nervous system have shown anti-inflammatory effects, yet existing systems lack the metabolic interoceptive feedback to fully restore immune-metabolic homeostasis4-9. Here we report an artificial neuroimmune axis (NeuroAxis) as a closed-loop immunomodulatory therapy for treating metabolic diseases. Analogous to its biological counterpart, NeuroAxis is solely powered by endogenous glucose, operating without batteries or wireless power transfer. It emulates the vagal reflex through closed-loop neuromodulation with metabolic interoceptive feedback. In a rat model of type 1 diabetes, NeuroAxis promotes the recovery of insulin-producing pancreatic β-cells and reduces inflammatory immune responses; in a rat model of type 2 diabetes, it drives macrophage remodelling and reduces systemic chronic inflammation. In both models, NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation. Our artificial neuroimmune axis promotes substantial advances in treating metabolic disorders and represents a general approach for autonomously regulating interorgan communication, central to homeostasis and pathophysiology.

title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
abstract: Current understanding of the host tissue response to solid tumours is largely based on investigations of tumour types in isolation1. Given the breadth and diversity of human tumour pathology and contributions of tumour microenvironment (TME) cells to disease progression, pan-cancer analysis is needed to bridge major themes of stromal and immune cell evolution. To date, however, efforts to compare the TME response across cancers have been limited in scope2,3. Here we conduct a comprehensive pan-cancer analysis by algorithmically screening thousands of publicly available single-cell transcriptomic datasets for stromal and immune signatures across species and tissue types. We demonstrate conserved hallmarks of host cell transcriptional programming in response to malignancy across 42 cancer types in more than 2,000 human and mouse tumour samples. These findings are codified as an interactive web atlas ( tmeatlas.stanford.edu ) and software package (scTME) that will serve as practical resources for the systematic interrogation of the TME in tumours.

title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
abstract: Position information underpins many modern technologies, from navigation and timing to authentication and critical infrastructure1-3. However, classical methods of proving that information originates from a particular position are vulnerable to spoofing4-6. This limitation can be overcome with quantum technologies7-16, but current protocols rely on trust in quantum hardware that can be undermined17,18, or require quantum computers and bounds on adversarial computation19. Nevertheless, there has been considerable interest in experimental demonstrations, and aspects of these protocols have been implemented20-22. Here we introduce and experimentally demonstrate the Bell-test quantum position verification protocol for device-independent quantum position verification that guarantees security with only observed correlations from a loophole-free Bell test23-25 across a quantum network. In the experiment, we implement a version of this device-independent protocol against adversaries who, before each trial, are weakly entangled. Our demonstration achieves a one-dimensional localization 2.47(2) times smaller than the best, necessarily non-remote, classical localization protocol. Compared with classical protocols with identical latencies, the localization volume is 4.53(5) times smaller, representing a certifiable quantum advantage. The general Bell-test protocol is loss-tolerant and secure against adversaries with substantial quantum resources. This work allows digital security to be anchored to physically trusted locations, enabling new position-based authentication protocols for applications such as financial transactions, legal agreements and securing critical infrastructure26-29.

title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Resistance in standard conductors decreases with increasing cross-section. Yet, in low-dimensional superconductors and superfluids, residual resistance arises from topological fluctuations of the order parameter, manifesting as phase slips in one-dimensional (1D) and vortices in two-dimensional (2D) systems. How resistance and dissipation evolve as geometry interpolates between these regimes remains an open question. This evolution is masked in solid-state experiments by disorder, impurities and geometric imperfections
                    1–3
                    , and poses theoretical challenges due to competing dissipative processes and pronounced finite-size effects. Here, we use a defect-free unitary Fermi gas in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox: in the crossover from one dimension to two dimensions, the resistance reaches a minimum. There, widening a channel increases its resistance. Narrower, quasi-1D channels show dissipation described by Langer–Ambegaokar–McCumber–Halperin theory of phase slips
                    4
                    . In this regime, varying the channel width yields the predicted exponential scaling of the activation factor over many orders of magnitude. Wider, quasi-2D channels show dissipation consistent with phase-slip events described by a finite-size vortex model
                    5
                    . The minimal dissipation in the dimensional crossover reflects a transition in the dominant dissipative mechanism, with both 1D and 2D events simultaneously suppressed. Our measurements suggest a route to minimizing dissipation in superconducting devices and provide a benchmark for theoretical efforts aimed at describing the dimensional crossover.

title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
abstract:
Abstract
                  
                    Photonic integrated circuits are emerging as a key technology for compact, analogue and energy-efficient optical information processing
                    1
                    . Yet, their practical implementation remains limited by the intrinsically weak optical nonlinearities of conventional materials, which demand high power and large device footprints to achieve substantial nonlinear responses
                    2
                    . Exciton–polaritons, hybrid light–matter excitations of semiconducting materials, offer a promising route to overcome these limitations by combining strong optical nonlinearities with the high speed and scalability typical of photonic platforms
                    3–5
                    . However, despite their potential, fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification have remained elusive. Here we demonstrate a fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings these functionalities together in a single-step-grown platform. We realize precise and scalable polariton circuits with integrated gratings that act as both couplers and reflectors, enabling in-plane Fabry–Pérot cavities. These structures support robust in-plane polariton lasing with coherent guided emission at a geometry-defined wavelength, optical amplification of propagating polaritons and nonlinear optical phase control exceeding π, all within the same on-chip architecture. Our results establish perovskite polariton circuits as a scalable platform for active and interferometric integrated photonics.

title: TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits
abstract: A major goal in neuroscience is to map the transformation of information as it flows through the brain. For example, neurons at many levels of the visual hierarchy are attuned to motion direction1-5. However, links between motion-selective computations and cell types at various stages of the visual hierarchy remain unidentified. A key first step in delineating these relationships is to map the wiring diagrams that connect different motion-selective cell types. Here we establish a systematic, cell-type-specific circuit-mapping method, combining an anterograde trans-neuronal fluorescent tracer (mWGA-mCherry)6 with spatial transcriptomics (multiplexed error-robust fluorescence in situ hybridization (MERFISH))7,8 to establish TransA-MERFISH. We used TransA-MERFISH to comprehensively map the synaptic target cell types of four retinal ganglion cell subclasses in superior colliculus (SC) at cell-type resolution. These experiments unexpectedly revealed that retinal on-off direction-selective ganglion cells (ooDSGCs) innervate several direction-selective SC cell types, but do not innervate a SC cell type that was previously reported to display strong direction-selective responses. We validated these results using orthogonal approaches and demonstrated the sensitivity and specificity of TransA-MERFISH. Functional studies of SC activity before and after ablation of retinal direction-selective circuits confirmed that these computationally distinct, ooDSGC-dependent and -independent direction-selective cell types are commingled in SC. Together, our study establishes TransA-MERFISH as a robust framework for mapping wiring diagrams at the cell-type level and uncovers divergent computational mechanisms of motion detection in early visual processing.

title: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies
abstract: The Amazon rainforest is a cornerstone of regional and global carbon cycling1 and is widely regarded and modelled as a perennially evergreen ecosystem2,3. This prevailing view, however, masks substantial fine-scale variation in leaf phenology, limiting our capacity to predict ecosystem responses to climate change. Here by combining 10-m Sentinel-2 observations with machine learning, we uncover pervasive, spatially structured seasonal deciduousness across the basin. In 70.0% of the Amazon, leaf shedding precedes leaf flushing by at least 3 months, creating pronounced asynchrony between deciduousness and greenness seasonality, whereas the remainder shows near-synchronous phenology. Hydroclimate emerges as the dominant factor associated with this asynchrony across 51.6% of the area, followed by soil properties (33.2%) and light availability (15.2%). Motivated by this widespread decoupling between deciduousness and canopy greenness, we incorporated deciduousness-constrained leaf turnover and the resulting leaf-age demography into ecophysiological models, yielding spatially widespread improvements in the seasonal agreement between simulated gross primary productivity and satellite-derived photosynthetic seasonality across 79.9% of the basin. These findings challenge the conventional view of Amazonian phenology, demonstrating that previously overlooked deciduousness influences Amazonian carbon dynamics. Incorporating these insights into process-based models is essential for refining projections of climate-forest feedbacks in the Amazon and for understanding its ecological functions under accelerating global change.

title: Carbon Upgrading of Glycerol to Glycolic Acid and Formic Acid via Radical-Mediated C–C Cleavage Using Gallium-Doped TiO2
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Precise C–C cleavage of biomass-derivative polyols is a promising yet challenging way to produce value-added chemicals. Herein, we designed a Ga-doped TiO2 with a preferential facet for highly selective glycerol upgrading to glycolic acid and formic acid in equal quantities, achieving a liquid-phase carbon balance of 94.5% and a total carbon closure of 98.2%. Detailed spectroscopic studies revealed that the interstitial Ga doping modulates the localized electronic structure of O–Ti–O sites, which drives the precise C–C cleavage by the surface-adsorbed hydroxyl radical. Mechanistic investigations identified glyceraldehyde absorbed on Ti sites as a key intermediate. It is coordinated to a bridge-adsorbed hydroxyl species on O–Ti–O sites, which attacks the C–C–O bond to produce break into •CH2OH and glycolaldehyde, and finally form formic acid and glycolic acid. This unique configuration of bridged hydroxyl species on doped TiO2 stabilizes the carboxylate intermediate and effectively suppresses overoxidation. The strategy is validated using a variety of polyol substrates and is successfully coupled with a self-powered photoelectrochemical–photovoltaic tandem device. This work establishes a radical-mediated route for the atom-efficient upgrading of biomass polyols with targeted cleavage of C–C bonds and minimal carbon emission.

title: A Tailor-Made Guanidine Ionizable Lipid as a Bifunctional mRNA Carrier and Nitric Oxide Production Inhibitor
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are the leading clinical platform for mRNA delivery, yet their capacity to trigger macrophage-driven inflammatory responses remains a fundamental barrier to therapeutic safety and efficacy. Here, we introduce a design principle in which a tailor-made nitric oxide (NO) inhibitory motif is embedded directly into the ionizable lipid, creating a single molecular scaffold that simultaneously delivers mRNA and suppresses macrophage inflammation. Screening of a focused acyl-guanidine library in LPS-induced peritoneal macrophages identified G9 as a potent NO inhibitor and reprogrammed macrophage polarization from the pro-inflammatory M1 to the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. Conjugation of the G9 headgroup to a lipid tail yielded G9-1, an NO-inhibitory ionizable lipid that retains anti-inflammatory activity and preferentially delivers mRNA to pulmonary vascular endothelial cells and alveolar macrophages in vivo. In a murine model of acute lung injury (ALI), G9-1 LNPs loaded with IL-10 mRNA reduce pulmonary immune cell infiltration, suppress inflammatory cytokine production, and attenuate systemic inflammation. These results establish NO inhibition as an actionable molecular design principle for intrinsically anti-inflammatory LNPs and position G9-1 as a dual-function ionizable lipid for safer and more effective mRNA therapeutics.

title: The emerging geopolitics of sustainable aviation fuel: Policy architectures, book-and-claim and european strategic dependencies
abstract: Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is becoming a strategic component of aviation decarbonization, but its expansion depends on technological, economic, institutional, and resource conditions. This study compares the combinations of policy instruments, structural production characteristics, and market-governance arrangements observed in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, Singapore, and Brazil, and considers the potential strategic vulnerabilities these configurations suggest, particularly for the European Union. The comparative qualitative policy analysis draws on peer-reviewed literature, legislation, regulatory documents, and institutional sources, organized through a single four-part framework: policy-instrument mix; structural production conditions; market and governance conditions; and potential strategic vulnerabilities. The cases display different configurations. The European Union and the United Kingdom emphasize mandatory demand; the United States relies more heavily on producer incentives; Japan and Singapore emphasize coordination and supply security; and Brazil combines established biofuel capabilities with a developing SAF framework. These observations do not identify causal effects or rank the configurations. Instead, they indicate possible exposure to feedstock, production, finance, policy-continuity, import, and certification constraints. Book-and-Claim is examined as a governance arrangement that separates environmental attributes from physical fuel flows; its practical contribution depends on credible certification, verification, registry governance, and interoperability. For the European Union, the comparison suggests that regulatory leadership may coexist with external supply and institutional dependencies. The concept of resilient interdependence is therefore proposed as a policy lens rather than a measured outcome.

title: An Autonomous Off-Grid MOF Water Harvester for Extreme Arabian Desert Conditions
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Here we report an off-grid, passively heated, sorbent-assisted atmospheric water harvesting device. A metal–organic framework, Al(μ2–OH)[(E)-5-(2-carboxyvinyl)furan-2-carboxylate], is integrated as thin coatings in a disc-stack architecture to enhance moisture transport and heat transfer. Under laboratory conditions, the device harvested 660 mL kgMOF–1 day–1 and recovered 175 mL of water across two cycles in an 11.5 h simulated day, demonstrating multicyclic operation in a passively heated water harvester. Field tests near Al-Muzahmiyya (24.3416° N, 46.0203° E) in the Arabian Desert of Saudi Arabia, performed under frequent sandstorms and extremely challenging conditions for water harvesting (RHavg = 12.4%, Tavg = 20.5 °C), including dust-attenuated solar irradiance (Iavg = 496 W m–2) produced 46.7 ± 1.5 mL day–1 (185 mL kgMOF–1 day–1). These results demonstrate the highest reported specific productivity for a passively heated water harvester under very low humidity (RHavg < 20%) desert operation and represent the most severe reported field deployment conditions for any water harvester.

title: Revealing Bulk-Phase Reactivity of Fe-Based Catalyst in the Reverse Water–Gas Shift Reaction
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous catalysis is conventionally interpreted as a surface-localized process, yet many catalysts undergo extensive reaction-driven restructuring that may fundamentally redistribute reactivity beyond the interface. Here we combine microscopy, isotope-labeling experiments, and large-scale molecular dynamics driven by a machine-learning interatomic potential (MLIP-MD) to investigate reactive carbon–oxygen chemistry in iron catalysts relevant to the reverse water–gas shift reaction. We show that under reaction conditions, the catalyst evolves into a dynamic FeOx/Fe3C mixed phase in which carbon and oxygen continuously redistribute across surface, subsurface and bulk regions. Isotope experiments reveal that bulk carbon is catalytically active, while simulations identify initial C–O association across a broad depth range, including within the catalyst interior, for carbon atoms subsequently removed as CO/CO2. Free-energy calculations characterize representative C–O association pathways at the surface and within the catalyst interior. Together, these results support CO formation beyond conventional surface sites and a surface-to-bulk catalytic picture for dynamically evolving iron catalysts.

title: De Novo Folding Mechanisms of Lasso Peptides
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lasso peptides adopt a distinctive [1] rotaxane conformation, yet the principles governing the folding of this kinetically trapped structure have remained elusive. Here, we integrated extensive molecular dynamics simulations and deep learning to elucidate the de novo folding mechanism of 20 lasso peptides lacking secondary post-translational modifications. We constructed Multi-Ensemble Markov Models for each lasso peptide and uncovered a consistent uphill folding landscape with spontaneous folding probabilities below 0.8%. Loop stability strongly correlated with folding propensity. Both simulations and experiments suggested that enhancing loop β-hairpin formation promotes folding of microcin J25, the well-studied lasso peptide extensively characterized as an in vitro model. This was confirmed by in silico loop-swap chimeras: grafting the microcin J25 loop onto the structurally similar klebsidin conferred prefolded stability. Leveraging Variational AutoEncoder-based pathway clustering, we resolved distinct pathway channels and representative folding pathways, further supporting this conclusion from a kinetic perspective. Additionally, a substantial entropy penalty was found to oppose lasso peptide folding. Simulations mimicking enzymatic spatial confinement reduced this penalty and stabilized the prefolded state. Together, these findings establish representative folding models and fundamental thermodynamic and kinetic principles which may be applied toward the rational engineering of lasso peptides.

title: A spatiotemporal scaffold in the human subiculum supports episodic memory and its enhancement through navigation training
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Episodic memory is grounded upon a spatiotemporal framework that binds discrete event details into a coherent structure. However, the neural mechanisms that construct this scaffold and their potential for memory enhancement through cognitive training have yet to be investigated. Here, we show a common spatiotemporal basis for human episodic memory across distinct populations, using a task in which participants remembered a sequence of objects placed in different locations in a virtual environment. Ultra-high-resolution 7-Tesla fMRI revealed that, within the hippocampal formation, the subiculum exhibited selective responses to spatiotemporal binding across sequences of spatial locations, which we attributed to its compressed, high-dimensional neural representational capacity compared to other hippocampal subfields. We then targeted this spatiotemporal framework through a two-week multi-target navigation training paradigm in a subset of participants, which led to transferable improvements in episodic memory. Critically, these behavioral gains were accompanied by enhanced retrieval-related activation and neural pattern reinstatement in the subiculum, measured using 3-Tesla fMRI. Together, these findings establish the subiculum as a core neural substrate for spatiotemporal scaffolding in human episodic memory and highlight its potential as a target for cognitive interventions.

title: Acid-Triggered Degradation of Diketopyrrolopyrrole Semiconducting Polymers via Alkyl Ester- and Carbohydrate-Containing Conjugation-Breaking Spacers
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of degradable semiconducting polymers is essential to reduce the large quantities of electronic waste anticipated from emerging organic electronic technologies. Yet degradable conductors and semiconductors remain underexplored relative to degradable substrates and dielectric materials, largely because of the challenge of balancing controlled degradability with the charge transport required for functional devices. In this work, a series of four diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based semiconducting polymers incorporating 10 and 20 mol % alkyl- and carbohydrate-based conjugation-breaking spacers (CBS) is reported. Each spacer combines a hydrolyzable ester linkage with a hydrophilic motif, distributed along the polymer backbone through random copolymerization to enable acid-triggered cleavage. Upon synthesis, the materials were characterized through a multimodal approach. Gel permeation chromatography revealed number-average molecular weights between 11 and 16 kg/mol, narrow optical band gaps were determined from the onset of the thin-film absorption, and atomic force microscopy revealed smooth surface morphologies across the series. Organic field-effect transistors prepared from the new polymers showed a decrease in hole mobility with rising CBS content, while remaining comparable to previously reported CBS-containing systems. Upon exposure to trifluoroacetic acid over several days, gel permeation chromatography confirmed a progressive decrease in molecular weight consistent with hydrolysis of the ester-containing spacers, whereas a fully conjugated DPP reference polymer remained intact under identical conditions. These results establish carbohydrate-based conjugation-breaking spacers as a new handle for backbone engineering, simultaneously modulating optoelectronic and morphological properties while imparting acid-triggered degradability, providing a design strategy toward degradable materials for transient organic electronics.

title: Photothermal Enhanced Droplet-Based Electricity Generator for Water Energy Harvesting at Subzero Temperature
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Droplet-based electricity generators (DEGs) can harness widely distributed water-droplet kinetic energy to generate electricity, but their applications in cold environments are severely limited by surface icing/frosting and residual droplets, which disrupt solid-liquid interfacial charge transfer and deteriorate electrical output. Here, we propose a photothermal-enhanced droplet-based electricity generator (PE-DEG) featuring a bifunctional dielectric layer consisting of the graphene-doped polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and fluorinated ethylene propylene (FEP). The bifunctional dielectric layer, benefiting from the high dielectric permittivity and photothermal performance of the graphene doping, endows both improved charge-storage capability and efficient solar-to-thermal conversion for surface temperature regulation. Consequently, the PE-DEG achieves an output voltage of 296 V at room temperature and maintains 188 V at –7 °C under 1 sun illumination. Under subzero operation, the output energy of the PE-DEG decreases by only 27.58%, markedly smaller than the 43.14% decrease observed for the conventional DEG. As a proof of concept, the PE-DEG can directly drive 186 LEDs and powers a thermohygrometer via capacitor charging. This study provides a materials-level strategy for maintaining high-performance droplet energy harvesting under cold environmental conditions.

title: Inflammation-Targeted Multifunctional Nanoparticles Remodel the Spinal Cord Injury Microenvironment to Promote Neurovascular Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Spinal cord injury (SCI) is characterized by interconnected inflammation, oxidative stress, vascular dysfunction, and impaired neural regeneration, while insufficient lesion-directed delivery further limits the efficacy of systemic therapy. Here, we developed macrophage membrane-camoufl11aged Sr-PDA/Fasudil/MnO2 nanoparticles (MM-NPs) that were designed to integrate inflammation-targeted delivery with complementary immunomodulatory, redox-regulating, and repair-supporting functions. Macrophage membrane camouflage reduced nonspecific phagocytic uptake, enhanced recognition of inflammatory endothelium, improved delivery in an in vitro endothelial barrier model, and increased lesion accumulation in vivo. The formulation provided sustained fasudil release and was designed to combine Rho-associated protein kinase (ROCK) inhibition with redox regulation and bioactive support. MM-NPs consequently attenuated microglial inflammatory activation and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation, improved endothelial migration and angiogenic responses, and alleviated inflammation-induced impairment of neural stem cell differentiation. In a rat SCI model, MM-NPs reduced lesion cavitation and fibrosis, improved the inflammatory microenvironment, enhanced vascular, axonal, and myelin-associated repair, and promoted neurological recovery. Transcriptomic profiling and quantitative spinal cord immunoblotting supported treatment-associated changes in ROCK-associated and NF-κB-related inflammatory signaling. Collectively, MM-NPs couple inflammation-targeted delivery with coordinated immune, redox, vascular, and neural regulation, providing a microenvironment-centered strategy for neurovascular repair after SCI.

title: Neural Estimation of Crystallographic Orientation from Rotating-Substrate RHEED with Limited Training Data: Application to CdTe Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We introduce a data-efficient neural-vision method to estimate the crystallographic orientation of a rotating substrate from reflection high-energy electron diffraction (RHEED) patterns during molecular beam epitaxy (MBE) growth. We combine single-frame azimuth predictions of a neural network with the known rotation kinematics in a physics-aware postprocessing step. This step detects the rotation direction and recovers a robust reference azimuth, replacing manual frame-by-frame inspection. Trained on RHEED patterns from only 15 independently grown CdTe samples, the model infers the crystallographic directions to within the 0.5° target for 95% of rotations. Under leave-one-structure-out evaluation on all 20 samples, the mean error is 0.18°. High accuracy stems from the postprocessing rather than from the network architecture. A 2D ResNet reaches the accuracy of a 3D ResNet benchmark trained on the same number of samples at approximately one tenth of the training cost. Our work delivers (i) a physics-constrained estimation procedure for rotating-substrate RHEED, applicable to any azimuth regressor that is unbiased over a rotation, (ii) an analysis of why few independently grown samples suffice, and (iii) a trained system validated for online orientation estimation during CdTe growth.
