Here, we employed pixel-wise spatial and spectral information from hyperspectral cathodoluminescence (HYP-CL) mapping to expose the SiH4 flow rate-mediated interfacial wetting/dewetting behavior of the SiNx nanomask that drastically affected the GaN nucleation kinetics at the SiNx/GaN interface. A low SiH4 flux induced wetting behavior, leading to a laterally extended SiNx nanomask, resulting in premature GaN island coalescence. Meanwhile, at a higher SiH4 flux, the observations are consistent with a wetting-to-dewetting behavioral transition, leading to aggregated SiNx clusters, resulting in vertically extended coalescence-free GaN pillars. Through this study, we unraveled the trade-off between cross-sectional film continuity and threading dislocation density suppression, which directly translates to the electrical performance. Also, we establish a design principle for nanomask engineering at semiconductor interfaces based on CL imaging for optimizing buffer layer design in high-voltage GaN-based devices.

title: Direct Inkjet Printing of Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
last_author: Louis C. P. M. de Smet
abstract: Abstract There is a growing need for gas and volatile organic compound (VOC) sensors in many areas, including air quality, safety monitoring, and (early) disease detection. VOC sensors can make use of affinity coatings to increase their sensitivity and selectivity. With their intrinsic high surface areas and chemically tunable pores, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are excellent candidates for the design and fabrication of such affinity coatings. However, precise, scalable, and easy deposition of such COF materials is proven to still be a challenge. In this study, we show the controlled deposition of COFs through direct inkjet printing for the first time, for which COFs are prepared as colloidal suspensions, serving as ready-to-use inks. We present a facile colloidal synthesis, leading to colloidal suspensions that are stable for months and which allow inkjet printing without any further processing. The COFs can be printed on gold as both isolated spots and as thin layers. The synthesis and printing conditions were carefully optimized to strike the balance between colloidal stability, printing robustness, and controlled drying. After exposure to saturated VOC environments, the printed layers show VOC desorption as monitored by infrared reflection absorption spectroscopy, not only confirming partial retention of the porous nature of the printed COF particles but also demonstrating the applicability of printed COF layers as affinity coatings on VOC sensors.

title: Graphene/MXene/Polydimethylsiloxane Composite Skin with Multiband Electromagnetic Absorption and Active/Passive Dual-Mode Infrared Camouflage
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The development of low-cost, highly reliable, and multispectral-compatible stealth materials remains challenging, necessitating ingenious microstructure design and a suitable multicomponent strategy. In this study, we fabricate graphene/polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and MXene-graphene/PDMS composite elastic films. The construction of porous architectures and multidimensional heterogeneous interfaces has enabled the realization of an integrated design that combines radar wave absorption with active and passive infrared thermal management. The superior microwave absorption performance exhibited by the elastic films is attributable to the electromagnetic wave loss mechanisms facilitated by extensive continuous heterogeneous interfaces, including appropriate impedance matching, abundant interface/dipole polarization, and multiple reflections and scattering. At a thickness of 2.5 mm, the G5T3P minimum reflection loss (RLmin) reaches as low as –48.84 dB, and at a thickness of 2 mm, the G8P effective absorption bandwidth (EAB) reaches 5.32 GHz. Concurrently, the intrinsic low infrared emissivity of MXene, combined with the porous framework, generates a powerful thermal camouflage effect. Within a broad temperature range of 100–300 °C, the material provides both stable passive infrared stealth and the capacity for active modulation of thermal infrared signals under an applied voltage of 10–50 V. This work offers a potential technical approach toward improving radar/IR compatibility for stealth materials.

title: Metal–Organic Framework-Derived Magnetic Nanoparticles Inducing Interfacial Polarization Enabling MXene-Based Composite Films with High-Efficiency Electromagnetic Interference Shielding
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With outstanding conductivity, tunable structure, and rich surface functional groups, two-dimensional (2D) MXene is extensively used for the electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding field. However, MXene suffers from self-stacking and secondary reflection pollution, which weakens the electromagnetic wave (EMW) attenuation performance. Herein, we introduced one-dimensional (1D) PPy nanotubes (NTs) and (FeO)0.198(MnO)0.802 (FMO) magnetic nanoparticles derived from FeMn-metal–organic frameworks into the MXene system. Furthermore, combined with K+-induced filtration and freeze-drying technology, MXene/PPy NTs/FMO (MPFMO) composite films with three-dimensional (3D) porous structures were successfully constructed, thereby achieving significantly enhanced EMI shielding performances. The introduction of conductive PPy NTs not only refines the 3D conductive architecture embedded within the composite film but also induces forming hydrogen bonding and supports adjacent MXene nanosheets to increase the mechanical properties. The abundant heterogeneous interfaces can generate interfacial polarization and promote EMW absorption, and the intrinsic magnetic loss of FMO can further attenuate EMWs. Profiting from multiple synergy mechanisms, the MPFMO porous composite film delivers a high EMI SE of 62.43 dB, an absorption loss ratio of 72.50%, and specific shielding effectiveness SSEt of 1.21 × 104 dB cm2 g–1 at a thickness of only 55 μm. Notably, the as-prepared composite membrane also demonstrates a superior thermal conductivity of 18.82 W m–1 K–1.

title: Interfacial Reorganization by Nonionic Surfactants Governs the Stability and Bioactivity of Exosomes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Exosomes are promising nanoscale agents that can serve both as efficient drug delivery carriers and as bioactive therapeutics with intrinsic biological functions. Yet their clinical translation is hindered by formulation-dependent instability and an incomplete understanding of excipient–membrane interactions. Here, we systematically and, to our knowledge, for the first time dissect how nonionic surfactants govern exosome stability, membrane organization, and bioactivity across sub- to supra-critical micelle concentration regimes. Using bovine exosomes as a model, we verify that exosomes in phosphate-buffered saline are intrinsically metastable, undergoing progressive interfacial reorganization and particle loss even at 4 °C. Surfactants exhibit distinct, structure-dependent effects: polysorbates (PS20, PS80) reduce hydrodynamic size but accelerate particle loss, whereas poloxamer 188 (P188) preserves both size and concentration. Membrane analysis shows that polysorbates increase lipid fluidity, potentially through interactions with the lipid bilayer. P188 may act through preferential surface association with limited effects on the measured lipid packing environment. Functionally, PS20 enhances cellular uptake at the expense of structural integrity, whereas P188 maintains vesicle integrity with moderate functional gain. Across multiple exosome sources, these trends are conserved, demonstrating the generality of the underlying mechanisms. Together, our results establish a mechanistic framework linking surfactant structure, concentration, and membrane interaction to both physicochemical stability and biological performance, providing actionable design principles for exosome formulations.

title: Resolving Coupled Cathode–Anode Failures in Li–S Batteries via Spin-State-Modulated Spinel Dual Interfaces
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lithium–sulfur (Li–S) batteries are promising candidates for next-generation energy storage due to their high theoretical specific energy. However, their practical applications are limited by kinetic mismatch between cathodic sulfur conversion and anodic lithium deposition, causing sluggish sulfur redox kinetics and heterogeneous Li growth. Here, we employ a homologous dual-interface CoMnFe@CNF architecture to reveal a site-differentiated interfacial regulation mechanism for synchronizing sulfur and lithium kinetics. Fe3+ incorporation triggers spin-state-dependent electronic reconstruction in the spinel lattice, generating distinct tetrahedral (Td) Co3+ and octahedral (Oh) Mn3+ centers. The reconstructed Td-Co3+ sites enhance polysulfide adsorption and facilitate sulfur redox kinetics. Meanwhile, Oh-Mn3+ centers regulate Li+ solvation and transport, enabling uniform Li deposition. This site-differentiated coordination establishes a cathode–anode kinetic synchronization mechanism, enabling Li–S full cells to retain 76.9% capacity after 400 cycles at 1 C. This work provides a spinel site-engineering strategy for rational regulation of coupled interfacial kinetics.

title: Colloidal Quantum Dot Photodetectors: From Nanocrystal Materials to Monolithically Integrated Imaging
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Colloidal quantum dot (CQD) photodetectors offer a promising, low-cost, solution-processed approach to infrared imaging. This review details their development, from controlling nanocrystal synthesis to integrating CQD photodiodes with silicon readout circuits. It focuses on five material platforms: lead and mercury chalcogenides, perovskite CQDs, heavy-metal-free silver chalcogenides and AgBiS2, and III–V CQDs such as InAs and InSb. The discussion covers device architectures that balance gain, noise, and speed, as well as the evolution from single pixels to complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor focal plane arrays and flexible wearable devices. The review concludes by examining key challenges, operational stability, the gain–noise–speed tradeoff, pixel yield, heavy-metal substitution, spectral extension, and defect passivation that will determine whether CQD imagers progress from experimental demos to commercial products.

title: Interfacially Compliant Li+-Ion Conductive Polymer Layer for Stabilizing Composite Cathode in Sulfide-Based All-Solid-State Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium batteries (ASSLBs) are promising next-generation energy storage systems owing to their high energy density and enhanced safety. However, their practical implementation is hindered by sluggish Li+ transport and oxidative degradation of sulfide solid electrolytes within the composite cathode, which progressively increase interfacial resistance during cycling. Here, we introduce an interfacially compliant and Li+-ion conductive polymer layer (ICPL), composed of poly(1,4-butylene adipate) (PBA) and lithium difluoro(oxalato)borate (LiDFOB), to simultaneously facilitate Li+ transport and stabilize the LiNi0.90Co0.05Mn0.05O2(NCM90)/Li6PS5Cl interface. The PBA matrix promotes the dissociation of LiDFOB while maintaining a viscous, amorphous state, thereby establishing intimate and conformal contact with Li6PS5Cl. Within the ICPL, the mobile Li+ provides additional ion-conduction pathways within the composite cathode, whereas DFOB– preferentially contributes to the formation of a robust B-rich interphase that mitigates the oxidative decomposition of Li6PS5Cl. This synergistic regulation of interfacial chemistry and Li+ transport suppresses impedance growth and enables stable cycling of ASSLBs employing NCM90 composite cathodes at 0.33 C. These findings demonstrate that coupling interfacial compliance with salt-mediated ion conduction and interphase chemistry provides an effective materials-design strategy for stabilizing high-energy sulfide-based ASSLBs.

title: Scalable Deposition Strategies for All-Inorganic Perovskite Thin Films via Ambient Slot-Die Coating
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract All-inorganic cesium lead halide perovskites, such as CsPbI3, exhibit excellent thermal stability and outstanding optoelectronic properties, making them highly attractive for next-generation photovoltaic and light-emitting applications. Despite these advantages, their practical implementation is hindered by intrinsic polymorphism triggering spontaneous phase transitions toward the non-photoactive yellow δ-phase, severely compromising device performance and long-term stability. To overcome these challenges, we deploy phase-stabilization strategies based on dimethylammonium iodide (DMAI) additive and mixed-halide I/Br compositional engineering to suppress undesired phase formation and enable reproducible, high-quality thin films. Beyond materials design, scalable fabrication remains a critical requirement for industrial adoption. Here, we demonstrate the deposition of CsPbI3–xBrx perovskite films over large areas under ambient atmosphere using slot-die coating. Process optimization combined with effective surface passivation yields devices achieving a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.8% for slot-die-coated solar cells fabricated on 5 × 10 cm2 substrates (active area of 0.09 cm2). Furthermore, a five-cell minimodule with an active area of 3.65 cm2 delivers a PCE reaching 13.0%, underscoring the scalability and industrial relevance of the proposed approach. In addition, the device stability, assessed through light cycling tests, reveals promising durability, with devices maintaining 80% of their initial performance (T80) for more than 80 h.

title: Dry Surface Decontamination of Nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and Blister (HD) Chemical Warfare Agents Using TiO2/CeO2 Nanosorbents
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dry surface decontamination is a highly practical approach for mitigating chemical warfare agent (CWA) threats without generating liquid waste. Herein, we systematically investigate the dry decontamination performance of nanoscale TiO2, CeO2, and mixed TiO2/CeO2 (TiCe) sorbents against nerve (A-234, GF, GD) and blister (HD) agents. Materials characterization confirms that mixing Ti and Ce shifts the microstructure into a highly open, mesoporous network, significantly expanding the total pore volume to 1.01 cm3/g. In dry batch experiments, all nanosorbents achieved rapid, complete depletion of parent extractable G-agents within 10 min, while the Novichok agent A-234 was reduced to <4% within 10 min, exhibiting comparable performance under both ambient daylight and complete darkness. To the best of our knowledge, this work represents the first demonstration of fully dry Novichok detoxification using metal oxide-based sorbents. Blister agent HD underwent slower degradation, achieving near-complete depletion (with <3% residual) after 480 min. GC–MS analysis confirmed that depletion is driven by safe hydrolytic pathways yielding low-toxicity derivatives, without hazardous oxidation byproducts. When applied to contaminated ceramic tiles, the dry powders successfully transferred and removed all parent CWAs to levels undetectable by GC–FID and GC–MS in both immediate and aged scenarios, except for A-234 on CeO2 (3.7% residue). These findings demonstrate that practical dry surface decontamination is governed by rapid mechanical transfer followed by intra-sorbent degradation. Furthermore, the successful up-scaling of the nanoporous TiO2 synthesis to a kilo-lab scale highlights the straightforward scalability of these materials for real-world applications on delicate equipment.

title: Interface Engineering of the Insulator to Metal Transition in V2O3 Thin Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Vanadium sesquioxide (V2O3) is a strongly correlated oxide that presents an insulator-to-metal transition (IMT) at a critical temperature (Tc) of about 160 K. In this work, we present a systematic control of Tc and resistance ratio across the IMT of sputtered V2O3 thin films by interface engineering. Implementing a pregrown nanometer-thick V2O3 buffer layer allows tuning of Tc over a 20 K range toward higher temperatures. Extensive state-of-the-art structural analysis, including X-ray diffraction and high-resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy, shows that the Tc shift is primarily associated with modulated strain at the film/substrate interface. Furthermore, incorporating nitrogen during buffer layer growth continuously reduces the resistance of the insulating phase, providing a straightforward method to tune the IMT on–off ratio. Engineered films show enhanced functionalities, including a reduction in resistive-switching threshold power and stable self-spiking oscillations. Our results show that a two-step deposition of V2O3 films offers a robust and practical pathway to energy efficiency and scalability in neuromorphic and resistive-switching applications.

title: Vertically aligned dual-channel metal-organic framework nanosheet membranes for gas separation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The nanostructure of two-dimensional (2D) membranes is crucial for their separation performance. However, in conventional 2D membranes, guest species unavoidably permeate through tortuous pathways, resulting in effective transport lengths that are orders of magnitude greater than the membrane thickness. Here, we propose vertically aligned metal-organic framework (MOF) nanosheet membranes featuring bimodal porosity: intrinsic lateral pores within the MOF nanosheets and interlamellar pores between them, forming an ultralow-tortuosity, dual-sieving channel system for efficient gas separation. Despite their relatively large thickness, the resulting MOF nanosheet membranes exhibit a high H2 permeance of 16673 GPU (up to an order of magnitude higher than the reported average) along with an H2/CO2 separation selectivity of 325 under standardized atmospheric Wicke-Kallenbach conditions (zero transmembrane partial pressure difference). This work not only provides a promising membrane platform for H2/CO2 separation but also offers an alternative strategy for constructing next-generation molecular sieve membranes.

title: First experimental observation of ‘Staircase’ high confinement mode in tokamak plasma
abstract: In magnetically confined nuclear fusion, the achievement of ignition necessitates the tokamak plasma in a high confinement state known as H-mode. A major challenge encountered in the standard H-mode is the abrupt collapse of its ultrathin edge layer. Here, we report a first experimental demonstration that a stable H-mode can be sustained by a staircase plasma profile. The basic physical picture is: by staircasing the plasma profile, the potential free energy stored in one single large edge layer is distributed into multiple mesoscale layers throughout the entire plasma volume. Consequently, the large scale edge collapse is converted into small scale desynchronized fluctuations, effectively reducing the risk of violent relaxation event. This finding uncovers a new benign high confinement regime of the tokamak plasma.

title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Friction at solid-liquid interfaces is typically interpreted through classical contact mechanics, but molecular origins of gas-bubble friction in aqueous environments remain elusive. Here we report the direct quantification of gas-bubble friction at solid surfaces using atomic force microscopy with nanonewton resolution. We show that bubbles enter a contact-line friction regime only after film-mediated attachment, with static and kinetic responses that reflect contact-line pinning and sliding. On octadecyltrichlorosilane-grafted substrates, friction varies non-monotonically with surface hydrophobicity, peaking at intermediate hydrophobicity due to enhanced chemical heterogeneity. Surface chemistry and nanostructure further regulate energy dissipation, with relatively low friction on uniformly rough polydimethylsiloxane-grafted surfaces. Oxygen bubbles generate higher friction than air, nitrogen and carbon dioxide bubbles, as supported by molecular dynamics simulations that implicate gas-specific intermolecular interactions in contact-line dissipation. These findings provide molecular-level insight into gas-bubble friction, with implications for friction-tunable interfaces in catalysis, microfluidics, and medical applications.

title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BOx catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The oxidative dehydrogenation of propane offers a promising route to propylene, but developing low-temperature catalysts that simultaneously achieve high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a Co@BOx inverse catalyst featuring engineered defects localized at face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter. Using an oxidative atmosphere-induced exsolution strategy, we continuously tune the face-centered cubic/hexagonal close-packed phase ratio, maximizing the density of stacking faults at a 1:1 phase ratio. Catalytic activity exhibits a strong positive correlation with stacking fault density, with the optimal CoF/H-1.0@BOx catalyst achieving 32% propane conversion and 83% olefin selectivity at 450 °C—5.1 times that of pristine cobalt boride. Density functional theory reveals that stacking faults modulate Co atomic spacing, weakening the excessively strong BOx-Co interfacial interaction. In situ spectroscopy demonstrates that maximized stacking faults strengthen O-H bonds in surface boron hydroxyl species and optimize radical initiation kinetics. This work establishes subsurface defect engineering as a potential strategy to enhance oxide overlayer reactivity in inverse catalytic systems.

title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metal fuels are central to energetic materials because of their high energy density and intense heat-release capability. However, early-stage formation of passivating oxide shells severely restricts oxygen diffusion, resulting in incomplete oxidation and limited energy utilization. Here, we report a Ce-assisted microstructure design strategy to overcome this long-standing diffusion barrier by constructing three-dimensional oxygen-diffusion scaffolds within aluminum-based fuels through trace cerium addition. Rapidly solidified Al–xCe powders develop an interconnected Al11Ce3 network, which subdivides the Al matrix into fine domains. During heating and combustion, this Al11Ce3 network is preferentially oxidized into a CeO2-x/CeO2-containing scaffold before extensive Al oxidation, thereby providing continuous oxygen-transport pathways into the particle interior. As a result, Al–xCe alloy powders exhibit shorter ignition delay, faster flame propagation, shorter combustion duration, and more complete oxidation than pure Al. This work establishes a general and scalable design principle for enhancing metal-fuel combustion through rare-earth-enabled oxygen-diffusion networks.

title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: The construction of atomically precise heterogeneous catalysts that integrate multiple distinct active sites into a synergistic architecture is highly attractive but challenging. Here, we report an Au39(PPhpy2)2(R1C ≡ C)19 (PPhpy2 = 2,2’-(phenylphosphanediyl) dipyridine, R1C ≡ CH = 4-ethynyl-α, α, α-trifluorotoluene) nanocluster. The heteroatoms (such as nitrogen) were introduced to modulate the local coordination environment and construct asymmetric coordination units on the surface of Au39 nanoclusters. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that, in addition to the symmetric R1C ≡ C-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif, Au39 features two asymmetric pyN-Au-C ≡ CR1 coordination motifs on the surface. Au39/XC-72 delivers 96.6% conversion of benzyl alcohol with 94.4% selectivity for benzaldehyde under mild conditions (40 °C, air). Mechanistic studies show that the pyN-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif facilitates O2 adsorption and activation, whereas the R1C ≡ C-Au-C ≡ CR1 motif adsorbs benzyl alcohol. The exceptional catalytic performance stems from the synergy between adjacent, functionally distinct Au sites, enabled by the asymmetric coordination strategy. This study highlights the critical role of asymmetric coordination protocols in synergistic dual-site catalysis for aerobic oxidation, providing new ideas for the rational design of synergistic catalysts.

title: Atom-level pinning effect reinforced electrooxidative coupling of anilines into azos
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Electrosynthesis of azo compounds via aniline oxidation represents a sustainable alternative to conventional methods, yet its efficiency is largely limited by sequential N–H dehydrogenation and N–N self-coupling steps. Herein, a single-atom Ba-doped nickel hydroxide (C-Ba1Ni1-x(OH)2) with an atom-level pinning effect is engineered to tailor a robust carbonate-functionalized interface and a spatially favorable Ni–O–Ni motif for N–H dehydrogenation and N–N coupling of aniline, respectively. The C-Ba1Ni1-x(OH)2 achieves electrooxidative coupling of various anilines, with up to 95.8% yield and 98.2% Faradaic efficiency for azos, along with good tolerance. Mechanistic investigations elucidate that carbonate bound on Ba single-atom weakens O/N–H interaction to increase their H removability that promotes adjacent Ni2+–OH reconstruction to generate active Ni3+–O species and bolsters N–H dehydrogenation of aniline (Ph-NH2), favoring *Ph-N intermediate generation. Further, single-atom Ba compresses the neighboring Ni–O–Ni distance to spatially favor *Ph-N self-coupling, overall facilitating azo electrosynthesis. This atomic-level strain engineering delivers a generalizable paradigm to construct self-adaptive electrodes for multi-step electrochemical transformations.

title: Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ3-iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: While 2- and 4-aryloxypyridines are ubiquitous in pharmaceutical molecules, efficient synthetic strategies—especially for synthesizing scaffolds with diverse multiple substituents on the pyridine core—remain limited. Here we show a hook-and-slide strategy for constructing these scaffolds, involving the in-situ generation of pyridonyl(aryl)iodonium salts from pyridones and Koser’s reagent (hook, C3 selectivity), followed by an iodine-to-oxygen aryl migration (slide, O selectivity). Such newly designed iodonium salts feature dual vicinal nucleophilic sites, and we demonstrate that using C2 − H imidazolium ionic liquids can exclusively transfer the aryl group to the strategic O site. This approach is transition-metal-free, scalable, and applicable to substrates with diverse electronic and steric properties or complex structures. Importantly, the resulting products retain −I and −NH2 handles that are amenable to downstream derivatizations, enabling extensive exploration of previously inaccessible chemical space. The utility of this approach is further demonstrated through the concise synthesis of multiple pharmaceutical intermediates and a CRF1 antagonist, CP-376395.

title: Droplet-Assisted Growth of Re-Entrant Micro-Mushroom Surfaces with Switchable Superhydrophobicity and Adhesive Resistance
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nature-inspired designs for surface micro- and nanostructures have long attracted attention for their potential multifunctionality. This study introduces a mushroom-shaped silicone re-entrant structure achieved through a one-step, in-situ dynamic Droplet-Assisted Growth and Shaping strategy. The unique shape and multicomponent hybrid properties of the inert rod base and chemically modifiable spherical head of these silicone micro-mushrooms (SMMs) provide exceptional surface wetting and adhesion characteristics. The engineered single-scale rough surface exhibits the remarkable rose petal effect, featuring a water contact angle exceeding 150° and demonstrating extraordinary water adhesion. The wetting states of these surfaces can be easily altered through O2-plasma treatment with the reconstruction of secondary and tertiary hierarchical nanostructures. This approach also effectively converts petal-effect surfaces into lotus-effect surfaces, significantly enhancing their self-cleaning performance. Furthermore, the SMM coatings display extremely low adhesion to various adhesives, including tapes, hot glue, and all-purpose adhesives, with pull-off forces nearing 0. This characteristic ensures a smooth detachment from sticky surfaces. The durability of the SMM structures is noteworthy, as they maintain their morphology even after 1,000 loop tack tests and can endure 8.7 MPa compression and 500 cycles of linear abrasion on sticky surfaces.

title: Rapid and selective metal-free O2 reduction to H2O2 using a molecular CpN3 electrocatalyst
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a commodity chemical used broadly in the industrial sector that heavily relies on the 80+-year-old anthraquinone process, requiring significant energy input in combination with precious metal-catalyzed hydrogenation. We describe a metal-free molecular cyclopentadiene-iminium electrocatalyst for producing H2O2 under ambient conditions with high Faradaic efficiency (> 99%) and turnover frequency up to 104 s−1, surpassing some of the most active transition-metal-based molecular catalyst systems. One-electron reduction of the dication [CpN3H]2+ generates a radical cation [CpN3H]+• that becomes a potent hydrogen atom (H•) donor to O2, operating through an unusual radical-rebound mechanism to form a key hydroperoxyl intermediate ([CpN3OOH]+•). This proposed pathway is rigorously supported by cutting-edge computational and experimental mechanistic analyses. Overall, this work demonstrates an innovative and sustainable molecular approach to furnish a valuable commodity chemical through an electrically driven process without the need for transition metals.

title: Chiral SERS and photochemistry via collective hotspot asymmetry in metasurface-templated gold networks with disordered nanoscale porosity
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Chiral molecules interact with light so weakly that discriminating enantiomers or driving enantioselective chemistry by using optical approaches requires intense circularly polarised lasers or complex resonant structures. Here we combine a geometrically disordered electrodeposited network with a lithographic chiral template resembling the shape of a shuriken. The resulting substrate generates superchiral fields that neither individual component produces. The mechanism underlying this anomalous response arises from two distinct effects: first, the shuriken structures generate substantial intrinsic optical chirality; second, the nanoporous network adds densely distributed plasmonic hotspots and an interference cross-term, which augments the local chirality even more prominently. This chiral plasmonic nanoporous network achieves not only ultrasensitive chiral detection by reaching the attomole range, but also introduces enantiospecific photochemical reactivity on a single substrate under continuous-wave linearly polarised light. Raman asymmetries approach the theoretical maximum ( ≈ 2), while enantiomeric excesses exceed 25%. Finally, a six-order-of-magnitude enhancement over conventional Raman optical activity was calculated.

title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Artificial intelligence for combinatorial optimization depends on high-quality, structured training data, yet transforming ambiguous natural-language descriptions into precise, executable formal models remains a major bottleneck, traditionally requiring extensive manual effort and domain expertise. We develop CPAM-LLM, an automated constraint-programming modeling framework based on large language models that converts unstructured problem specifications into validated and executable formal models. The framework integrates retrieval-augmented generation grounded in formal concept analysis for structural validation, chaos-mapping-based data augmentation to enhance cross-domain generalization, and dynamic constraint adaptation to accommodate evolving problem settings. We demonstrate its effectiveness across five scenarios, including DNA sequence design, reconfigurable energy storage systems, and unmanned vehicle logistics. The results show that the framework can automate the data-to-model pipeline while adapting reliably to changing requirements, providing a practical approach to automated data formalization and indicating the importance of accessible, high-quality structured data for reliable downstream artificial intelligence applications.

title: Atomically ordered few-layer molybdenum boride MBenes for enhanced electromagnetic response
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal borides (MBenes), boride analogues of MXenes, combine layered frameworks with tunable surface chemistry, yet high-quality MBenes remain difficult to access. Existing methods for preparing MBenes often suffer from incomplete dealumination, Mo2AlB2 intermediate-phase formation, multilayer restacking, or Mo vacancies. Here, we report a Lewis-acid molten-salt route that converts MoAlB into few-layer MoB MBene nanosheets with an atomically ordered Mo−B framework and a low density of Mo vacancies. Comparative thermodynamic calculations and control experiments with ZnCl2, ZnBr2, ZnF2, and ZnS identify molten ZnBr2 as the preferred etchant for redox-driven Al extraction and delamination. Temperature-dependent free-energy analysis and Mo−Al−B ternary isothermal sections further define 700 °C as a processing window that suppresses Mo2AlB2 formation and promotes direct conversion from MoAlB to MoB MBene. Selective Al extraction from MoAlB produces few-layer MoB MBene, retaining an ordered Mo−B framework while inducing b-axis contraction, strengthened Mo−B covalency, and enhanced electron localization. Together with O/OH and Br surface terminations, these structural and electronic features promote multiple polarizations and enable an effective absorption bandwidth of 8.7 GHz at 2.1 mm. This theory-informed molten-salt etching strategy expands redox-mediated MBene synthesis and connects atomically ordered few-layer MoB MBene with electromagnetic functionality.

title: Performance and damage mechanisms of dispersion-strengthened tungsten under H-mode plasma in DIII-D
abstract: Dispersion strengthened tungsten (DSW) alloys are promising materials for plasma facing components, displaying improved mechanical properties and microstructure stability compared to pure tungsten. In this work, the performance of DSW reinforced with 1 wt% transition-metal carbide (TaC, TiC, or ZrC) has been examined under H-mode plasma in the DIII-D tokamak. DSW samples were mounted both flush with the divertor floor and at a 10 angle towards the incoming plasma fluxes to further increase the heat and particle loading. To simulate the impact of prolonged tokamak operation, similar plasma exposures were repeated on two additional sets of DSW samples: one set pre-implanted with 10 m helium, and another set heated in-situ to an additional 500 C. Flush mounted samples exhibited good surface stability, with no evidence of melting or cracking regardless of composition or treatment. Carbon redeposition was observed on most samples, likely due to the graphite environment of DIII-D. Under coupled thermal loading and helium implantation, surface nanostructuring developed in some DSW samples; however, DSW containing tantalum dispersion phases showed strong resistance to such surface modification. In contrast, obvious surface melting was observed on 10 angled samples containing TaC and ZrC dispersoids, likely associated with dispersoid oxidation during fabrication, which reduced thermal conductivity and promoted elevated surface temperatures during plasma exposure. The grain morphology of DSW containing TiC remained largely unchanged, although near-surface dispersoids on the angled TiC sample were missing after plasma exposure. The loss is associated with oxidation of the dispersoids during fabrication, followed by sublimation during plasma exposure. Through systematic comparison of DSW performance under H mode plasma conditions, this study identifies key degradation mechanisms and highlights strategies to improve the performance of DSW as plasma facing materials.

title: Collaborative multi-objective dispatch of cascade hydro-wind-solar systems based on adaptive density reshaping evolutionary algorithm
Asymmetric Amyloid Cross-Seeding Beyond “Like-Seeds-Like”
abstract: Abstract Amyloid cross-seeding has often been viewed as a “like-seeds-like” extension of homologous nucleation, in which structurally similar amyloid proteins reciprocally accelerate assembly through a shared cross-β architecture. Increasing evidence instead reveals frequent asymmetry: A→B and B→A can differ in rate, mechanism, structural outcome, and biological consequence, and may change with seed state, fibril polymorph, or microenvironment. Here, we propose that productive cross-seeding is governed by directionally selective compatibility rather than generic β-sheet similarity. We examine six mechanistic origins of asymmetry: conformational selection and population shift, fibril-end templating, dock-and-lock kinetic gating, lateral-face recognition, surface-catalyzed secondary nucleation, and coaggregation coupled to strain selection. We integrate kinetic, structural, cellular, animal, and human evidence, emphasizing that bulk aggregation measurements alone cannot distinguish templated elongation from secondary nucleation, adsorption, sequestration, coaggregation, or strain conversion. We further discuss how heterotypic interfaces reshape fibril polymorphism and disease relevance, and assess emerging molecular-simulation and machine-learning approaches for predicting directional cross-seeding. This mechanism-centered framework provides a basis for understanding mixed amyloid pathologies and for developing strategies to block, redirect, or exploit heterotypic propagation in disease.

title: Interpretable day-ahead sister interval forecasting of distributed photovoltaic power under generalized weather scenarios
Quaternary carbon–guided carbocation cascade rearrangement to enantioenriched polycycles
abstract: Polycyclic frameworks are prevalent in natural products and bioactive molecules, yet their efficient enantioselective synthesis remains a longstanding challenge. Carbocation cascade cyclization is a textbook reaction that has transformed the synthesis of fused polycycles, but extending this strategy to bridged architectures requires precise control over highly reactive carbocation intermediates while overcoming the intrinsic energetic barrier of transannular cyclization. Herein, we report a quaternary-carbon-guided carbocation cascade rearrangement platform that enables enantioselective and divergent assembly of complex polycyclic architectures from readily available substrates. An enantioenriched quaternary center, installed via transition-metal-catalyzed allylation, serves as a temporary structural linchpin in an acid-triggered cationic cascade rearrangement process, forming multiple bonds and chiral centers in a single step. In combination with pre-embedded quaternary centers, this strategy provides bicyclic and bridged polycyclic frameworks bearing multiple stereocenters with high enantioselectivity.

title: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination
abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

title: Piezocatalytic Sulfonation Enables Nongenetic Competition Therapy for Colorectal Cancer
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Irreversible post-translational modifications provide a potential means to impose persistent changes in protein function, yet their controlled generation inside living cells remains challenging. Here, we develop an ultrasound-responsive potassium sodium niobate–gold (KNN@Au) piezoelectric nanoheterojunction functionalized with hyaluronic acid (KNN@Au-HA) to enable in situ terminal protein sulfonation. Under ultrasound excitation, the dynamic modulation of KNN polarization generates a piezo-potential that facilitates interfacial charge separation and electron transfer, promoting the single-electron reduction of O2 to •O2–. Meanwhile, Au–S coordination positions thiol substrates in close proximity to the catalytic surface, facilitating the subsequent multistep oxidation of cysteine thiols to the terminal −SO3H state. Using this platform, we identify ribosomal protein RPL32 as a functionally relevant sulfonation target and resolve sulfonation at Cys96 by mass spectrometry. This modification disrupts ribosomal proteostasis, induces NRF2 nuclear translocation and stress signaling, and converts colorectal cancer cells into a competitive “loser” state that undergoes neighbor-dependent apoptotic elimination. In HCT116 xenograft-bearing mice, ultrasound-activated KNN@Au-HA suppresses colorectal tumor growth; analysis of patient-derived single-cell transcriptomic data reveals RPL32 upregulation as a hallmark of the malignant “winner” state, establishing a functional match between this competition therapy and colorectal cancer. Together, these findings demonstrate that piezocatalytic protein modification can chemically reprogram cellular competitive fitness without genome editing, providing a proof of concept for nongenetic competition therapy against cancer.

title: 1,8-Azulenedicarboxylic Imides: Excited-State Properties and Catalytic Activity of a Nonalternant π-System
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Imide-functionalized polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) represent an important class of π-conjugated molecules; however, their nonalternant isomers remain largely unexplored. Herein, we report the synthesis and investigation of the structural, photophysical, and excited-state properties of 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides as nonalternant isomers of 1,8-naphthalimides. These compounds retain the characteristic photophysics of the azulene framework, including near-infrared (NIR) absorption and anti-Kasha emission, while substitution at the imide nitrogen enables modulation of their excited-state electronic structures. QD-NEVPT2 calculations identified an S2–T1 pair with relatively large SOC and LE-to-CT character, suggesting a plausible ISC pathway associated with the observed singlet-oxygen photosensitization. Consequently, 1,8-azulenedicarboxylic imides function as an effective visible-light photocatalyst for the α-cyanation of secondary and tertiary amines. These findings demonstrate that the present nonalternant molecular design provides a strategy for tuning excited-state properties by modulating locally excited and charge-transfer states in imide chromophores.

title: A Unified Asymmetric Approach to Tetracyclic Diterpenoids via Ring Reconstruction Strategy
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Tetracyclic diterpenoids exhibit intricate densely fused and bridged polycyclic architectures and diverse biological profiles, yet their collective asymmetric synthesis from a unified precursor remains a formidable challenge due to immense topological barriers between distinct scaffolds. Herein, we report a divergent asymmetric synthesis of the tetracyclic diterpenoid family driven by a “ring reconstruction” strategy. Commencing with a platinum-catalyzed diboration/tandem allylation to establish the initial stereocenters, we assemble a highly oxidized ent-kaurane central hub via an orchestrated sequence featuring hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) and Johnson–Claisen rearrangement. Leveraging this platform, we deploy tailored radical and photochemical skeletal editing to overcome inherent topological constraints. This enables the divergent remodeling of the ent-kaurane core into an array of complex architectures, including ent-atisane, ent-beyerane, jungermannenone, and ent-aphidicolane frameworks. This unified strategy provides an efficient route to complex polycyclic natural products and highlights the power of skeletal editing for rapidly expanding chemical space.

title: 8-Oxoguanine Is the Major Product of the Reaction of Guanine Radical Cations with •NO2: A Spin-Orchestrated, Anisotropic Reaction Landscape and Its Biological Implications
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Formation of guanine radical cations (G•+) represents a hallmark DNA lesion produced by ionizing radiation and one-electron oxidation processes. •NO2, a reactive nitrogen species in living systems, drives nitrative and oxidative damage linked to mutagenesis and inflammation. Herein, we delineate spin-orchestrated interactions between •NO2 and radical cations of 2′-deoxyguanosine (dGuo•+) and its model compound 9-methylguanine (9MG•+) to probe synergistic pathways that exacerbate guanine nucleobase and nucleoside damage. Kinetic energy-resolved reaction coupled with mass spectrometric measurements revealed distinct pathways governing regioselective nitrite- and nitro-additions, adduct decomposition, and charge transfer. Direct dynamics simulations and potential energy surface analyses of the 9MG•+ + •NO2 model system, using spin-projected and time-dependent DFT, CCSD(T), and CASPT2 theories, characterized reaction mechanisms, thermodynamics, and kinetics arising from anisotropic interactions within open-shell 1,OS[G•+(↑)···(↓)•NO2] and 3[G•+(↑)···(↑)•NO2]. Through radical combination, the reaction system advances through multiple excited electronic and vibrational manifolds while preserving spin states (no intersystem crossing); only singlet states are open to chemical transformations. •NO2 markedly amplifies the lesion of guanine radicals by promoting sequential electron and H loss, producing 8-oxoguanine in neutral, radical cation, and doubly oxidized forms, along with release of •NO, NO+, and HNO. These pathways proceed through nitrite addition rather than guanine nitration, and HNO forms through •NO-mediated hydrogen abstraction via both conventional and roaming mechanisms. The studies identified new routes to the 8-oxoguanine lesion that has been traditionally attributed to reactive oxygen species. The biological implications of •NO2-mediated damage to guanine radical cations are discussed.

title: A Three-Motif-Based One-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework as an Efficient Cathode Material for Stable Rechargeable Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Crystalline one-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (1D COFs) hold great promise for diverse applications; however, their synthesis remains challenging, as it requires simultaneous control over chain dimensionality and crystallization of polymeric chains that are intrinsically prone to entanglement. Here, we show that benzo[1,2-b:4,5-b′]difuran-2,6(3H,7H)-dione (BDFO), in the presence of isoquinoline, effectively compels the trifunctional monomer 2,4,6-tris(4-formylphenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TPFT) to polymerize as a V-shaped ditopic linker, affording 1D zigzag chains that stack in a staggered arrangement to form the crystalline porous framework (CityU-31). CityU-31 exhibits a rectangular nanowire morphology with well-defined lattice fringes, a narrow pore-size distribution of 1–2 nm, and a surface area of 185 m2 g–1. Importantly, the V-shaped connectivity leaves one formyl group at each TPFT unit unreacted, and these pendant aldehydes serve as built-in handles for postsynthetic functionalization. As a proof of concept, a third motif was covalently linked via Knoevenagel condensation, converting the aldehyde groups into cyano functionalities to yield CityU-31-CN. Endowed with the cyano-decorated 1D backbone, CityU-31-CN delivers an extended voltage window (0.8–3.5 V), a high capacity of 160 mAh g–1 at 0.1 A g–1, and outstanding cycling stability (>10,000 cycles). The intrinsic backbone reactivity of CityU-31 thus offers a versatile platform for postsynthetic modification, greatly expanding the application scope of crystalline 1D polymers.

title: Awakening Latent Diradicals to Enhance Antiferromagnetic Coupling between Localized Organic Spin Centers
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Connecting persistent radicals through π-conjugated linkers provides a promising route for developing organic magnetic systems. However, the simultaneous realization of localized addressable spins and thermally robust antiferromagnetic (AFM) coupling remains challenging. Conventional approaches based on quinoidal versus aromatic resonance forms impose electronic constraints that limit access to this regime. Here, we introduce a molecular design principle in which the latent open-shell character of selected heterocyclic linkers is activated to significantly strengthen AFM interactions between localized radical centers. First-principles calculations reveal that this enhancement: i) originates from increased linker spin polarization acting synergistically with partial quinoidalization, and ii) is robust across a series of diradicals combining an expandable family of linkers with representative persistent radicals. We identify diradicals displaying pronounced open-shell character with unusually large singlet–triplet energy gaps typically associated with closed-shell systems. Extending this concept to two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks, we further show that our approach translates from discrete molecules to strongly AFM materials.

title: Terahertz Stimulation Enhances Nanopore Capture Rate via Mitigating Voltage-Induced Water Compression
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nanopore sensing has emerged as a powerful tool for proteomic analysis, yet controlling molecular translocation, particularly for neutral residues, remains a significant challenge. Here, we use all-atom molecular dynamics simulations to investigate the translocation of electrically neutral peptides and amino acids, and to elucidate how nanoslit geometry and applied voltage jointly regulate the process from both kinetic and thermodynamic perspectives. As the applied voltage increases from 0 to 1 V, the biomolecule capture time doubles, whereas the dwell time is reduced by half. Potential-of-mean-force calculations reveal a higher entry barrier and a lower exit barrier. Further analyses of solvent density and the corresponding bulk-equivalent pressure show that increasing the voltage or narrowing the nanoslit raises the density of the confined solution, generating a bulk-equivalent static-pressure differential that increases resistance to molecular entry while reducing resistance to exit. To relieve this voltage-induced compression, we apply an external terahertz (THz) electromagnetic stimulation, which effectively shortens the capture time by lowering the entry barrier from 48.49 to 38.76 kJ/mol. This study provides molecular-level insights into nanopore translocation and offers practical strategies to enhance molecular capture, potentially advancing nanopore proteomics and informing related applications. Notably, this computational research is the first to introduce THz stimulation for regulating nanopore translocation, offering a noncontact approach to mitigate water compression, as well as for active and reversible nanopore control.

title: Palladium-Catalyzed Enantioselective Oxidative Remote (4 + 1)-Cyclization of 1,6-Enynes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Herein, we report a palladium-catalyzed enantioselective oxidative remote (4 + 1) cyclization of 1,6-enynes using PhI(OPiv)2 as the oxidant. Both Z- and E-enynes are competent substrates, affording the same cyclopentane-fused lactones and lactams with high efficiency, and excellent enantioselectivity is achieved using chiral pyridinyl oxazoline ligands. These cyclopentane-fused lactones can be readily transformed to other chiral cyclopentane derivatives. Notably, the use of TFE as the solvent is critical for attaining high chemoselectivity and enantioselectivity. Density functional theory calculations reveal that unlike previous reports of asymmetric enyne cyclization, the enantioselectivity of this reaction is governed by cis-oxypalladation of the alkyne. The resulting vinyl-Pd(II) intermediate undergoes sequential alkene insertion, palladium migration, and oxidation steps. The generated terminal alkyl-Pd(IV) species then undergoes an SN2-type reductive elimination with the enol ester as the nucleophile, which accounts for the formation of the cyclopentane skeleton.

title: Enhancing Grignard Reactions via Anion Borrowing in Deep Eutectic/Organic Biphasic Media
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rational optimization of the Grignard reaction remains a considerable challenge for synthetic chemists. Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have emerged as powerful reaction media to enhance nucleophilic additions to unsaturated organic molecules. In this protocol, a solution of the Grignard in THF is added to the DES containing the substrate under vigorous stirring. In this study, we determine the underlying causes for this beneficial effect by combining ab initio molecular dynamics, QM/MM simulations, and enhanced sampling, using i-PrMgCl and acetophenone as reagents, THF as the organic solvent, and a 1:2 solution of choline chloride:glycerol as the DES. Our results demonstrate enhanced chemoselectivity for the Grignard addition over β-H transfer side reaction from the isopropyl group when in DES/THF. This enhanced selectivity stems from the formation of chlorinated dimagnesium entities at the DES interface. While the neutral Grignard species in neat THF kinetically favors β-H transfer, chloride enrichment from the DES renders both pathways kinetically competitive and markedly increases the thermodynamic preference for the addition product through enhanced intramolecular stabilizing interactions. This is in line with experimental evidence of increased selectivity in the presence of various halide salts. This mechanistic interpretation paves the way for the rational improvement of Grignard reagents, allowing an even broader application of these compounds in these nonconventional solvents.

title: Atomically Confined Structural Self-Compensation at Grain Boundaries in Ba-Based Layered Proton Conductors
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Ion transport and interfacial stability in oxide materials are strongly influenced by the electrostatics that develop at grain boundaries. In conventional ABO3-type perovskites, grain boundary resistance is well-explained by space-charge effects, in which a positively charged grain boundary core is compensated by the accumulation of negatively charged acceptor dopants. By contrast, the compensation mechanism in recently developed Ba-based layered perovskites has remained unclear. In this study, by directly resolving the grain boundary atomic structure of this material class, we identify a previously unrecognized, structurally confined charge-compensation mode. Using atomic-resolution imaging, spatially resolved electron energy-loss spectroscopy, density functional theory, Poisson–Cahn calculations, and impedance spectroscopy, we show that acceptor-doped BaZrO3 compensates its grain boundary through diffuse dopant segregation, whereas layered Ba2LuAlO5 and Ba5Er2Al2ZrO13, which possess intrinsically oxygen-deficient frameworks, instead form a BaLnO3-δ-type layer (Ln = lanthanide) immediately adjacent to the grain boundary core. Relative to the diffuse space-charge layer in BZY82, this atomically localized compensation confines the compensating charge to a single structural block, thereby lowering the electrostatic barrier and the grain boundary activation energy for proton transport. These findings establish spatially confined structural compensation as a key determinant of grain boundary charge balance in layered perovskites and provide a general design principle for engineering next-generation, high-performance Ba-based protonic electrolytes.

title: Molecular Origins of Lithium-Ion Transport in the Anionic Metal–Organic Framework SU-102
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Metal–organic framework (MOF) quasi-solid electrolytes offer chemically tunable environments for ion transport, but the molecular roles of framework coordination and confined solvent remain unclear. We combined solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (ssNMR) measurements with molecular dynamics simulations to determine the Li+ transport mechanism in propylene carbonate (PC)-filled SU-102. Variable-temperature direct- and cross-polarization 7Li ssNMR reveal two distinct Li+ populations with different local tumbling dynamics. Our simulations identified Zr-associated, linker-associated, and fully PC-solvated Li+ coordination environments. The most strongly stabilizing Li+ site is not necessarily the one that carries transport: Zr-associated sites bind Li+ most strongly but form a discontinuous network along the pore axis, whereas the weaker-binding linker sites form a continuous one. Linker-associated Li+ also shows faster site-persistence decay and the largest trial-weighted displacement, and linker-to-linker hopping is the most frequent classified event, followed by Zr-to-Zr hopping. Chemical color-diffusion nonequilibrium molecular dynamics yielded an ionic conductivity of 1.34 ± 0.48 mS cm–1 along the one-dimensional channels and negligible conductivity perpendicular to them, giving an orientational average of 0.45 ± 0.16 mS cm–1, in close agreement with experiment (0.52 mS cm–1). Together, our results indicate that PC-assisted hopping between linker sites contributes more strongly than vehicular diffusion of fully solvated ions, with confined PC retained in the coordination shell across these transfers. These findings identify the balance between ion–framework stabilization and facile site-to-site exchange as a key design principle for reticular quasi-solid electrolytes.

title: Directed Attachment of Catalysts into the Extended Environments of Soft Photoelectrodes for Hydrogen Evolution
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We present a detailed investigation of early stage photoelectrochemical deposition of platinum nanoparticle (Pt-NP) catalysts on semiconducting polymer platforms for the light-assisted hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) using electrochemical, spectroscopic, and microscopy characterization, combined with density functional theory (DFT) modeling. The photoactive junction─formed from a blend of donor (PTB7-Th) and acceptor (P(NDI2OD-T2)) polymers─exhibits HER efficiencies that increase exponentially with Pt-NP loading (ca. 8.0 × 101 to 2.5 × 104 ng/cm2) of highly faceted Pt-NPs. The blended heterojunction demonstrates acceptor enrichment of the near-surface region as the point of Pt deposition via progressive nucleation, at sites which we posit are the near-surface termini of “fast transport pathways” created within the PTB7-Th/P(NDI2OD-T2) blend film. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), for the lowest coverage Pt-NPs, combined with DFT modeling, suggests Pt–S interactions via the bithiophene groups in P(NDI2OD-T2) might dominate at the earliest stages of Pt deposition, while larger DFT-modeled 14- and 38-atom Pt clusters demonstrate Pt–C and Pt–O═C interactions on naphthalene diimide cores. Collectively, our findings suggest that submicron environments in soft photoelectrode materials function as integrated architectures, as expected, where charge creation requires well mixed domains, adjacent to domains optimized for charge transport. Photoelectrochemically deposited metals such as Pt-NPs decorate the most photoelectrochemically active near-surface regions, producing good HER efficiencies. Hierarchical assembly of such photoactive soft materials has the potential to provide a transformative framework for scalable energy conversion that extends beyond hydrogen evolution.

title: Author Correction: Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
