Precise regulation of iridium electronic state reversely stabilizes cobalt oxide for practical proton-exchange membrane electrolysis
abstract: Reducing iridium use without sacrificing activity and durability is a key challenge for proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis. This work shows that confining low-valent Ir within the Co3O4 lattice can electronically stabilize neighboring Co sites, suppressing support degradation and Ir loss. By linking Ir electronic state to catalyst stability, this study offers a general strategy for designing low-Ir, durable anodes for practical green hydrogen production.

title: Synergistic Integration of Materials and Design Strategies for Next‐Generation Stretchable Displays
abstract: ABSTRACT Stretchable displays rely on sophisticated integration enabled by materials engineering, structural strategies, and micro‐nano integration, encompassing stretchable substrates, conducting and semiconducting components. This review provides a focused discussion of recent technological advances. We highlight key innovations in stretchable electrodes, interconnects, emissive materials, transistor arrays, circuit layouts, and deformable substrates for their roles in improving electrical uniformity, mechanical resilience, and display performance. Additionally, we summarize the latest strategies for achieving stretchability, either by using intrinsically elastic electronic materials or by structurally engineering rigid components. We introduce emerging applications with substantial potential, including epidermal human‐machine interfaces, conformal biomedical monitoring and visualization, soft robotics with distributed optical feedback, and skin‐integrated augmented reality (AR)/virtual reality (VR) systems, to illustrate the transformative opportunities ahead for stretchable display technologies.

title: Trace‐Metal‐Assisted Flash Synthesis for Fast‐Charging Graphite Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Graphite has remained the dominant anode material in lithium–ion batteries (LIBs), powering portable electronics and electric vehicles (EVs). However, sluggish Li + diffusion kinetics in natural and synthetic graphite can severely limit charging rates. Overcoming this bottleneck requires the rational design of graphite architectures that enable rapid Li + transport in LIBs. Here, we disclose a trace‐metal‐assisted flash (TMF) process for the millisecond synthesis of catalytic flashed graphite (CFGr) with exceptionally fast‐charging capabilities. The TMF process induces in situ formation of trace nickel nanoclusters that catalyze ultrafast graphitization of amorphous carbon into highly ordered graphite within I D / I G of 0.09, with calculations yielding an interlayer bonding energy ( E b ) of −2.297 eV, while diffraction reveals an interlayer spacing (d 002 ) of 3.4 Å. These features enhance structural stability and Li + accessibility. Consequently, optimized CFGr achieves a high reversible capacity of 347.4 mAh g −1 at 0.25 C and retains 158.8 mAh g −1 at 15 C with 80% capacity retention after 1000 cycles, outperforming the rate and cyclability of both commercial graphite and graphite prepared by flash Joule heating. The TMF route can replace conventional energy‐intensive graphitization, reducing energy use and emissions by over 80% and lowering the production cost of premium fast‐charging synthetic graphite by ∼80% to only US$0.84 kg −1 . These findings establish a promising pathway to advance fast‐charging graphite anodes into next‐generation LIBs.

title: Bioinspired Molecular‐Scale Tape Interface Towards Ultrahigh‐Pixel‐Density Flexible Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Devices
abstract: ABSTRACT Flexible, high‐density integrated optoelectronics underpin emerging wearable information systems and human–machine interfaces. However, as pixel size decreases to a few micrometers, emission uniformity and performance of flexible light emitting diodes (LED) degrade severely due to microscale electrical and optical nonuniformity of electrodes especially after bending, hindering their potential applications. Inspired by fish scales, we propose a molecular‐scale tape interface as a transparent electrode for ultrahigh‐pixel‐density flexible LEDs. An atomically thin MXene layer, assembled via liquid–air interfacial assembly, conformally adheres to indium tin oxide through reversible hydrogen bonding and van der Waals coupling, enabling stress redistribution, crack bridging, and potential homogenization. This electrode enables flexible quantum‐dot LEDs with uniform micro‐area current and emission up to 25 400 ppi and a record external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.4%, maintaining performance after 3000 bending cycles. This biomimetic transparent‐electrode interfacial strategy unites mechanical flexibility with ultrahigh pixel density, advancing high‐density integrated optoelectronic architectures.

title: Influence of Local Curvature and Structural Chirality on Magnetic Spin Textures in Fe Thin‐Film Möbius Bands
abstract: ABSTRACT The Möbius band is a fascinating three‐dimensional (3D) architecture that exhibits a geometric chirality where left‐ and right‐handed twists cannot be interchanged via continuous rotation, along with a varying extrinsic curvature. Here, we demonstrate that spin textures in arrays of Fe magnetic Möbius structures are fundamentally governed by their geometric chirality and extrinsic curvature. Magnetic full‐field soft x‐ray transmission microscopy reveals that the unique geometry drives domain fragmentation into nontrivial arrangements in regions of maximal curvature, along with the formation of nontrivial vortex domains. Magnetometry and first‐order reversal curve measurements reveal a complex magnetization reversal process, as the lateral and vertical portions of the Möbius structures respond differently to in‐plane and out‐of‐plane applied fields. Micromagnetic simulations confirm a vortex state with geometry‐driven preferred circulation direction. The resulting spin textures propagate either clockwise or counterclockwise along the Möbius structures, depending on the direction of an in‐plane magnetic field applied along the primary bend of the structure. These geometric‐chirality‐driven effects are manifested in the experimentally captured evolution of the remanent magnetization. Our results demonstrate a new platform where curvature and real space topology of 3D nanostructures may be used as degrees of freedom to tailor spin textures.

title: Widespread marine mammal and seabird reductions are unlikely to benefit salmon due to indirect ecosystem effects
abstract: Pacific salmon are depleted due to anthropogenic impacts, and populations have failed to recover despite management interventions. Predation on salmon by pinnipeds and seabirds has been suggested as a barrier to recovery, leading to calls for predator culls by some. However, no studies have evaluated the whole-ecosystem impact of removing these predators nor estimated the direct and indirect effects of these culls on salmon. We use an end-to-end ecosystem model to assess the efficacy of widespread culls in marine environments. We find that culls are unlikely to benefit salmon due to the indirect food web effects of predator reduction and the low biomass of top predator groups. Instead, more abundant fish predators, northward-expanding competitors, and temperature-sensitive prey have larger effects on salmon in the ocean.

title: Electronic Spin States in Oxygen Reduction: From Identification Divergence to Mechanism Clarification
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) is a cornerstone process in clean‐energy technologies including fuel cells, metal–air batteries, and electrochemical hydrogen peroxide synthesis. Emerging evidence has established the electronic spin states of transition‐metal active centers as a critical descriptor that governs ORR activity and selectivity, yet present studies of the same metal center have reported divergent electronic spin states and ORR pathway selectivity. This review attempts to perform a comprehensive discussion about this divergence. The fundamentals of spin states are first introduced within the frameworks of crystal field theory and molecular orbital theory and the principal characterization techniques for spin states identification. Subsequently, the contradictory correlations between spin states and ORR selectivity reported in different catalytic systems are critically analyzed in terms of d ‐orbital occupancy and reaction kinetics. Furthermore, rationally regulating spin states strategies are elucidated to optimize ORR performance. Finally, key challenges and future research directions are outlined, emphasizing the need for in situ characterization, advanced theoretical modeling, and unambiguous identification of active sites. This review will furnish theoretical guidance for subsequent investigations of spin effects, and provide insights into extending spin state engineering to other small‐molecule electrocatalytic reactions.

title: Strong and Thermally Conductive Graphene‐Bamboo Nanocomposites by Topological Fiber‐Network Engineering Towards Intelligent Energy‐Efficient Floors
abstract: ABSTRACT Smart floor‐heating systems that integrate occupancy sensing with localized thermal regulation offer a promising route toward low‐carbon buildings, yet existing flooring materials cannot simultaneously provide robust mechanical properties and rapid heat delivery. Here, a topological fiber‐network engineering and thermorheology‐assisted assembly strategy is reported that enables continuous thermal‐transport and load‐bearing networks to coexist within a single material. Long bamboo fibers form a topologically entangled framework that simultaneously serves as a mechanically robust scaffold and a three‐dimensional template for graphene nanoplatelet assembly, while thermorheological phenol‐formaldehyde (PF) resin facilitates their rearrangement into ordered face‐to‐face configurations under low pressure. The resulting graphene–bamboo composites (GBC) exhibit metal‐level thermal conductivities of 12.8–116.7 W m − 1 K − 1 together with outstanding flexural strengths of 75–155 MPa, outperforming conventional flooring materials. When integrated into a pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating system, the composites enable rapid thermal homogenization and occupant‐responsive localized heating. Whole‐building simulations indicate that nationwide adoption of the composite in pressure‐sensing smart floor‐heating systems in China could reduce annual heating‐electricity consumption by up to ∼208 TWh, corresponding to a ∼37% reduction compared with conventional wood flooring. This work establishes the integration of topological fiber‐network engineering with thermorheology‐assisted assembly as a general strategy for overcoming the thermal–mechanical trade‐off in structural biomass composites and advancing energy‐efficient building materials.

title: Molecular Engineering of Redox Mediator for Accelerated Multi‐Electron Transfer Reactions in Lithium Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium–sulfur and lithium–oxygen batteries are highly attractive due to their ultrahigh theoretical energy densities, while their performance is severely constrained by sluggish multiphase reaction rates and limited reaction stability at the cathodes. The conventional solid‐phase catalysts suffer from small interfacial contact area and activity loss of active sites, while the mobile redox mediators (RMs) present a new paradigm for accelerating multi‐electron transfer pathways through a solution‐mediated electron transfer pathway. This review first discusses the critical rate‐limiting factors governing reaction rate at the cathode, and then systematically examines the latest advances in the molecular engineering of RMs for cathode catalysis from the viewpoint of redox potential, solubility, molecular size, and chemical stability. Following these points, we comprehensively analyze, from both thermodynamic and kinetic perspectives, how the molecular engineering of RMs affects the redox potential, solubility, stability, and so on. These characteristics strongly dictate the specific capacity and lifespan, elucidating key structure–activity relationships. Finally, we propose systemic strategies expanding beyond isolated liquid‐phase catalysis toward solid–liquid synergistic design and functionalized electrolyte/separator engineering.

title: Zero-shot de novo design of a metalloenzyme
abstract: De novo design of enzymes is a frontier challenge, requiring consideration of catalytic mechanism and optimization across biochemical and biophysical criteria. Here, we present dEVA (design by EVolutionary Algorithm), a multi-objective protein design method built on principles drawn from evolutionary biology. We apply dEVA to the zero-shot, de novo design of metalloenzymes by optimizing the coordination sphere of catalytic metals. We characterize a bi-zinc metalloenzyme that exhibits promiscuous hydrolytic activity towards both phosphomonoesters and phosphodiesters. This design achieves a rate enhancement ((k cat /K M )/k w ) of up to 3 x 10 13 relative to the uncatalyzed reaction, comparable to characterized natural phosphatases. Structural characterization via x-ray crystallography and absorption spectroscopy supports the design of a de novo active site. These results demonstrate that de novo enzymes can be designed without pre-specified motifs, natural templates, or evolutionary information.

title: Re‐Evaluating the Role of Water in Hexacyanoferrate Cathodes for Sodium and Potassium Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Hexacyanoferrates (HCFs) are among the most promising cathode materials for sodium‐ion and potassium‐ion batteries owing to their open three‐dimensional framework, high operating voltage, and fast alkali‐ion transport. As an unavoidable constituent of hexacyanoferrates (HCFs), water is intimately associated with crystal growth, vacancy formation, local coordination, and framework stability. Water has long been regarded primarily as a detrimental impurity in cathodes because it blocks ion transport, accelerates electrolyte decomposition, and promotes structural degradation. However, recent studies indicate that interstitial and coordinated water exhibit distinct binding strengths, mobilities, and electrochemical reactivities, rendering their roles far more complex than can be described by total water content alone. In this Review, we re‐evaluate the role of water in HCF cathodes by redefining it from a structural impurity to a functional component. We discuss how water governs crystal structure, electronic structure, ion transport, interfacial reactions, and electrochemical performance. We further summarize advanced characterization techniques, particularly neutron methods, for probing the dynamic behavior of water molecules, and highlight regulation strategies. This work establishes a unified framework linking water with crystal, electronic structure, and electrochemical behavior, providing guidance for the rational design of high‐performance HCF cathodes.

title: Edge computing and interoperability in energy consumption prediction for smart grids
Gaining the upper hand
Tropical forcing and high-latitude ice dynamics: dual engines of millennial climate variability
Mineralogical evidence for hydrous carbonaceous chondrite relics in Chang’e-6 regolith
abstract: Hydrous carbonaceous chondrites are potential carriers of exogenous water to the Earth–Moon system, yet well-preserved hydrous carbonaceous impactor fragments are rarely found in lunar samples, with previous discoveries limited to the lunar nearside. The Chang’e-6 mission returned the first sample from the farside, providing a unique opportunity to identify the exogenous materials that have added volatiles to this region. We document well‑preserved relics showing C1-like mineralogical features in a Chang’e-6 regolith breccia. They are dominated by fine-grained Mg-rich saponite with partially collapsed basal spacing, along with magnetite, dolomite, sulfides, and organic nanoglobules, matching mineral assemblages of heavily altered carbonaceous chondrites and hydrous materials returned from asteroids Ryugu and Bennu. This diagnostic mineral assemblage and in‑situ space‑weathering overprint confirm that these clasts are surviving fragments of the incoming impactor, and in situ dehydration records water loss during lunar surface exposure. Our study provides the first mineralogical and petrographic evidence for preserved hydrous carbonaceous impact debris in lunar farside regolith, revealing the microscale preservation of hydrated minerals and carbonaceous components and providing new constraints on impact-induced volatile injection and release from carbonaceous materials.

title: Harvesting thermal energy from sunlight with wood
abstract: An article in Advanced Functional Materials reports a wood–metal–organic framework thermoelectric that converts both heat and evaporation-driven water flow into electricity, inspired by the transport functions of natural trees.

title: Nanocellulose strengthens bamboo from within
abstract: An article in Advanced Materials reports bamboo veneers reinforced with cellulose nanocrystals that are strong, flexible and can be made at scale.

title: Anthropic IPO: four ways the AI giant wants to disrupt science
abstract: The firm aims to cure diseases, accelerate discovery and automate science — but many researchers are sceptical of its lofty ambitions.

title: Bacteria and viruses team up to hasten the demise of algal blooms
abstract: Algal blooms are important ecological phenomena that drive carbon fixation and fuel the marine food web. Viral infection often ends them abruptly. Some bacteria can sense infected algal cells and then act in synergy with viruses to expedite a bloom’s collapse.

title: AI is turbocharging cyberattacks — can computer scientists catch up?
abstract: Cybersecurity researchers who don’t use the technology for spotting software bugs now 'risk falling behind'.

title: Advances and Perspectives of Cobalt‐Free Li‐Rich Mn‐Based Layered Oxide Cathodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Lithium‐rich manganese‐based oxides (LRMOs) are prioritized for next‐generation batteries due to their high theoretical specific capacity and energy density. In particular, the cobalt‐free LRMOs offer additional competitive advantages due to their lowered production cost and reduced resource dependence. However, the cobalt‐free LRMOs still suffer from persistent structural stability challenges, exhibiting low initial Coulombic efficiency, rapid capacity and voltage decay, and inferior rate capability. To advance cobalt‐free LRMO development, massive research efforts focused on effective regulation strategies have emerged recently. It is therefore imperative to timely summarize these recent works to systematically evaluate the attained achievements, recognize the unresolved issues, and formulate the key optimization approaches in the next stage; however, such related reviews for cobalt‐free LRMOs remain limited. Herein, we carefully examine the fundamental advances in cobalt‐free LRMOs and give a comprehensive review work. Initially, the microstructure of cobalt‐free LRMOs is dissected, and the corresponding electrochemical mechanism is elucidated. In addition, the faced challenges are described and analyzed in detail. More importantly, the currently proposed modification strategies are primarily discussed from the microstructure regulation, element doping and surface coating views. Finally, the significant perspectives are highlighted.

title: Multiscale Modeling of Virus Capsid Self-Assembly Reveals How Small Molecule Antivirals Can Redirect Assembly Pathways and Products
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Controlling the assembly of a virus capsid, a regular complex of hundreds of subunits, has applications for development of antivirals and for development of nanocontainers. Recent work has shown that a class of small molecules called capsid assembly modulators (CAMs) is promising for treating Hepatitis B virus (HBV). CAMs bind to HBV capsid proteins and alter their self-assembly, leading to nonfunctional and malformed structures. The mechanisms by which CAMs alter capsid assembly remain unclear. Here, we use a kinetic Monte Carlo (KMC) model for HBV capsid assembly to simulate how CAMs affect this complex reaction. The model is parametrized from all-atom simulations, resulting in unprecedented correlation between simulation and biochemical and structural observations. Simulations reproduce the effect of CAMs on experimental assembly products and their distributions. By analyzing assembly trajectories, we clarify the roles of thermodynamics and kinetics in determining assembly products, identify assembly mechanisms, and predict the key intermediates that lead to either capsids or malformed structures. Our findings enhance our fundamental understanding of capsid assembly, help advance the development of CAMs as a treatment for HBV and, more broadly, inform efforts to direct self-assembly pathways toward specific products.

title: In Situ Polymerized Main/Side-Chain Bifluorinated Cross-Linked Polyether Electrolytes for High-Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polyether electrolytes are compelling candidates for lithium metal batteries owing to their high ionic conductivity and conformal interfacial contact. However, their widespread adoption is impeded by inherent vulnerabilities, including limited oxidative stability against high-voltage cathodes, uncontrolled lithium dendrite growth, and persistent interfacial side reactions. To overcome these challenges, we report an in situ polymerized cross-linked polyether electrolyte engineered with a bifluorinated molecular architecture (PTFMO-BEP), incorporating −CF2– segments in the polymer backbone and −CF3 groups on the side chains. This design significantly enhances the intrinsic oxidative stability, extending the electrochemical window beyond 5.5 V. Concurrently, the electron-withdrawing fluorinated motifs weaken the Li+-polymer coordination, steering an anion-derived decomposition pathway to form a homogeneous, inorganic-rich solid electrolyte interphase (SEI). Consequently, the PTFMO-BEP electrolyte enables exceptional cyclability in Li||Li symmetric cells (>800 h) and uniform, dendrite-free lithium deposition. When paired with high-loading LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 (NCM811) cathodes (∼4.4 mAh cm–2) and thin lithium anode (50 μm), the Li||NCM811 full cells achieve outstanding capacity retention of 85.6% after 150 cycles at 4.3 V and 91.5% after 100 cycles at 4.5 V. Remarkably, stable operation is maintained even under an ultrahigh cutoff voltage of 4.7 V with a 20 μm Li anode (88.7% retention over 100 cycles). Furthermore, ampere-hour-scale pouch cells configured with LiNi0.90Co0.05Mn0.05O2 (NCM9055) cathodes deliver a high gravimetric energy density of 510.1 Wh kg–1. This work exemplifies a potent molecular-design strategy to advance polyether electrolytes for practical high-energy-density lithium metal batteries.

title: Defect-Mediated On–Off Growth in Tautomeric Crystallization: The Curious Case of Theophylline Monohydrate
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Crystal growth is inherently sensitive to interfacial structure, yet it remains poorly understood how intrinsic molecular heterogeneity in tautomeric materials translates into dynamic growth behaviors. Here, we combine microfluidics, in situ atomic force microscopy (AFM), molecular dynamics (MD), and density functional theory (DFT) to investigate the crystallization of theophylline monohydrate, which exhibits a minor tautomer (TP-N9, percent-level) coexisting in growth solutions with the dominant lattice-forming species (TP-N7). Facet-resolved measurements show that the (101̅) and (103̅) surfaces exhibit markedly different growth kinetics owing to their distinct interfacial structures, including transitions between arrested and active growth states. On basal (011) and (01̅1) planes, we observe anisotropic step propagation arising from direction-dependent molecular packing at step edges, which impose conformational constraints on solute incorporation into surface growth sites. Despite its low abundance, the TP-N9 tautomer functions as a growth inhibitor and exerts a disproportionate, facet-dependent influence on surface growth. MD simulations indicate that solute adsorption strength alone cannot explain growth rate anisotropy; instead, adsorption in growth-incompatible configurations appears critical, with growth rates governed by the energetic barriers for post-adsorption rearrangement into registry with the crystal lattice. Time-resolved measurements across a range of synthesis conditions revealed defects that transiently pin advancing steps, persist through partial overgrowth, and create local strain, which we attribute to TP-N9 adsorption. These collective effects give rise to spatially heterogeneous growth and dissolution and, macroscopically, drive defect-mediated on–off growth through dynamic shifts in faceting. These results reveal how trace-level tautomeric heterogeneity can redirect crystal growth through facet-dependent incorporation and defect-mediated kinetic regulation.

title: Thermodynamic Activity Regulation Enables Low-Voltage Alloy-Mediated CO2-to-Carbon Conversion
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molten-carbonate electrolysis integrates CO2 capture with conversion to storable solid carbon, yet direct carbonate electroreduction suffers from cathodic polarization, raising cell voltage and energy consumption. Here, the cathodic pathway is redesigned by coupling electrochemical alkali-metal alloying with thermochemical carbonate reduction. Alloying with liquid metals lowers the thermodynamic activity of the alkali-metal mediator and shifts its equilibrium alloying potential to more positive values, while sufficient activity must be retained to drive subsequent thermochemical carbonate reduction. These competing constraints define a thermodynamic reactive window that guides liquid-metal screening, identifying Sb as a host. Stepwise experiments separating alloying from open-circuit thermochemical carbon formation directly support the proposed pathway. Liquid Sb sustains CO2-to-carbon electrolysis for 72 h at 700 °C and 2.0 V with 80.9% Faradaic efficiency and 22.08 kWh kg C–1 electrical energy consumption, 36.9% below a reported solid-electrode benchmark. These results establish thermodynamic activity regulation as a strategy for lower-voltage electrochemical–chemical conversion.

title: Beyond Current Matching: A Voltage-Matched Perovskite-Silicon Tandem Mini-module as an Alternative to Monolithic Tandems
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Current matching limits the performance of two-terminal (2T) monolithic perovskite-silicon tandems. Voltage-matched (VM) tandems remove this constraint by connecting the perovskite and silicon sub-modules in parallel. Here, we report an area-matched 2T VM perovskite-silicon mini-module with a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.77% at minimal voltage mismatch. Tuning the voltage-matching ratio (VMratio, the ratio of the perovskite to silicon maximum-power-point voltages) through the silicon cell count reveals an asymmetry between the silicon- and perovskite-limited regimes: at equal voltage mismatch, the PCE loss relative to the four-terminal (4T) tandem is 1.1% (absolute) lower in the silicon-limited regime. Under controlled temperature (0–60 °C) and spectral variation, the VM tandem remains within 0.1–1.7% and 0.8–1.2% absolute of the 4T tandem, respectively, demonstrating near-4T performance with a two-terminal connection.

title: Competitive Coordination of Solvent in Electrolyte to Stabilize Li-Rich Mn-Based Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The practical application of lithium metal batteries equipped with lithium-rich manganese-based layered oxide (LRMO) cathodes is severely impeded by aggressive electrolyte decomposition under operational voltage above 4.5 V. Herein, we discover a unique competitive solvent coordination behavior in the electrolyte solvation structure that enables significant stabilization of LRMO-based batteries. This rarely reported mechanism inspires the design of a low-concentration electrolyte (0.5 M lithium hexafluorophosphate, LiPF6), which employs a binary fluorinated solvent system consisting of weakly solvating tris(2,2,2-trifluoroethyl) phosphate (TFP) and ethyl difluoroacetate (EDFA). Benefiting from the optimized solvation structure, the assembled Li||LRMO cells achieve cycling stability, retaining 80.5% of the initial capacity after 450 cycles at 4.8 V and 0.5 C. We further establish a molecular-level interfacial model to elucidate the performance enhancement mechanism. This work provides insights into the unique competitive coordination effect of solvents within solvation structures and offers an innovative strategy for electrolyte design toward LRMO-based battery systems and beyond.

title: Revealing the Atomic-Scale Degradation of Platinum-Based Intermetallic Nanocatalysts Upon Relevant Fuel Cell Conditions
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Platinum-based intermetallic nanomaterials are promising catalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) in proton-exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs). However, insights regarding their degradation under realistic PEMFC conditions still represent a knowledge gap. Herein, a systematic series of L12-Pt3M (M = V, Cr, or Zn) intermetallics with a similar structure, chemical composition, and morphology were synthesized, and their activity-stability trends were evaluated under conditions relevant to PEMFCs. Time- and potential-resolved catalyst dissolution were acquired and quantified through online ICP-MS using 1 M HClO4 at 65 °C, revealing that the first catalyst/electrolyte contact induces significant catalyst degradation before operation. During electrochemical operation, the anodic dissolution at 65 °C is substantially higher than at 25 °C, and a strong competition between cathodic dissolution and ion redeposition takes place. Identical-location electron microscopy analyses captured atomic degradation processes directly linked to catalyst electrochemical dissolution enhanced by temperature, providing new understanding for developing robust catalysts for PEMFCs.

title: Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
abstract: Using data from 21,609 homes in California, this study finds that electrification economics vary widely, with homes that have air conditioning better positioned to benefit. Targeted incentives and rate reform could support equitable adoption.

title: Incorporating Noncanonical Amino Acids for Protein Structure Analysis: Site-Directed Spin Labeling CW and Pulsed EPR Approaches
abstract: Abstract Site-directed spin labeling in combination with electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy (SDSL–EPR) has emerged as a powerful and highly adaptable platform probing protein structure and dynamics with residue-level precision. In its classical strategy, a stable paramagnetic label, most commonly a nitroxide radical, but not only, is covalently introduced at a predefined position, typically through an engineered cysteine residue. Continuous-wave (cw) EPR spectroscopy provides sensitivity to protein dynamics across a broad range of time scales (and techniques), from backbone motions (ps-ns) to protein complex assembly and conformational transitions (ms-s) or characterization of protein conformational exchange (μs-ms). Pulsed EPR methodologies, particularly double electron–electron resonance (DEER), provide access to long-range distance distributions in the nanometer regime (ca. 2–8 nm) through the measurement of dipolar interactions between pairs of spin labels. Recent developments in the genetic encoding of noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) have substantially expanded the scope of SDSL–EPR by overcoming the intrinsic limitations associated with cysteine-based labeling. In this review, we provide a comprehensive overview of ncAA-based spin-labeling strategies for SDSL–EPR, discuss the repertoire of reported spin labels and their synthetic routes, and highlight representative applications in structural investigations of proteins in vitro as well as in cellular environments.

title: Development and Application of Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing
abstract: Abstract Individual RNA strands can be sequenced directly using nanoscale protein pores. This process, Nanopore Direct RNA Sequencing (Nanopore DRS), uses a helicase motor protein to regulate RNA displacement through the nanopore orifice in single nucleotide steps. Partial blockade of the monovalent ionic current is recorded at 4 kHz and converted to a string of RNA nucleotide basecalls using machine learning models. In this review, we discuss the development of Nanopore DRS from 1996 to the present. This includes performance metrics, evolution of machine learning models, and applications of Nanopore DRS to major RNA classes across kingdoms. Advantages of the technology are highlighted with special emphasis on nucleotide modifications along intact single strands. Shortcomings of the technology are also considered along with possible solutions. We close with forward looking Nanopore DRS applications: Single cell RNA sequencing; remote monitoring of infectious agents; principled understanding of nanopore ionic current patterns using all-atoms simulations; global food security; and clinical applications.

title: Substitution Reactions of Halogen-Substituted Acetals: Glycosylations and Related Reactions
abstract: Abstract The nucleophilic substitution reactions of halogen-substituted acetals are useful for the synthesis of a variety of compounds, most particularly of sugar derivatives. This review will summarize the current understanding of the mechanisms involved in these reactions and will present substitution reactions of carbohydrate derivatives with fluorine, chlorine, bromine, and iodine substituents. The halogen atom at C-2 can have a powerful influence on the stereoselectivities of the glycosylation reactions, most often leading to 1,2-trans stereoselectivity. Examples of the uses of these halogen-substituted products will also be provided.

title: Data-driven distributionally robust planning of coastal distribution networks and PV-storage-EV stations for low-carbon energy transition
abstract: Coastal distribution networks (DNs) are becoming key infrastructure for the low-carbon energy transition as electric vehicle (EV) charging, photovoltaic (PV) generation, energy storage, and marine renewable procurement are increasingly coupled at the planning stage. Existing planning models, however, usually treat network expansion, PV-storage-EV station (PSES) deployment, low-carbon operation, and coastal asset degradation separately. This paper proposes a data-driven distributionally robust planning framework for coastal DNs and PSESs. The framework jointly optimizes radial network topology and PSES siting while incorporating salt-spray degradation costs, carbon-emission-flow (CEF)-based nodal carbon accounting, and tidal-generation-driven procurement costs. To represent heterogeneous uncertainty, the model combines continuous box uncertainty for load and PV availability with probability ambiguity over EV-charging scenarios generated from historical charging profiles. The resulting two-stage distributionally robust optimization problem is reformulated through exact relaxation of ESS mode binaries and KKT-based decomposition, and is solved by an inexact column-and-constraint generation (i-C&CG) algorithm. Case studies on a realistic 47-node coastal feeder show that salt-spray exposure can alter the selected topology and PSES siting, while the proposed planning scheme improves voltage quality, reduces annualized total cost, and reveals the cost--carbon trade-off of tidal procurement. The tailored i-C&CG algorithm obtains the same optimal design as conventional C&CG with about an order-of-magnitude reduction in solution time.

title: When Is Molecular-Dynamics-Predicted Ionic Diffusivity Reliable in Solid Electrolytes?
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics is widely used to predict ionic diffusivity in solid electrolytes, but the reliability of these predictions is often difficult to assess. Our analysis identifies finite trajectory length, limited cell size, and insufficient sampling as key limitations. Using cubic Li7La3Zr2O12, we show that these limitations can remain hidden behind apparently linear mean-squared displacements and well-behaved Arrhenius relations, leading to inaccurate diffusivities, activation energies, and extrapolated Nernst–Einstein conductivity estimates. Such errors can misrank candidate materials and misdirect computational screening. We examine the local mean-squared-displacement exponent, α(t), as a diagnostic of dynamical convergence and relate it quantitatively to finite-time bias in an MSD-ratio estimator within a caging-diffusion model. This relation estimates a characteristic analysis time for a prescribed accuracy. Independent replicas reduce statistical uncertainty, while selective single-axis expansion mitigates finite-size effects. These findings improve materials ranking and the efficiency of computational screening.

title: Spatial patterns of hybrid PV–CSP–TES configurations for green hydrogen production across Algeria
abstract: Existing studies have optimized hybrid PV–CSP plants or mapped suitable locations for solar hydrogen production, but the spatial dependence of the optimal hybrid architecture remains insufficiently resolved. This study develops a national-scale framework that couples GIS–FAHP screening with hourly PV–CSP–TES–electrolyzer simulation and site-specific NSGA-II optimization to determine how the cost-optimal system design changes across Algeria. At each meteorological location, PV capacity, CSP power-block capacity, TES duration, and solar multiple are jointly optimized for a fixed 50 MW electrolyzer, with the final configuration selected as the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) solution satisfying annual demand satisfaction (ADS) ≥ 90%. The resulting architecture varies substantially across the country: optimal PV capacity ranges from 70.03 to 168.86 MW, CSP power-block capacity from 50.00 to 92.98 MW, and solar multiple from 2.35 to 3.40, while annual hydrogen production remains comparatively stable at 7.58–7.65 kt H₂ yr −1 . Unconstrained LCOH ranges from 6.00 to 10.78 € kg −1 H₂ and narrows considerably after GIS-based deployment constraints are imposed. At Hassi R'Mel, the selected architecture combines approximately 100 MW PV, 50 MW CSP, SM = 2.80, and 16 h TES, achieving an LCOH of 6.53 € kg −1 H₂, 90.3% ADS and approximately 7.6 kt H₂ yr −1 . Sensitivity analysis identifies the discount rate and CSP capital cost as the strongest economic influences within the examined parameter ranges. A matched-output comparison shows that PV-only production can achieve lower LCOH when intermittency is acceptable, whereas PV–CSP–TES substantially increases electrolyzer utilization and production continuity. The results demonstrate that site-specific optimization is necessary to capture how economically preferred generation capacities and solar-field sizing adapt to local solar-resource conditions.

title: Bio-based deep eutectic solvents as advanced phase change media for solar thermal storage: Mechanisms, computational design, and industrial deployment challenges
From biological principles to battery interfaces: recent progress in bio-inspired design for aqueous zinc-ion batteries
Robotic inspection and maintenance for energy infrastructure: a systematic review and future perspectives
Data center cooling in the AI era: cross-scale challenges and system-level outlook
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) is fundamentally reshaping data center thermal and energy requirements, driven by increasing power densities and heterogeneous workload characteristics. This review provides an integrated cross-scale and temporal perspective that connects AI heat generation with chip-, rack-, and facility-scale thermal management and their interactions with external energy, water, and grid infrastructures. Modern AI workloads, enabled by accelerator-based hardware, can generate highly localized and temporally dynamic heat fluxes, challenging traditional assumptions of uniform and steady-state cooling design. Accordingly, a range of cooling technologies is examined, including air-based systems, liquid cooling approaches, hybrid configurations, and heat-reuse strategies, with emphasis on their performance limits and deployment constraints. The analysis further identifies key cross-cutting barriers to scalability and efficiency, including thermodynamic irreversibility, coupled water–energy–grid dependencies, cross-scale thermal interactions, reliability and maintainability constraints, and technology-specific trade-offs. Building on these observations, future cooling systems are expected to shift toward integrated and adaptive designs that prioritize multi-objective optimization rather than isolated performance improvements. Emerging directions include grid-responsive and water-aware operation, thermal storage-enabled temporal decoupling, co-designed computing and cooling infrastructures, and predictive closed-loop thermal management enabled by digital twins and data-driven control. Collectively, the findings highlight a transition from component-level optimization toward fully integrated system architectures that jointly optimize energy efficiency, resource utilization, operational resilience, and computational performance across spatial and temporal scales.

title: Advances in sorption-based thermochemical energy storage: from material properties to prototype-level performance
Learnable delay-stability coupling for energy-information co-optimization in smart grids
Optimal integration of Power-to-Vehicle and Power-to-Heat systems to support renewable deployment in smart urban energy districts
abstract: Decarbonising smart urban energy districts through distributed renewable generation requires planning frameworks able to capture sector-coupling flexibility, while accounting for the multidimensional trade-offs among technical, economic and environmental objectives. This study aims to address the complexity of energy district planning by applying a multi-objective optimisation framework to assess how Power-to-Heat and Power-to-Vehicle strategies can jointly enhance renewable integration. A residential district is modelled in EnergyPLAN comparing a reference configuration based on electricity grid and gas boilers with electrified scenarios including heating, cooling and transport demand under five electric vehicle penetration levels. For each scenario, photovoltaic, small-scale wind, electric batteries, and thermal storage capacities are optimised by minimising annual costs, critical excess electricity production, and CO 2 emissions. Results show that increasing electric vehicle penetration reduces emissions and annual costs, while lowering stationary battery requirements through smart charging flexibility. Beyond a certain level of on-site renewable deployment, further decarbonisation depends primarily on the combined electrification of mobility and domestic end-uses, rather than on additional renewable capacity alone. At intermediate electrification levels, thermal storage supports a solar-dominated mix, whereas higher electric vehicle penetration favours a more balanced renewable mix with reduced storage needs. The fully electrified configuration decreases primary fossil energy consumption, achieving 90% CO 2 abatement and reduces annual costs by about 7% compared with the reference case, while reaching 67% self-sufficiency and 79% self-consumption. The findings demonstrate that exploiting heat pumps and electric vehicles for system flexibility can enhance renewable integration and limit local excess electricity production.

title: Continual reinforcement learning for adaptive ship energy efficiency optimization: A LoRA-enabled low-parameter incremental framework

Water-energy-carbon nexus footprint of seawater desalination and transfer for industrial development: a hybrid life cycle -node-flow framework
abstract: Seawater desalination is becoming increasingly important in arid, industrializing regions, but planning assessments often consider the embodied energy of supply chains and the operational energy of water transfer separately. This study presents a hybrid life cycle and node-flow framework that combines embodied energy and carbon emissions with a spatially explicit model of pumping energy based on elevation gain and hydraulic head losses. The framework is applied to Iran's Persian Gulf Seawater Desalination and Transfer (SDT) project, which supplies 138.76 million m 3 of water annually. Two strategies are compared: Water Transfer (WT), which pumps water inland while transporting products to the coast, and Industrial Transfer (IT), which relocates industries to the coast and transports raw materials from inland areas. Rail and truck freight represent the best- and worst-case transport scenarios, respectively. Pumping-energy intensity ranges from 333.2 to 21,462.4 MWh per million m 3 , depending mainly on transfer distance and elevation. Although industrial relocation reduces long-distance pumping-energy by 99.4%, transporting raw materials offsets much of this saving. Under the grid-average electricity scenario, rail transport results in nearly unchanged total energy use (+0.9%) but reduces carbon emissions by 22.7%. With truck transport, energy use and carbon emissions increase by 121.9% and 53.8%, respectively. Under low-carbon electricity, relocation increases carbon emissions with both transport modes. Benefits also vary by industry: relocation reduces energy use at the steel site under both modes and at the pelletizing site by rail, but not at the copper sites, where raw-material requirements are substantially greater than product output. The water footprint changes only slightly (−4.4%). This framework supports integrated assessments of energy and carbon trade-offs in desalination-dependent industrial systems.

A retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)-enhanced framework for knowledge-guided campus-scale building retrofit design
abstract: Urban-scale building envelope optimization is constrained by the computational burden of iterative simulation. This study proposes a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)-enhanced framework that replaces the search phase of conventional optimization: literature-screened envelope solutions are retrieved from a curated corpus and then cross-checked through physics-based EnergyPlus simulation, rather than located through exhaustive parametric search. The corpus comprises 20,247 initially identified publications screened to a core of 338 studies, together with an experimentally characterized database of 502 envelope materials, of which 65 were used in the assemblies evaluated here. A three-stage progressive retrofit strategy — conventional high-performance insulation; vacuum insulation panels, aerogel and phase change materials (PCMs); and optimized PCM hybrid assemblies — was applied to seven reference buildings on Yonsei University's 86-building campus in Seoul, Korea. A systematic literature review established that whole-building field-measured savings are systematically 0.25–0.75× of simulation-only upper bounds, a correction embedded directly in the retrieval thresholds and screening criteria. The seven reference buildings produce a simulated mean building-level EUI reduction of 21.5%, ranging from 9.5% in high window-to-wall-ratio modern buildings to 39.6% in thermally deficient heritage structures, while campus-wide analysis of all 86 buildings yields 15.7% (124.4 to 104.9 kWh/m 2 ·year). EnergyPlus models were not calibrated against sub-metered operational data, so all reported reductions are simulation-based screening estimates. The framework offers a scalable, computationally efficient route to envelope retrofit planning for large institutional portfolios and urban decarbonization programs.

title: Flexibility-oriented hierarchical energy management for transmission–distribution–microgrid coordination
Beyond facility-level metrics: A whole-system energy–water nexus analysis of data centre integration in Great Britain’s net-zero transition
abstract: The rapid proliferation of hyperscale data centres (DCs) presents compounded challenges to Great Britain (GB)’s net-zero energy transition, superimposing large, continuously growing electricity loads on an energy system simultaneously aiming to be net-zero by 2050. However, existing assessments of DC sustainability rely largely on facility-level metrics such as Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE), which provide limited insight into indirect water use and the cross-sector effects of DC integration on power-system infrastructure and decarbonisation pathways. Here, we develop a spatially explicit whole-system energy–water nexus optimisation model for 13 GB regions, representing air-cooled, water-cooled, and direct-to-chip (D2C) cooling architectures. The model uses 24-hour resolution within weighted representative days and a rolling-horizon solution approach with a one-period look-ahead, with weather-dependent PUE and WUE derived from regional typical-meteorological-year data. Under the modelled scenarios, 21.7 GW of installed DC IT capacity adds 124–133 TWh/yr of electricity demand to the GB energy system by 2050, and water-cooled configurations consume 297 × 10 9 litres/yr of direct, on-site cooling water, compared with 31 × 10 9 litres/yr for air cooling. DC integration also increases indirect water consumption by 229 -- 255 × 10 9 litres/yr through the additional generation required, almost entirely from nuclear generation. Relative to water cooling, D2C cooling reduces total system water consumption by 322 × 10 9 litres/yr, almost entirely through the elimination of direct water use, while differences between the three configurations in electricity generation ( 6 TWh/yr between D2C and water cooling), indirect water and heat supply lie within the numerical variability of the optimisation. Under hypothetical water-availability constraints, the air-cooled configuration remains feasible down to 70% of its unconstrained regional water consumption, at which system cost rises by 4.7% (from £593 to £621 billion), solar capacity increases by 25 GW, nuclear capacity falls by 11 GW, and DC capacity relocates from NT and SW towards SO, WN, NO and SC. The water-cooled configuration remains feasible only down to 95% availability, because its direct cooling water cannot be reduced without changing the installed DC capacity. In an exploratory analysis, integrating DC waste heat with Direct Air Capture (DAC) installs 59 MtCO 2 /yr of fully utilised DAC capacity by 2050, using 87% of the available waste heat and adding 11 TWh/yr of electricity demand. Relative to the D2C, net CO 2 emissions decrease from − 9 to − 68 MtCO 2 /yr, system cost (excluding the reserve-margin penalty) rises by £4–5 billion, while changes in generation and installed capacity remain within the variability between independent solutions, reflecting that DAC deployment is driven by the carbon price applied to net emissions rather than by the net-zero constraint, which is already met without DAC. These results indicate that the system-level consequences of DC deployment can differ from those inferred from facility-level PUE and WUE metrics alone, highlighting the importance of jointly considering electricity, water, cooling, heating, and negative-emissions interactions in planning future DC infrastructure.

abstract: An amphiphilic ionic bicontinuous mesoporous carbon nitride enables simultaneous photocatalytic co-production of H2O2 and tandem C–H activation/C–N cyclization at the oil-water interface. By repurposing a sacrificial agent into a high-value pharmaceutical intermediate (BzlM), this dual-functional catalyst sustains co-production in a continuous-flow reactor for over 200 hours, offering a generalizable strategy for sustainable biphasic chemical synthesis.

abstract: The reduction propensity of the electrolyte governs the interfacial stability of batteries. Leveraging this principle, we screened 72 molecules and identified CMDO as the effective additive capable of suppressing the side reactions of ethyl acetate at the interface.

title: Atmospheric organic nitrogen is a major nutrient source to global oceans
abstract: Atmospheric nitrogen (N) deposition is a critical nutrient source for marine ecosystems, but its organic nitrogen (ON) component remains poorly quantified. We measured ON in marine aerosols collected during 21 research cruises transecting multiple ocean basins and both hemispheric high latitudes. We used these observations to constrain and evaluate an atmospheric chemistry model with updated ON sources and sinks, enabling global mapping of ON deposition. The model estimated annual ON deposition to oceans at 12.8 (4.0 to 22.7) teragrams of nitrogen per year (Tg N year −1 ), contributing 27% (11 to 40%) of total N deposition. Marine emissions supply 3.9 (0.7 to 6.9) Tg N year −1 (30%) of deposited ON, while terrestrial sources contribute 8.9 (3.3 to 15.7) Tg N year −1 (70%). In N-limited regions such as the central Atlantic and Indonesian seas, ON accounts for ~50% of total N deposition.

title: Quiet within, chaos without: Turbulence shelters drive selective particle capture and release
abstract: Turbulence is chaotic, yet its fluctuations follow a structured, nonequilibrium energy cascade unconstrained by the equilibrium theorems that limit passive energy extraction from molecular gases. Here, we introduce turbulence shelters: hollow shells with a single aperture that filter eddies by scale, sustaining gradients in fluctuation intensity that drive directional particle transport despite zero mean fluid flux. Across three orders of magnitude in size, shelters establish particle concentration contrasts between their interior and the surrounding flow, with selectivity controlled by particle geometry, inertia, thermal fluctuations, and electrostatic forces. At the microscale, shelters discriminate particles differing by tens of nanometers independently of material composition. These results establish a design principle for selective filtration: Geometry that compartmentalizes turbulent fluctuations can harness ambient eddies to direct particle transport.

title: Beyond containment in insect farming
Meso–microporous zeolitic materials with thin walls containing ordered 10-ring channels
abstract: Aluminosilicate zeolites offer exceptional size and shape selectivity but suffer from diffusion limitations imposed by subnanometer micropores. Intrinsically meso–microporous zeolites integrate mesopores with micropores to create interconnected pathways that accelerate diffusion while preserving selectivity, yet their synthesis remains challenging. In this study, we report NJU120-5 and NJU120-7, intrinsically meso–microporous aluminosilicates that integrate micropores with mesopores enclosed by two-T-atom-thick walls containing 10-ring channels, forming a fully interconnected three-dimensional pore network. Their plausible framework models were established on the basis of advanced electron ptychographic imaging, revealing representative quasi-rectangular mesopores in calcined NJU120-5 with a uniform width of ~12 angstroms and lengths from 41 to 162 angstroms. Both materials exhibit high porosity, strong Brønsted acidity, and enhanced performance in heavy-oil cracking, delivering high yields of valuable fuels with suppressed coke formation.

title: The scientific record is never finished
abstract: The scholarly scientific record has always been a work in progress. From the earliest days of scientific publishing, new findings would come along that changed the way earlier findings are understood. When research journals were published only in print, occasional errors would be reported by the authors or found by others, and papers would be retracted or corrected. When publishing became digital, many more people could quickly access and scrutinize data and images for accuracy. Now, in the age of artificial intelligence (AI), it is possible for machines to do these examinations more expeditiously and at a larger scale. All of this has added an important new layer to the publishing process and put more responsibility on authors, who must update their work if new issues arise. In response to this need, Science is improving the ways in which it will flag and notate papers that require adjustment or where changes are under consideration. Our Editorial Policies now reflect these updates.

title: Telemetric calorimetry for wireless continuous reaction profiling
abstract: Real-time monitoring of chemical reactions is often achieved with specialized instrumentation along with custom-designed reactors or intrusive sampling. In this study, we introduce reaction telemetry, a wireless analytical strategy that enables remote, nonintrusive monitoring directly within operating reaction vessels. This approach uses light-powered microelectronic devices that communicate optically and function as autonomous sensing elements. We demonstrate continuous calorimetric measurements across diverse chemical reactions relevant to pharmaceutical and fine chemical synthesis, including photochemical and electrochemical systems, providing access to reaction kinetics under native operating conditions with subsecond temporal resolution. The resulting measurements will support catalyst evaluation, safety assessment, and mechanistic investigation and will accelerate data-driven reaction discovery. By embedding analytical functionality directly within reaction vessels, reaction telemetry establishes a general framework for information-rich observation of chemical processes across research, development, and education.

title: Balancing redox-mediated cytotoxicity and catalysis in natural product biosynthesis
abstract: Redox-mediated chemistry is central to both the biosynthesis and cytotoxicity of many natural products, yet how microbes balance these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover a conserved mechanism that coordinates three redox-mediated processes in secondary metabolite biosynthesis: self-protection, prevention of substrate degradation, and late-stage biosynthesis. Using the antitumor antibiotic doxorubicin as a model system, we show that the vicinal oxygen chelate (VOC) protein DnrV prevents reactive oxygen species formation and substrate degradation while promoting P450 catalysis. We expand this paradigm to a conserved family of VOC-fold proteins, redox-associated cytotoxin-binding proteins (REACT), found across bacteria, fungi, and plants. REACT represents a multifunctional protein class that balances antibiotic assembly, self-protection, and prevention of metabolite destruction, providing a foundational understanding of production of redox-active natural products.

title: A thalamo-amygdalar circuit drives female vulnerability to chronic pain after early-life stress
abstract: Childhood adversity increases the risk of chronic pain and anxiety later in life, particularly in women, yet the neural mechanisms linking early-life stress to adult vulnerability remain elusive. Here, we show that social isolation and nerve injury interact to amplify activity-dependent synaptic gain and anticipatory recruitment of the paraventricular thalamus-to–central amygdala pathway in female, but not male, mice. This female-specific circuit sensitization enhances mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance behaviors in adulthood. Chemogenetic pathway inhibition selectively rescued these behaviors when stress and injury co-occurred, whereas sustained and phasic pathway activation triggered mechanical hypersensitivity and avoidance, respectively. Together, these findings uncovered a latent thalamo-amygdalar synaptic gain state that is unmasked by a subsequent injury and transforms early-life stress into female-specific vulnerability to chronic pain and anxiety-like avoidance.

title: Angular momentum transfer from an optical vortex to an atomic rotor
abstract: Light carries angular momentum in two forms: spin, associated with polarization, and orbital, associated with helical wavefronts. Whereas spin angular momentum underlies well-known atomic selection rules, the role of orbital angular momentum (OAM) in light-matter interaction continues to be discussed in the literature. In this work, we investigate OAM transfer from a vortex laser beam to a trapped-ion quantum rotor using rotational sidebands of the electric quadrupole transition of 40 Ca + . We directly observe coherent transfer of optical OAM into quantized rotation and identify distinct selection rules for different rotational sidebands. This observation provides experimental evidence for a scale-dependent separation of angular momentum transfer pathways in light-matter interactions. Further, our work elucidates the previously reported modified selection rules in trapped-ion experiments, establishing a unified framework for twisted light–matter interactions.

title: Interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer for low-loss soft ultrasonic interfaces
abstract: Ultrasound imaging relies on soft interfaces that transmit sound efficiently between a device and the body. Conventional gel couplants provide low acoustic loss but contain mobile liquid phases that can dry, flow, or leach during extended use. By contrast, mobile phase–free elastomers are more stable but generally attenuate megahertz ultrasound strongly, limiting their use as couplants. We report an interpenetrating bottlebrush elastomer molecularly designed to overcome this trade-off. A densely grafted backbone lowers the shear modulus without increasing shear loss, whereas well-packed sidechains reduce bulk compressibility, jointly suppressing acoustic attenuation in a soft elastomer. The resulting elastomer combines soft tissue–like mechanics with low-loss acoustics, providing a durable couplant for soft ultrasonic interfaces.

Quantum-classical separation in bounded-resource tasks arising from measurement contextuality
abstract: Quantum phenomena can be exploited to tackle certain problems beyond the reach of classical approaches. In this study, we focus on coordinated decision-making among many players without communication, the study of which, on current quantum processors, has remained elusive. Using a superconducting qubit processor, we show that quantum contextuality enables certain tasks to be performed with success probabilities beyond classical limits. With a few qubits, we illustrate quantum contextuality with the magic square game and quantify it through a Bell-Kochen-Specker inequality violation. To examine many-body contextuality, we implement the N -player Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger game and separately solve a two-dimensional hidden linear function problem, advancing the state of the art on fidelity and system size in both tasks. Our work introduces benchmarking of quantum processors using contextuality-based algorithms.
